News.title: Sick moment thug laughs in police interview after filming himself beating ‘kind & gentle’ man to death over 2 days
News.content:
THIS is the sick moment a killer laughs during a police interview after filming himself beating a kind Samaritan to death over two days.

Jamie Gawler, 54, was tragically found dead at his flat in Hereford in January last year after Matthew Jonathan, 40, repeatedly beat assaulted him.



Jamie had kindly offered homeless Jonathan a place to stay with him after the pair had struck up a friendship while Jonathan had been staying at a night shelter.

But a month later, Jamie’s brother found his dead body after he was viciously attacked for days.



Police recovered seven “extremely graphic and distressing” videos filmed on a mobile phone showing Jonathan savagely beating Jamie which ultimately led to his death.

In an episode of BBC’s crime documentary Murder 24/7, footage of Jonathan’s interview with West Mercia Police reveals how he laughed when being questioned about the heinous crime.



A detective asks Jonathan if he was in possession of Jamie’s phone to which Jonathan replied “no comment”.

The officer says: “Now, that phone has been recovered” and Jonathan asks her: “So? What’s it got to do with me?”



“I’m asking you to account for that. I’m asking you to account for how Jamie’s phone has made a telephone call to your brother,” says the detective.

Jonathan, who appears to have multiple bruises on his face, repositions himself in his chair, before replying: “I ain’t accounting for sh**.”

Then there’s an eerie silence before the callous killer starts laughing.



The detective asks: “Are you alright?” and Jonathan replies: “Yeah, I’m fine thank you.”

Horrified and puzzled by his reaction, she asks: “You’re laughing. Why are you laughing? It’s not a laughing matter.”

But Jonathan says “this is all a joke” while the detective insists that this is a “serious investigation”.

“It might be a serious investigation but it’s nothing to do with me,” Jonathan replies.

“Nothing to do with me, leave me alone. Leave me to just live my life.”



The detective says: “You’re sat here and we’re asking you questions about a serious matter”, to which Jonathan tells her she will “get the same answer over and over and over again”.

“Obviously we’re doing our investigations and we’re here to gather the information,” says the detective.

But Jonathan replies curtly: “Yeah, but it’s bollocks” and tells her “You are the police, do your work”.

The detective explains: “Well, I’m doing my work by asking you questions now, Matthew.”

But he retaliates: “You’re clutching at straws, just wasting my time, wasting my time and wasting everybody else’s time.”



Jonathan was jailed for 32 years at Worcester Crown Court in September last year after pleading guilty to murder for killing Jamie in his own home.

Police investigations found two fingerprints on one of eleven empty vodka bottles in the flat matched him, and a bloody boot print at the scene was traced to his rare footwear through a national database.

Detectives also found that Jonathan had used Jamie’s bank cards to make purchases in local shops both during and after the brutal attack.

Jonathan travelled to South Wales on January 17, 2025 where he had a medical episode on a train station platform.

Several items had fallen from his pocket including Jamie’s mobile phone, bank card and his car keys.



Jamie’s brother had tried calling him the next day as he hadn’t heard from him but a South Wales Police officer picked up the phone.

They told him they had discovered the phone earlier in the day at Porth railway station

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Concerned for Jamie’s welfare, he decided to check on him at his home where he found his brother’s body.

Jonathan was arrested on January 19 by South Wales Police where he was then transferred to Hereford Police Station and quizzed by detectives.

News.title: Rookie cop ‘bundled woman into car then sexually assaulted and raped her before he was snared in motorway police chase’
News.content:
'SNATCH' CHARGE Rookie cop ‘bundled woman into car then sexually assaulted and raped her before he was snared in motorway police chase’

A ROOKIE cop allegedly bundled a woman into a car before sexually assaulting then raping her, a court heard today.

Mohammad Hassan, who was off duty at the time, was arrested following a police pursuit on the M62.

The Greater Manchester Police trainee, 23, appeared at Stockport Magistrates’ Court today.

He is charged with oral rape, kidnap, strangulation, sexual assault, theft of a mobile phone and dangerous driving.





The court was told the alleged kidnapping took place on Saturday night when a woman in her 20s was bundled into a car.

She was then driven to an area of Manchester and was sexually assaulted and raped, it is alleged.

The suspect then drove off at 120mph, Ewan Cooper, prosecuting, told the court.

A 999 call was made shortly before 10.20pm in which a woman could be heard in distress in a vehicle in the Manchester area, JPs were told.

GMP said a woman was safeguarded at the scene and continues to be supported by specialist officers and support services.

Hassan, who has been suspended by the force, spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth.

He was remanded into custody to next appear at Manchester Crown Court on September 15.

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said: “GMP detectives and staff have been working on this investigation throughout the last 48 hours to ensure charges are brought in this case.



“The victim is our priority, and we are ensuring she continues to receive specialist support. Criminal proceedings must now take its course without interference.

“I understand and share the feeling among the public and our thousands of hard-working, decent staff who will have seen this news.

“Proceedings are under way and necessary action will be decisively taken within the regulations.”

News.title: Terrifying moment zipline thrillseeker is STRANDED 150ft up as high wind stops her ride leaving her flailing in panic
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a tourist is left dangling around 150ft above a river after high winds bring her zipline ride to a horrifying halt.

The thrill-seeker is seen flailing in panic as she hangs helplessly above the Yellow River in north-western China.



Shocking footage shows the woman suspended in mid-air as tiny parachutes designed to slow her descent flap violently around her.

She became stranded on the single-cable zipline after the sudden change in wind direction left her ride grinding to a terrifying stop.



The panicked tourist is seen frantically kicking her legs and thrashing in mid-air as panic visibly sets in, seemingly overwhelmed by the sheer drop beneath her.

From the rider’s angle and the height shown in the footage, she appears to be suspended around 150ft above the water.



The heart-stopping ordeal unfolded at the Shapotou Scenic Area in Zhongwei, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, on August 7.

The attraction, known as the Fei Huang Teng Da single-cable zipline, carries visitors across the Yellow River.

Operator China Travel Ningxia Shapotou Cableway Amusement Co Ltd said the tourist became stuck at around 3.52pm after the wind suddenly changed direction.

The company said she was left hanging in the air for around one minute before staff sprang into action.



Workers manually adjusted the steel cable and instructed the frightened tourist to change her riding position.

The desperate intervention allowed the zipline to start moving again and carry her safely to the end of the ride.

Staff then comforted the shaken tourist, explained what had happened and apologised for the terrifying stoppage.

She reportedly accepted that the sudden halt had been caused by the dramatic change in wind direction.

The operator has now vowed to overhaul its arrangements according to real-time weather conditions.



It also promised to ramp up emergency-response training for staff operating the Yellow River zipline.

Earlier, Shapotou Scenic Area staff had warned that factors including a visitor’s weight and weather conditions could cause the zipline to temporarily stop during a descent.

The footage has since sparked furious and horrified reactions online.

One viewer wrote: “My legs are shaking just looking at the screen. One minute up there feels like an absolute century.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another questioned why visitors were not screened before riding, saying: “If the park already knows that being lightweight causes people to get stuck, why aren’t they proactively forcing everyone onto a scale before they buy a ticket?”



A third commenter suggested a stark warning should be displayed before visitors take the plunge, writing: “If you are thin or if it’s windy, you might become a human pendulum.”

News.title: How to make a pinhole projector to watch the solar eclipse safely without glasses
News.content:
THE UK is gearing up for a sensational celestial show on Wednesday, when the best solar eclipse in decades will grace our skies.

But with certified eclipse glasses selling out fast, people are looking for alternative ways to witness the phenomenon.



Even if you do manage to buy a genuine pair online, they most likely won’t arrive on time for the solar eclipse.

A Royal Observatory Greenwich spokesperson said: “We have sold out of solar eclipse glasses, both online and in our shops, due to an unprecedented volume of orders.”



How do you make a pinhole eclipse viewer?

If proper glasses are unavailable, the best way to see Wednesday’s partial solar eclipse is to make an indirect viewer instead.

All you need to do is punch a small, clean hole in one piece of card and use a second section white card as a screen in your other hand or on the floor.

You have to stand with your back to the Sun, hold the holed card above the screen and let sunlight pass through it.

The distance between the cards needs to be adjusted until a small image of the Sun appears clearly on the other white card below.

During this week’s partial eclipse, it should appear as a crescent.

Only watch the projected image – never turn around and look at the Sun through the hole.



Looking directly at the Sun may damage the retina without causing any pain.

So it is possible to cause a permanent injury without even noticing anything is wrong until it is too late.

Regular sunglasses are also unsafe for viewing a solar eclipse, no matter how much they cost or how dark they might appear.

What other ways can you watch the eclipse without glasses?

There are even simpler ways to enjoy the solar eclipse that need no assembly whatsoever.



UKHSA says “you can watch the eclipse indirectly without any specialist equipment at all”, listing safe options including “viewing the Sun’s image projected through a colander or the gaps between tree leaves”.

For the colander method you will also want a sheet of white card or paper.

Lay it on the ground or hold it out, stand with your back to the Sun and position the colander so sunlight shines through its holes onto the card.

Each hole will then project its own tiny crescent Sun.

The tree method requires nothing at all – stand under a leafy tree and look at the shadows on the ground, where the gaps between leaves act as natural pinholes.



What time will the eclipse happen in the UK?

On Wednesday, August 12, a deep partial solar eclipse will sweep across the UK.

Astronomers have said it will be the most striking eclipse Britain has seen since 1999.

Between 90% and 96% of the Sun will be covered by the Moon n the UK,.

Depending on where you are, the Moon will start to pass the Sun at around 6.15pm, with the maximum eclipse roughly an hour later between 7.05pm and 7.15pm, and the event finishing just after 8pm.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

As the eclipse occurs in the evening in the UK, the sun will be low in the western sky, so you will need a clear, unobstructed view towards the horizon.

News.title: Two 11-year-old girls ‘sexually assaulted’ in underpass in broad daylight attack – as man, 59, arrested
News.content:
UNDERPASS HORROR Two 11-year-old girls ‘sexually assaulted’ in underpass in broad daylight attack – as man, 59, arrested

TWO 11-year-old girl’s were allegedly sexually assaulted in an underpass in broad daylight attack.

The shocking incident is said to have happened between 1.30pm and 2.30pm on Thursday in Burnley, Lancashire.

It’s believed the two girls – both aged 11 – were assaulted on an underpass connecting Pendle Way and Gannow Lane as well as the Adamson Street and St Johns Street area.

The girls were able to flee their attackers ask for help and cops have now launched an investigation.





Lancashire Police has arrested a 59-year-old man on suspicion of sexual assault.

The force said they are still looking for people they want to speak to and are urging any witnesses to come forward.

A spokesperson for the force said: “We know there were some people in the area who we haven’t yet spoken to, and so we are publicly appealing for witnesses today, to ask for your help.

“If you saw the man, described as white, with grey hair and glasses, with the two girls, or if you saw him in the above street areas between 1:30pm and 2:30pm, or witnessed the incident take place, please get in touch.

“If you have CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage that covers the area, we would be very interested in seeing it.

“You can call 101 quoting log 0899 of 6th August.”

News.title: Shocking moment car bursts into flames on busy UK motorway sending plumes of black smoke billowing across three lanes
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a campervan burst into flames on a busy motorway, sending a huge plume of black smoke billowing across the road.

Dramatic footage shows the vehicle engulfed in flames on the side of the M40 in Oxfordshire.



The blaze broke out at around 4pm on Sunday, August 9, between junction 10 at Ardley and junction 11 at Banbury.

In the video, flames can be seen shooting from the car as thick black smoke rises high above the motorway.



The inferno appears to intensify as the vehicle is completely surrounded by flames, with the smoke visible across the carriageway.

The dramatic footage was recorded by Chris Aramini-Brant, councillor for the Cropredy and Hook Norton division.



Lanes were closed following the blaze as emergency crews dealt with the incident and the fire damaged the road surface.

National Highways warned drivers of delays of more than 20 minutes as traffic began to build up around the scene.

The fire also caused damage to the road surface.

Fire crews were called to the vehicle and worked to tackle the blaze before carrying out a clean-up operation on the hard shoulder.



Oxfordshire Fire and Rescue Service confirmed that they were called at 3.48pm and sent three fire engines to tackle the blaze.

Firefighters used hose reel jets to extinguish the campervan after the fire spread to grass and scrubland on the side of the motorway.

Crews remained at the scene until around 5.15pm before leaving.

All lanes were eventually reopened around two hours after the fire broke out.

Residual delays then gradually dispersed and traffic returned to normal.



This incident comes just days after a lorry burst into flames on the A31 in Hampshire, sparking a huge blaze that spread into nearby heathland.

The fire, which broke out on Sunday evening, forced the A31 to close in both directions and saw more than 120 firefighters battle the flames.

Cops said 23 cars were abandoned by motorists after the blaze erupted, while National Highways warned of significant damage to the road.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The latest M40 blaze is understood to have caused no lasting disruption after the motorway was reopened and residual delays cleared.

The cause of the M40 fire is not yet known.

News.title: Shocking moment man, 21, smashes car into kebab shop while using phone causing front of takeaway to collapse
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a speeding driver who had no insurance ploughed into a kebab shop while on the phone.

Footage shows Daniel Mohammed, 21, losing control of his Ford Focus, before it smashes into Burslem’s Rose Fast Food takeaway in Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire – causing it to partially collapse.



Debris, including the building’s walls and windows, are seen crashing to the ground after the vehicle smashes into it.

The vehicle ends up in the middle of the road, as a huge dust cloud emanating from the rubble blows into the street.



Before the crash, Mohammed overtook a vehicle on a bend while he had his phone in his hand, and his passenger was asking him to slow down, Stoke Crown Court heard.

Mohammed’s passenger suffered a broken collar bone and fractures to two bones in her forearm after the crash at 6am on July 20, but nobody inside the takeaway was injured.



Staffordshire Police said Mohammed lost control of his car after overtaking another vehicle on a bend.

After the dramatic crash the building was partially demolished.



Mohammed, of Cobridge, was jailed for two years and two months after pleading guilty to causing serious injury by dangerous driving, using a vehicle without third party insurance, and using a handheld mobile phone while driving a vehicle.

Judge Graeme Smith told him he made a “deliberate decision to ignore the rules of the road” and “drove at speeds in excess of the speed limit”.

He added: “You overtook a vehicle on the approach to a zebra crossing where the zigzag lines indicate you should not overtake and also on a bend where you could not see whether anything was coming in the opposite direction.

“You were using a mobile phone at the time. You had been warned by your passenger to slow down but disregarded that warning.

“Having watched the video, it is astonishing that both of you were not more seriously injured.



“She was the more seriously injured. You were using the mobile phone and had no insurance.

“You accept responsibility for what happened. What happened appears to be out of character.

“However, there was a previous driving-related offence committed earlier last year. I cannot suspend the sentence because of its length.”

Mohammed was also banned from driving for three years and 10 months and until he passes an extended test.

The court also heard he had a conviction for drug-driving.



PC Tom Poole, of Stoke-on-Trent north local policing team, who led the investigation, said: “Mohammed’s reckless driving not only caused serious injury to his passenger but also had a great effect on a local business, which has sadly been closed since the collision.

“When he was interviewed in custody he answered ‘no comment’ to all questions, but we worked tirelessly to gather CCTV evidence, which eventually led to him pleading guilty in court.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our thoughts remain with all those affected by this incident and I hope this sentence offers them some closure.”

The passenger, who knew Mohammed through mutual friends, experienced tingling and reduced sensation in her fingers in the immediate aftermath of the crash, the court heard.

News.title: Brit TikToker facing death in Dubai ‘stabbed violent boyfriend in self defence after 5hr booze session’ as CCTV emerges
News.content:
A BRIT TikToker facing the death penalty in Dubai stabbed her violent boyfriend to death in self-defence after a five-hour drinking session, it is alleged.

Brooke George, 23, was arrested after the death of William Treeby, who suffered a single stab wound to the chest at a villa in Dubai on June 21.



The former John Lewis worker has been holed up in a hellhole prison station in the UAE since then.

She has now finally been handed a court date, and will appear on September 2.



Brooke admits inflicting the fatal wound – but says she picked up a knife during a struggle after being attacked by Treeby and prevented from leaving.

New details from the Dubai Public Prosecution investigation reveal Treeby, who was living in Dubai under the identity Kaspars Aglitis, was wanted in Britain to face trial over a cocaine conspiracy in Kent.



The files also show that he was heavily intoxicated and had allegedly punched Brooke in the face shortly before his death.

Toxicology results cited by the group Detained in Dubai, which is supporting Brooke’s family, show Treeby had a blood alcohol concentration of 188mg/dL, or approximately 0.19 per cent.

A UAE forensic expert concluded his level of intoxication was sufficient to affect his “awareness, perception and reactions”, according to the case material.

Investigators also documented fresh bruising and an injury to Brooke’s left eye which campaigners say was consistent with witness accounts that Treeby had punched her during the journey home from a bar.

The evidence provides the most detailed account yet of the hours preceding Treeby’s death – and is expected to be central to Brooke’s claim that she was defending herself.



CCTV cited in the investigation shows Brooke, Treeby and a friend arriving at McCafferty’s in Jumeirah Village Circle at around 3.23pm on June 21.

They remained there for several hours drinking before leaving at around 8pm.

According to the prosecution investigation, Treeby was “agitated” and “angry” and at one stage had to be calmed by his friend.



Campaigners say the evidence records that he punched Brooke in the face during an argument in the car before returning to the villa, where he angrily threw her belongings across the downstairs area.

Brooke told investigators she had returned to the villa to collect her handbag before leaving the country.

She said that when she opened an upstairs bedroom door, she found Treeby holding a knife.

Brooke told investigators she said she was leaving but Treeby refused to let her go and tried to push her.

She claims the knife fell during a struggle in which their friend intervened, before she picked it up and stabbed Treeby once.



A witness subsequently described Brooke as “crying hysterically”, according to the material released by Detained in Dubai.

She fled to Dubai airport with her bag, where staff noticed her injuries and emotional state.

Police records cited by the campaign group describe her as being in “shock”.

She initially remained silent before cooperating with investigators and giving her account of what had happened.

Forensic examination recorded fresh bruising and injury around her left eye as well as several other injuries which had been sustained during the preceding days.



Brooke also made an allegation about what had been happening privately during her relationship with Treeby.

When confronted with witness claims that Treeby had treated her kindly, she told investigators: “He sometimes assaults me when I refuse to have sex with him.”

Radha Stirling, chief executive of Detained in Dubai, said: “This is not a case where Brooke denies causing the fatal injury.

“The question is why it happened and whether she was defending herself.

“The prosecution’s own evidence confirms that Treeby was heavily intoxicated, had punched Brooke shortly beforehand, was angry and agitated, and had thrown her belongings throughout the villa.



“Brooke was subsequently described as hysterical and in shock.

“She is now facing a potential death sentence and it is imperative that her allegations of violence and her account of self defence receive the most rigorous examination before any irreversible judgment is made.”

Stirling also raised concerns about witnesses who have since left the UAE.

She said: “It is extremely difficult to secure a fair hearing in the UAE, particularly when key witnesses have left the country and are no longer available to be cross examined.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Where a young woman is facing the possibility of capital punishment, every witness and every piece of evidence must be subjected to the highest level of scrutiny.”



Brooke’s family said she was “very stressed and panicking” ahead of next month’s hearing, adding: “She’s scared.”

News.title: Amber Met Office extreme heat warning issued as temperatures could reach 38C
News.content:
The Met Office has issued a rare amber weather warning for extreme heat, external for parts of England on Thursday, where temperatures could peak at 38C.

The highest temperatures will be in parts of the east, south-east and the Midlands and may lead to impacts on transport, infrastructure and health.

The last time we saw temperatures above 36C in August was 2020 when 36.4C was recorded at Heathrow and Kew Gardens.

The Met Office warning runs from 0900 BST until 2359 on Thursday, which is when the summer's latest heatwave reaches its peak.

If the temperature does hit 38C, it would equal this year's top temperature of 38C recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on 26 June.

News.title: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
News.content:
At a bakery in central London, stock has been flying off the shelves.

"I've sold, like, 100 this morning," a staff member tells the BBC. But it's not baked goods driving queues out of the door - customers are here to buy eclipse glasses.

They are among those hoping to catch a safe glimpse of Wednesday's solar eclipse - the UK's most significant since 1999 - but struggling to get their hands on the right gear.

Experts have urged eclipse enthusiasts not to look directly at the Sun - with even brief exposure causing lasting damage - and to seek out specialist glasses instead.

But online, pairs that meet safety specifications have all but sold out. Those still available either require a hefty next-day delivery fee or simply cannot arrive on time.

Even the Royal Museums Greenwich - recommended as a reputable retailer by UK health officials - has sold out, citing an "unprecedented volume" of orders.

"I Googled 'where can I get eclipse glasses but not through the post', because I realised I was too late," one customer waiting to buy three pairs at the bakery on Monday tells BBC Radio 4's PM programme.

"People have been struggling to find them all over," says another.

With around 90% of the Sun set to be obscured by the Moon, the UK is expecting its most significant eclipse in 27 years.

The right glasses should have the international safety standard ISO 12312-2 printed on them, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has advised, and the lenses should not be scratched, torn or damaged.

It has also advised caution surrounding glasses being sold online, as the scramble for safe spectacles has prompted eclipse chasers to trawl social media for tips.

News.title: Watch: Family narrowly escapes home during Colombia earthquake
News.content:
A family captured video of the moment they fled their home during an earthquake in Colombia.

Liliana PÃ©rez Ocampo and her family escaped moments before their home was rocked by a 7.4 magnitude quake on Monday.

"At first, we thought it was just a mild tremor like the ones that usually happen in Colombia, but when more than 30 seconds passed and everything was shaking harder, we realised it was an earthquake," the mother-of-four told the BBC World Service.

Her family, including two young children at school, are safe.

"In the end, material things can be replaced," she said. "The most important thing is life, and we have that."

With at least 169 people killed, this has been the strongest earthquake to hit Colombia in the 21st Century, according to the country's Geological Service.

More on this story.

News.title: Anne Hathaway pokes fun at 'fake baby bump' theories
News.content:
Anne Hathaway has poked fun at those who suggested her baby bump didn't look real after a recent film premiere, telling them she had "fake hair, real bump".

The US actress turned heads in an outfit that showed off her bare bump at the launch of her new film, The End of Oak Street, in Los Angeles on Sunday.

It sparked a flurry of comments on social media, external from people saying "Why does it look fake?" and "Oh come on. That is not real." But others leapt to her defence, with one writing: "A lot of people in these comments have never seen a pregnant belly on someone who has abs."

Hathaway, 43, announced in June that she is expecting her third child with husband Adam Shulman.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and for many people, the high streets they grew up with are "unrecognisable".

He said the plans were "shaped" by a BBC News investigation which exposed organised crime on high streets, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes, vapes, cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham told the BBC that the changes would make it "easier for police to close a vape shop and have it closed for longer".

He said: "At the same time we're changing the planning regime... which should stop the proliferation of vape shops on our high streets."

The prime minister added that Operation Vulcan in Cheetham Hill, Greater Manchester, cleared the area of counterfeits and crime and "proved" what could be achieved.

"When I look at police reform across England, I will be asking for a similar approach to be taken," he said. "I want the strongest possible neighbourhood policing, with all agencies involved, to rip out criminal behaviour that is pulling places down."

Burnham said he did not accept the decline of the high street as "inevitable".

"I don't see why anywhere should have to accept they have empty shops, vape shops and the challenges that come with that."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: Call with No 10 gives us hope, PC Harper's mother says
News.content:
Cole and Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020. Under changes to the Sentencing Act made this year, they will become eligible for release from custody next January.

They are in a category of prisoners - those who have committed certain serious violent or sexual crimes - who until now would have had to serve at least two-thirds of their sentence in jail before being considered for release.

Downing Street had earlier warned it would not be possible to exclude "one or two offenders" convicted of manslaughter from the early release scheme.

However, the BBC has been told that Burnham has now instructed his justice secretary to find a way to exclude Cole and Bowers from the scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

In a later statement, the PM said he was "increasingly confident" that work to increase space in the prison system "will allow us to reduce the number of people released early".

He added: "And, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC [Andrew] Harper, prevent their early release altogether."

Adlam said the conflicting reports had been making her "more and more angry" and the uncertainty had left her family "in turmoil".

Of the phone call she received, she said. "I think the fact it's actually come from Downing Street, I've got to try and have some faith in it, but at the same time I've got to protect my own feelings."

Thames Valley Police officer PC Harper, 28, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged behind the getaway car of three teenagers who had fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Adlam said: "Everybody is watching this. This is obviously extremely personal to us but it's to do with the country as a whole really. This is really vital to get right, it feels like a hash, like a rush job."

Speaking about Cole and Bowers, she added: "They weren't given extreme sentences and I'm only asking for them to do what they were given, I'm not asking for anything more than they were sentenced."

News.title: England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: Perseid meteor shower reaches peak: When and where to catch a glimpse
News.content:
The best annual meteor shower has once again returned to our skies, and the Perseids dazzling display is set to peak on Wednesday night.

But skywatchers will be treated to not one, but two, impressive astronomical events within just a few hours of each other.

A deep partial solar eclipse will be also visible in the UK in the early evening before the Sun sets and the stars emerge. While the two events are unrelated, their timing makes for an exceptional night of stargazing.

Astronomer Dr Becky Smethurst said it was "the perfect cosmic coincidence of events".

Here is when to look up and where you will have the best views of the meteor shower.

News.title: Murder arrest over fatal shooting in Clapham
News.content:
A man has died in a shooting in south London and police have arrested a suspect on suspicion of murder.

Officers and paramedics were called to Willington Road, Clapham, just before 22:00 BST on Monday following reports of gunshots near The Landor pub.

A 25-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, the Metropolitan Police said.

Shortly after the shooting, a 22-year-old man attended hospital with a gunshot wound. He was arrested and remains in hospital while police await an update on his condition, the force added.

News.title: Two in court over teens' Thailand drug courier case
News.content:
Two people accused of trafficking teenagers to Thailand as part of an international drug ring have appeared in court.

Tremaine Jeanne and Jessica Sani, both 28, are charged with drug offences and conspiring to arrange the travel of another with a view to exploitation.

It is alleged they used two 17-year-olds as drug couriers after they were caught with 64kg (141lb) of cannabis in their suitcases while travelling back to the UK.

The teenagers from Cardiff, were arrested in Thailand in June and remain in custody. They are being supported by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

Four other people appeared at Cardiff Magistrates' Court last Friday in connection with the case.

A 23-year-old man from Keighley, West Yorkshire, who was also arrested on suspicion of improper importation of controlled drugs, has been bailed.

Jeanne, from Llanrumney, and Sani, from Newport, are both charged with conspiring to fraudulently evade a prohibition on the importation of a Class B drug and four counts of conspiring to arrange or facilitate the travel of another person with a view to exploitation.

They appeared via video link and spoke only to confirm their names, dates of birth and addresses. They were not asked to enter pleas.

Jeanne and Sani were remanded in custody and will next appear with their co-accused at Cardiff Crown Court on 4 September.

South Wales Police officers were told in June the teenagers had been arrested, and launched an investigation into the "circumstances" behind their trip.

A spokesman for the force said: "The children remain in custody in Thailand where they are being supported by their families and the Foreign and Commonwealth Office.

"The families have been updated regarding the arrests and charges."

News.title: Teenager lured to park before knifepoint robbery
News.content:
Two teenagers who robbed one of their classmates at knifepoint and shared footage of the attack online have been given suspended jail terms.

Zain Khan and Nahid Ali, both 19, lured the victim from Craven College in Skipton, North Yorkshire, to nearby Airedale Park on 6 March 2024, where he was threatened with a knife, beaten, and made to transfer more than Â£800 into Khan's bank account.

Both men, who are from Keighley, West Yorkshire, admitted robbery and Khan also admitted possessing a knife.

At Bradford Crown Court on Friday Khan was given a two year jail sentence suspended for two years, and Ali was given a 20-month sentence also suspended for two years.

Khan also received a nine-month sentence for possessing a knife, suspended for two years.

Both Khan and Ali were ordered to complete 240 and 200 hours of unpaid work.

Two other teenagers who were involved in the attack were dealt with at an earlier hearing and ordered to pay compensation.

The court heard how on the day of the attack, the victim had been to the college cafe with Khan, a fellow student who he believed to be a friend.

While there, Khan suggested they go to the local Morrisons supermarket to buy food.

News.title: Risk of explosion at warehouse fire closed M25
News.content:
The risk of an explosion at a large warehouse fire closed both carriageways of the M25 between junctions 22 and 21A.

Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue was called to the blaze in Ventura Park, Old Parkbury Lane, Colney Street, in St Albans, at 09:21 BST.

National Highways said 15 crews had been at the scene and the motorway had been closed because of the risk of a "secondary explosion, along with smoke and debris affecting the carriageway".

It was shut for about one hour and reopened at about 12:15 with 40mph speed restrictions.

News.title: London Heathrow no longer Europe's busiest airport
News.content:
Heathrow has lost its position as Europe's busiest airport to Istanbul, new figures show.

The west London airport said 7.86m passengers passed through its four terminals in July, whereas Istanbul Airport in Turkey's largest city recorded 8.15m passengers.

The US-Israel conflict with Iran has had an impact on Heathrow's passenger traffic with Middle East routes in July down 20.2% year-on-year.

Annual figures from trade body Airports Council International show Heathrow was Europe's busiest airport from 1996 to 2019. It lost that title in 2020 amid coronavirus travel restrictions before regaining it in 2023, holding it ever since.

Heathrow continues to operate its two runways at near-full capacity and is seeking government permission to build a third.

News.title: Suspicious item near canal was replica grenade
News.content:
Police have confirmed a suspicious item which led to road closures around a canal in Retford was a replica grenade.

Nottinghamshire Police set up a cordon and a number of roads were closed around Chesterfield Canal and Raglan Road on Monday.

The force gave an update on Tuesday to say the item was a training device, which was "safely removed" before roads reopened.

The force had said there was "no threat to the public", but the area was cordoned off as a precaution. Officers thanked the public for their "patience and cooperation".

News.title: Great-grandad with cancer risks his health to help others on 460-mile journey
News.content:
A great-grandfather with bladder and kidney cancer is walking 462 miles (743km) for charity, despite knowing it could impact his own treatment.

John Eryl Parry, 78, from Pontypool, Torfaen, began his coast-to-coast journey at the UK's most easterly point in Lowestoft, Suffolk, on 21 June, and is due to reach St David's Head in Pembrokeshire on 11 August.

He found out he had cancer after he fell off a ladder and was taken to hospital.

John admitted he had not told his oncology team about his challenge, but said he was warned by a doctor that his body would "change" during it, and it could impact his treatment plan.

News.title: Cocaine worth £232m found in banana shipment
News.content:
Cocaine with a street value of Â£232m was discovered hidden in a large shipment of bananas from South America.

The 2.9-tonne (2,900kg) haul was smuggled into London Gateway Port in Thurrock, Essex, on Thursday.

Border Force intercepted the cocaine at the port and removed it from a trailer, before the drugs courier took the empty load to an address near Buntingford, Hertfordshire.

Nine men allegedly connected to the bust were then arrested and later released on bail.

Border Force had been tipped off about the illegal consignment by the National Crime Agency.

YouTube star and music educator Ms. Rachel and her husband, Aron Accurso, are releasing a debut 23-track record on Sept. 25.

"Music is such a wonderful way for people to bond, for parents to bond. I know from the minute my kids were born, we’re singing to them," said Ms. Rachel, whose full name is Rachel Griffin Accurso.

The couple originally launched their immensely popular YouTube channel in 2019, with her husband known online as "Mr. Aron." Instrumentation is central to the album's educational focus.

"I am a music educator, so I get excited about kids hearing a real clarinet on ‘Icky Sticky Bubble Gum’ and kids getting excited about hearing more real instruments," said Ms. Rachel.

The record, "I'm So Happy," also promotes social development with tracks like "I Could Be Your Friend."

Honoree Rachel Griffin Accurso (aka Ms. Rachel), and husband Aron Accurso attend the Glamour Women of the Year Awards at The Plaza Hotel, Nov. 4, 2025, in New York ( AP Photo/Evan Agostini )

Inclusivity remains key: "We’re always thinking about all kinds of kids, whether they have disabilities, whether they’re autistic," she said. "We just want the world to feel like it’s helpful to all children and the musical worlds as well."

The music spans several genres, featuring a bossa nova arrangement on "I Love a Rainbow" alongside a bluegrass-inspired take on the traditional classic "Old McDonald."

Ultimately, the release provides families an opportunity to connect offline.

"Music is at the heart of our show," added Aron Accurso. "And so, we’ve always wanted to release the music and have families experience the music away from the screen."

Big arrangements and simple songs

“I'm So Happy” was co-produced by Accurso and Grammy winner Scott Riesett and principally arranged by Accurso. He reimagined a number of Ms. Rachel's fan favorite songs and childhood classics with a team of 19 vocalists and 42 instrumentalists.

“It’s songs that people know from the show, but we decided to expand them and elevate them with new arrangements and reproducing them,” Aron Accurso said. “It was a process of, you know, looking at them and saying, ‘OK, what else can we do to this to make it sparkle more? What can we add to it? What does it need to be on the album?’”

He says they mostly hope that the album will inspire “living room dance parties, because that’s what we love with our children,” he said. “We love to put on an album and dance around.”

An album next to advocacy

Ms. Rachel has made headlines over the last few years for using her social media platforms to advocate for global humanitarian crises, with particular attention given to the plight of children in Gaza and those detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Most recently, she shared comments about the mysterious death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells in Mississippi, a case shadowed by the state’s fraught racial history and lingering distrust in law enforcement.

“We know the investigation and everything that followed would have been different if Nolan Wells were white and his friends were black. Nolan and his family deserve justice,” she wrote on Instagram.

Ms. Rachel says she knows her album may bring attention to her advocacy and vice versa.

“I view myself as an advocate for children’s rights so anytime they’re being violated by anyone anywhere, I want to be speaking out,” she said. “I want families to be happy and safe and healthy, and I think that’s a wonderful thing. So, if it’s brought up with the album, that’s great.”

A six-year-old girl has died and a second child has been taken to hospital with a leg injury after a serious crash involving a lorry and a car.

Emergency services responded to reports of a collision on the A12 northbound carriageway near junction 28 shortly after 10.30am on Monday.

The road was closed in both directions to allow emergency services to work, but the six-year-old girl died at the scene. The second child is being treated in hospital.

The force said no arrests were made at the scene, with the lorry driver passing all road-side tests.

The lorry driver will be interviewed in the coming days, police said.

open image in gallery Essex Police said all emergency services were called to the northbound road close to junction 28 shortly after 10.30am on Monday. ( Alamy/PA )

Detective Inspector Mark Fraser, of the serious collision investigation unit, said: “First and foremost, my thoughts are very much with this young child’s family and wider loved ones.

“We have specialist officers in place with them to ensure they are given as much support as possible.

“Our investigation is progressing and we will be interviewing a driver of a lorry in the coming days.

“Incidents such as this are clearly sensitive and complex and we are committed to fully understanding the circumstances around what happened yesterday.

“If you have any information, dash cam or footage of any kind which you have not yet shared with us, please get in touch.”

To submit a report to Essex Police online, visit www.essex.police.uk/digital101.

The force has asked that people who do so quote incident 421 of 10 August. Alternatively contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: AOC reveals cost of egg freezing as insurance doesn’t cover treatment
News.content:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has revealed the cost of freezing her eggs as she explained that her insurance does not cover her treatment.

During an Instagram livestream Saturday (8 August), AOC explained to her 9.6 million followers that she was undergoing the treatment “to feel more in control of my life”.

In a later Q&A session on Instagram, the Democratic congresswoman revealed that her insurance “covers nothing” and she will be paying for it all “out of pocket”.

She explained that there are two aspects of the payment: the fee for the medicine and also to the clinic.

The 36-year-old added that she is going to a clinic that specifically has options for women who do not have insurance coverage, and she estimates her grand total will be approximately $9,000.

President Donald Trump’s reported covert departure from Turkey aboard an aircraft other than Air Force One has triggered a wave of AI-generated memes and jokes online.

On July 8, following a NATO summit in Turkey, the Republican president quietly left the country on a military aircraft, even as the White House maintained that he was traveling aboard Air Force One, The Washington Post reported Monday.

The operation, reportedly prompted by an Iranian assassination threat, began with the 80-year-old president boarding the older Air Force One in Ankara in full view of cameras. He was later moved in secret to a smaller plane via “an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies,” according to the Post, citing people familiar with the matter. The original Air Force One, still carrying reporters and some administration staffers, served as a “decoy.”

“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” a White House spokesperson told the outlet, while defending the new Qatari-gifted Air Force One, which reportedly lacks the necessary security measures.

The elaborate maneuver, also reported by The New York Times, quickly became fodder for social media users, who imagined the president squeezed into everything from a catering cart to a laundry bin.

Ron Filipkowski, editor-in-chief of MeidasTouch, posted what appeared to be an AI-generated image of Trump lying inside a metal cart on the tarmac beside cartons of McDonald’s fries and bottles of Diet Coke.

“EXCLUSIVE. Meidas has obtained footage of Trump hiding in the catering truck while switching planes,” he jokingly wrote on X.

Another user shared an image of a flight attendant pushing a service cart down the aisle of a packed plane, with Trump seated inside.

Elsewhere, a parody account calling itself the Associated Fress posted an image of the GOP president poking his head out of a McDonald’s truck parked beside Air Force One — an apparent reference to the viral image of Trump working the drive-thru at a Pennsylvania McDonald’s during the 2024 campaign.

Another AI-generated meme showed the president being whisked away from Air Force One in a laundry cart, his head emerging from a heap of towels.

A left-leaning account repurposed imagery from Jaws, riffing on the film’s famous tagline with: “We’re gonna need a bigger catering cart!”

Yet another meme depicted a catering truck painted in Air Force One’s color scheme and bearing the presidential seal. “American coward-n-chief, Donald Trump, sneaks out of Turkey aboard Food Truck One,” the caption read.

Another X account posted a clip of the HBO show House of the Dragon, depicting King Aegon Targaryen shouting “I’m alive!” alongside the caption: “Trump watching air force 1 get shot down with all the journalist[s] he hates on board.”

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool ‘agree’ Barcola terms, Arsenal offer Lewis-Skelly to Chelsea, Man City close in on Rodri replacement
News.content:
Liverpool are hoping to swiftly add to the loan signing of Ronald Araujo by hashing out a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola after reaching a reported agreement over personal terms. Barcola leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger.

Arsenal’s busy transfer window looks set to continue as they move on from their disappointment in not signing Vinicius Jr. They are hunting alternatives in the forward line with Julian Alvarez and the aforementioned Barcola on their list but defensive reinforcements may yet come in the form of Cristian Romero. The Tottenham captain is rumoured to leave Spurs this summer and is eyeing up a switch to their closest rivals.

Meanwhile, Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca – who are considering a second bid after an initial offer of £38m was rejected. City seem to be making preparations for that outcome as they close in on the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille.

Finally, Manchester United are still searching for a left-back with Newcastle’s Lewis Hall seemingly off the table they instead turned their interest on the likes of Antonee Robinson, Jorge Salinas and Joaquin Seys.

An explosive row within Reform UK has burst into the open after the party’s leader Nigel Farage publicly slapped down one of his key allies for calling a former Tory defence secretary a “traitor”.

Mr Farage said his home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf had gone “over the top” in the attack on Ben Wallace, a former soldier who served in Northern Ireland.

Mr Yusuf had even suggested that Mr Wallace should be prosecuted for his role in Afghans coming to Britain after the UK’s withdrawal.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage has reprimanded Reform’s Zia Yusuf ( Reuters )

Asked about the “traitor” outburst, Mr Farage told The Sun: “That’s too strong a word. I shall give him a ticking off.”

He added: “I’ll speak to him today... it’s over the top.”

The attack erupted after Mr Wallace criticised Reform’s new pledge to deport all foreign nationals from Britain’s jails to countries such as El Salvador.

Writing on X in response, Mr Yusuf said it was “incredible that this moron was defence secretary. Our policy today is in direct response to your government’s failures.”

He said the new policy “may well include some of the thousands of Afghans you imported, including those who had not been vetted properly and including Taliban fighters (!). You know, the ones you took a super injunction out to keep secret from the British people?

“That’s why I call you a traitor to Britain. You fit the dictionary definition.”

He also posted a poll in which he asked if the Tory politician should be “prosecuted for treason”.

open image in gallery Former defence secretary Ben Wallace was also called ‘a moron’ ( AFP/Getty )

Earlier, Tim Montgomerie, a commentator and high-profile Reform supporter said on X, formerly Twitter: “This isn't acceptable from Zia... Zia's language and attitude towards any opponent is inappropriate and counter-productive. Opponents are opponents... they aren't enemies... or "moron"s.”

He added that “one of the biggest question marks over Nigel Farage’s leadership is whether he brings Zia under control. ZY is a man of huge talents but too much of his social media output is intemperate and reinforces Reform's number one problem: our negative tactical voting challenge.”

He also said he had raised the issue “privately and repeatedly” with both men.

Labour MP Oliver Ryan called for Mr Yusuf to be sacked.

He said: “This Reform nonentity calling a former serving Captain in the Scots Guards, and former defence secretary, a "traitor to Britain" is a... disgrace. What happened to decency? Zia ought to be sacked from whatever made up Reform job he has.”

Myanmar’s military escalated attacks in the run-up to the last election in a deliberate campaign to inflict greater harm on civilians, with investigators finding evidence of torture and sexual violence, according to a new UN report.

Airstrikes on homes, schools, medical facilities and displacement camps “intensified” ahead of the election, held between ‌December last year and January, and continued afterwards, investigators appointed by the Human Rights Council found.

The report – covering the period from July 2025 to June 2026 – was released by the Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar, which was set up in 2018 by the UN to investigate abuses against civilians in the Southeast Asian country.

It found the military has increasingly used weapons that have made it harder for people to escape the attacks. “Growing use of motorised power gliders and drones has made attacks harder for civilians to see coming, cutting the time people have to flee or find shelter,” it noted.

The revelation of abuses as recently as earlier this year, including during the election period, undermine attempts by the new military-backed government to present itself as legitimate and stable as it pursues a diplomatic drive to deepen ties with neighbouring countries.

Aung Min Hlaing, the junta leader who took over the civilian role of president after the election, visited China, India and Laos earlier this year and Thailand most recently as part of an ongoing effort to bolster his international legitimacy and re-enter the regional diplomatic mainstream.

open image in gallery A man clears debris after an airstrike by Myanmar's military in Kyauktaw in western Rakhine state ( AFP/Getty )

However, Asean, the regional bloc of Southeast Asian nations, has banned Myanmar from its meetings for failing to comply with a peace plan agreed upon in April 2021 and has pressured Naypyidaw for the unconditional release of Aung San Suu Kyi, who has remained in detention since the military removed her elected government in a 2021 coup.

The military’s seizure of power triggered a civil war that has so far killed over 100,000 people, according to a conflict monitor. The junta detained Ms Suu Kyi and thousands of other political opponents as it cracked down on resistance to military rule.

The coup was led by Min Aung Hlaing, who was the army chief then and became the junta’s de facto leader.

After years of fighting with anti-junta forces, the military held elections around the turn of this year that were widely criticised as neither free nor fair. The military-backed process resulted in Min Aung Hlaing becoming president in April 2026, allowing the former coup leader to formally consolidate his grip on power.

open image in gallery Thailand's prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, center left, and Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing review an honor guard during a welcome ceremony in Bangkok ( AP )

“Communities across Myanmar are not only living under the constant threat of violence, but are also coping with the profound and lasting impact of what they have endured,” said Nicholas Koumjian, the head of the Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar.

Investigators said they documented widespread torture and sexual violence in military-run detention facilities, including cases tied to a 2025 law that criminalised criticism of the elections.

The military-run government enacted the Law on the Protection of Multiparty Democratic General Elections, commonly called the Election Protection Law, criminalising speech, protests or social media posts deemed to criticise or disrupt the general election. Violations of the law carry harsh penalties ranging from three years in prison to 20 years in jail, life imprisonment, or even the death penalty.

As the election approached, the report found, the military increasingly used low-cost paramotors, gyrocopters and drones to conduct low-altitude strikes with unguided explosives.

The investigators said they were examining incidents in Sagaing region where pilots had allegedly cut their engines before reaching targets, allowing them to glide silently and giving civilians little warning.

Investigations over the past year showed “the frequency and intensity of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed by the Myanmar military and by various armed groups continued to escalate", the report said.

open image in gallery People walk past destroyed buildings following airstrikes in Kyauktaw town in western Rakhine state ( AFP/Getty )

Mr Koumjian said their investigation was focused on command structure and how the orders would be given for such airstrikes. "In particular, there are many airstrikes targeting, hitting schools. Children are often the victims of these airstrikes and also hospitals. So our team is collecting that evidence of where it has occurred, the kind of munitions that are used," he said.

The investigation draws on more than 1,600 sources, including over 750 witness accounts, along with photographs, video, forensic evidence and satellite imagery.

While most of the evidence concerns the military and allied militias, the investigators are also looking at abuses by armed groups opposed to the military.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“We have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; we were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

Sports.title: Who is Jose Mourinho’s wife Matilde Faria and how many children do the couple have?
Sports.content:
JOSE Mourinho has been one of the loudest voices in football for more than 20 years.

But the woman who has the “biggest influence” on him has maintained a much lower profile – here’s everything we know about the serial winner’s wife and kids.



Who is Jose Mourinho’s wife Matilde Faria?

Matilde Faria has followed the Special One through Benfica, Uniao de Leiria, Porto, Chelsea, Inter Milan, Real Madrid, back to Chelsea, Man Utd, Spurs, Roma, Fenerbahce, a return to Benfica, and now a second stint at the Bernabeu.

Born in Angola, Matilde grew up in Setubal, the Portuguese port city south of Lisbon where Jose Mourinho was born and where a street now carries his name.



Known to family as Tami, she knew him as a teenager and married him in 1989, before he’d managed a professional side.

In May 2014, the same day her husband was named a United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) ambassador against hunger, Matilde was appointed a WFP Special Ambassador for school feeding, promoting the agency’s work providing free school meals to around 24million children a year.



Mourinho has been blunt about the pecking order at home.

In 2015, he told The Big Issue: “My wife and my son and my daughter have the biggest influence on me, that’s for sure. And why? Because they are the bosses and control everything in the house!”

He added: “When it comes to make big decisions – where to go, where to work, when to change – on this kind of thing they have a big influence on me.”



Did Matilde Faria stop Mourinho becoming England manager?

England sacked Steve McClaren after failing to qualify for Euro 2008, and Mourinho, freshly out of Chelsea, was in talks to replace him.

In 2014, he explained: “I was almost, almost, almost, almost England manager at that time. My wife was right. She told me not to take it.”

Asked how close he came, he held a pen above an imaginary dotted line and said: “This close.”

He continued: “[Frank] Lampard, [John] Terry, Joe Cole, everybody, was saying, ‘Come, come, come.

“My players said, ‘The guys from Manchester United and Liverpool call us and say to us: Tell your boss to come.’ I had lots of positive things to push me…



“I cannot wait two years for a big competition. I cannot be spending two years playing against Kazakhstan and San Marino.”

He added: “In the end, my wife was saying, ‘No football, no matches is not for you’.”

Fabio Capello got the job, while Mourinho went to Inter and won the Champions League.

How many children do Jose Mourinho and Matilde Faria have?

Mourinho and Matilde have two children – daughter Matilde, known in the family as Tita, was born in 1996, and son Jose Mario Jr, known as Zuca, followed in 2000.



In 2013, he had his wife’s and their two children’s names tattooed on his left wrist.

Both kids had a nomadic childhood tracking their father around Europe – Matilde said she attended 11 schools before university.

Jose Jr went into football, coming through the youth systems at Real Madrid and Chelsea as a promising goalkeeper before signing a two-year scholarship at Fulham in 2016.

Since leaving the Cottagers the following year, Jose Jr has been away from the game.

But reports suggest he aims to follow in his father’s footsteps and pursue a career in coaching.



His daughter did a master’s degree at the Conde Nast College of Fashion and Design in London and runs her own jewellery label.

She married property consultant Danny Graham on October 12, 2024, at the family estate in Azeitao near Setubal.

The couple met as teens in London, but it was almost a decade later that he popped the question during a holiday in Portugal.

Matilde told Vogue: “He got down on one knee on the beach just by my family’s place. It couldn’t have been more perfect.

“After it happened, we spent the evening at home with my family, had pizza and wine to celebrate, and called our friends and family to share the news.”

Sports.title: Awkward moment new signing left hanging by his girlfriend as he goes to kiss her at transfer unveiling
Sports.content:
THIS is the embarrassing moment a footballer’s unveiling was ruined when he was snubbed by his girlfriend after leaning in for a kiss.

Luciano Rodriguez was celebrating his move to Cruzeiro and was joined by his partner – who’s been dubbed the Uruguayan Kim Kardashian – for the special day.



The striker, who just missed out on a place in Uruguay’s 26-man squad for the World Cup, has joined the Brazilian giants on loan.

But Rodriguez’s arrival has been overshadowed by an awkward moment after the switch from ambitious Saudi Arabian side Neom went through.





The marksman, 23, was joined by his girlfriend Antonela Ciavaglia for snaps as soon as he had put pen-to-paper.

And the Uruguayan model left Rodriguez hanging as he went to kiss her in front of the photographers.

Ciavaglia quickly dashed off, leaving the former Sunderland target sheepishly touching his hair as he hoped the gaffe had not been spotted.

But, in a huge blow for Rodriguez, footage of the incident has gone viral after being uploaded onto social media.



Ciavaglia has been forced to deny there is a rift between them and insisted she rushed away because of feeling nervous.

The influencer, 23, said: “When I entered, I greeted him and when I left, I was very nervous.

“The moment overwhelmed me and I preferred to give him space. There was no disrespect or anything like what they are trying to make it seem like.”



Ciavaglia has been dubbed the Uruguayan Kim Kardashian after amassing more than 170,000 followers across her social media platforms.

And Rodriguez has linked up with two former Premier League stars following his move.

Luis Sinisterra, who joined Leeds in a £25million deal four years ago, is now on Cruzeiro’s books after arriving from Bournemouth.

Ex-West Brom talisman Matheus Pereira is also among Rodriguez’s new team-mates.



Cruzeiro are fifth in the Brazilian top-flight – sitting 15 points adrift of table-topping Palmeiras.

Rodriguez could be handed his debut in a Copa Libertadores tie against Flamengo later this week.
