Sports.title: Man Utd star Ayden Heaven’s mum reveals how argument with Arsenal coach Per Mertesacker helped her son’s career
Sports.content:
AYDEN HEAVEN’S mother has recalled her unusual argument with Per Mertesacker that shaped her son’s career.

Lisa Heaven tired to put up a fight against Mertesacker when the former Arsenal academy manager told her Heaven should change positions.



Ayden Heaven, 19, had spent most of his youth career playing as deep-lying midfielder.

But when Mertesacker first saw the youngster play at Arsenal, he was convinced that he needed to be shifted to defence.



The decision ultimately proved to be the right one, earning Heaven a reputation as a defender that landed him his move to Manchester United.

But Lisa, who is also Heaven’s agent, remembers immediately trying to shut down any suggestion that her son should be shifted back during his time with the Gunners.

She told the Stretford Paddock: “I remember the conversation, it was between myself and Per Mertesacker.

“I was having a debate with Per like, ‘he’s not a defender.’ He was saying he was and I was saying he wasn’t.

“I remember it was one of his first couple of games, and it was Per’s first season as the academy manager.

“Ayden made a save off the line and I saw Per’s face light up. I thought, ‘He’s not a defender. He’s scoring goals.’

“I think he was playing as a No6 and No8 role, really box-to-box. Per wasn’t having it.

“He was like, ‘He is a great player, but he is going to be a defender.'”

Heaven soon switched to the back line and quickly became one of the top-rated defensive youth prospects in the country.

The teenager had played just one full season at centre-back before he was snapped up by Man Utd.



Lisa revealed: “When we came to Manchester United, he had only been playing that role for one full season as a centre-back. Before that it was a centre-defensive [midfield] role.

“So that is where he gets his ability on the ball, carrying the ball forward, left and right foot. He is still mastering the position. It was Per that called it.”

Heaven left Arsenal for Man Utd last summer in search of regular first team football.

Sports.title: Arsenal release statement banning fans from stadium for offences including assault and racism
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have banned nine supporters for abusive and discriminatory behaviour following their title-winning 2025/26 season.

Football banning orders and stadium bans have been dished out that prevent the fans from attending Arsenal matches for between one and three years.



Arsenal have announced that the action has been taken against the individuals following offences involving assault, racism, antisemitism, anti-social behaviour and homophobia.

Gunners chiefs are also assisting police with a further 13 ongoing investigations covering alleged offences taking place both at games and online.



Arsenal have been working with a data science company to try and crack down on online abuse directed at players, coaches, staff and supporters.

The club verified more than 17,700 posts and comments as abusive during the previous campaign.

That work resulted in 39 individuals being referred to Arsenal or other clubs for further action and nine cases handed over to law enforcement.

Arsenal CEO, Richard Garlick, said: “This season gave us many moments to be proud of and showed once again the role football can play in bringing people together.

“The overwhelming majority of our supporters help make Arsenal a welcoming, inclusive and respectful place to be.

“Those standards are a big part of who we are, shaping the experience people have when they come to Arsenal, and how we represent our club around the world.

Sports.title: Man Utd's last-minute attempt to sign Real Madrid star Endrick revealed
Sports.content:
Man Utd's last-minute attempt to sign Real Madrid star Endrick revealed

Manchester United considered a surprise loan approach for Real Madrid forward Endrick, who headed out last term, but Jose Mourinho wants to keep him beyond this summer

View 2 Images Endrick has struggled for form at Real Madrid - but he will not be allowed to leave this summer

Manchester United made moves to sign Endrick from Real Madrid before Jose Mourinho made it clear he was part of his plans moving forward.

‌



The Brazilian star, who scored the winner to down England at Wembley only two years ago, has endured a difficult start to life at the Bernabeu. So much so that he headed out on loan last term, playing for Lyon in a bid to rediscover his form.

‌



Endrick has now returned to the Spanish capital after scoring eight times in 21 outings during his time in Ligue 1. Loan offers continue to come in for the 20-year-old with United among those making their interest known.

‌



Fellow Premier League side Aston Villa, and Serie A giants Roma were also keen, but Mourinho has stepped in and, according to AS, made it clear to Endrick that he will play an important role for Los Blancos over the coming season.

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

It all but ends any hopes United would've had of signing the ex-Palmeiras sensation. Their interest comes as something of a surprise given the depth they have in the final third. They've just welcomed Marcus Rashford back from his loan spell away and he comes into a team that already includes Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Amad Diallo.

United's summer has focused on bolstering their midfield, they would also welcome an addition at left-back, but investing in their frontline has not been seen as a priority.

‌



Mourinho, who is back at Real for a second stint more than a decade after leaving, sees Endrick as someone he can use as an out-and-out striker as well an option on the right wing. The Brazilian was used in those positions during his loan spell at Lyon.

View 2 Images The Brazilian spent time on loan at Lyon last season

Los Blancos will be keen to get value from Endrick given the investment they made in him, when he was nothing more than potential. They landed him in July 2024 after he turned 18 and paid an initial €35million (£29.9m), with potential add-ons totalling €25m (£21.3m).

‌



He was included in the 26-man Brazil squad for the World Cup by Carlo Ancelotti, who signed him when he was in charge at Real. The attacker appeared in all but one of the team’s games at the tournament.

Mourinho and Madrid haven't wasted time in improving their squad this summer with Yan Diomande, the £120m signing from RB Leipzig, their marquee arrival. They begin their La Liga campaign against Espanyol on August 22.

Sports.title: What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season
Sports.content:
What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season

Marcus Rashford is planning on holding talks with United boss Michael Carrick following the Red Devils friendly with Leeds United in Dublin on Wednesday night

View Image Marcus Rashford of Manchester United in action during a first team training session at Carton Hotel on August 10, 2026 in Dublin, Ireland. (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

Marcus Rashford is still keen to find an escape route from Manchester United. But Rashford might have to go abroad again - because his hopes of remaining in the Premier League look slim.

‌



Rashford has returned to pre-season training at Carrington following his summer break after the World Cup. He is planning to hold talks with manager Michael Carrick once the squad returns from its commitments in Dublin. But Rashford’s immediate future remains unclear and complicated.

‌



Co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe remains keen to get Rashford off the club’s wage bill. But he is not willing to sell the England forward to main rivals Arsenal, Liverpool or Manchester City.

‌



While loan deals with the likes of Chelsea, Aston Villa and Tottenham have been ruled out. Because if Rashford was to help any of these clubs finish in the Champions League places this coming season, it would prove embarrassing to United bosses.

9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

It’s understood Rashford would prefer to find a new club - and continue to revive his career elsewhere. He has the option of running down the remaining 24 months of his United deal, and leaving Old Trafford for nothing in 2028.

He could also use the next campaign to put himself in the shop window in the hope of securing a dream move in 2027 - assuming someone will pay.

‌



He believes there has been too much bad blood between him and his hometown club. And he knows there is still time in the summer window for him to negotiate a deal with someone else which suits him.

Rashford, 28, had been hoping to make his loan deal with Barcelona permanent, but the Spanish giants rejected the option to sign him for £24m, opting to sign Anthony Gordon instead.

United, meanwhile are considering opening talks with Club Brugge about a potential £30m deal for left back Joaquin Seys.

Article continues below

United have been priced out of a move for England and Newcastle defender Lewis Hall, and could turn their attentions to Seys instead.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute clown' and admits 'you might laugh'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute clown' and admits 'you might laugh'

Cristian Romero is set to leave Tottenham this summer and Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to hijack the transfer

View 2 Images Paul Scholes is a fan of Cristian Romero (Image: PA)

Paul Scholes believes Manchester United should try to hijack a move for Cristian Romero, whom he described as an 'absolute clown.' The Argentine, appointed captain only last year after signing a four‑year deal, is expected to leave Tottenham this summer, with Atletico Madrid currently in negotiations over his transfer.

‌



Fabrizio Romano reports that the deal between Spurs and Atletico is edging closer, though clubs are still a few million apart on the guaranteed fee and have yet to finalise the bonus structure. Atletico remain determined and are preparing a new offer.

‌



Inter Milan, Barcelona and Arsenal have also shown interest, but a sale to Spurs' north London rivals appears highly unlikely. Despite Romero favouring Atleti, Scholes believes United should attempt a late hijack, arguing that adding a top‑level centre‑back alongside Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire would be crucial as they prepare for a demanding season across all competitions.

‌



Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

"This is one you might laugh at," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast. "[United should sign] Cristian Romero from Tottenham. I know it might sound stupid, but I just think... I like him. I think he's a nutcase.

"He's a very good defender that does some stupid things. He is an absolute clown. But I think if someone could get hold of him, like Michael Carrick, who is very calm and relaxed, he might be able to [help him]. He seems like a bit of a cult hero defender, really. I know it might sound strange, but I think the fans at Old Trafford would like him."

Scholes added: "There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him....and he's cheap, £30-40million.

‌



"I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing]. You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You'd like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

View 2 Images Paul Scholes would like to see Romero at Man United

"Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They've got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he's still going to make mistakes. He's young. Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league]."

‌



Romero previously came close to leaving Spurs, most notably after Ange Postecoglou's departure. Roberto De Zerbi has since made it clear that he would respect Romero's wish to move on from north London.

"At the beginning of my time, in April, I had, I don't know, one million individual meetings!" he said. "And [the players] told me what was their idea. I said: 'Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave'. If you don't help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me!"

"But Romero with me was unbelievable. Top. In his behaviour, his respect, he suffered when he did not play the last game. It is not true that he wanted to leave for Argentina to prepare for their World Cup. It's not true."

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

De Zerbi added: "After the semi-final [against England] we text a message, but I never called him to convince him to stay. I respected what he told me. Like for Vicario, like for every player. Romero as a player is one of the best centre-backs in the world, but at the end I said I want to respect the will of the players."

United have already added three new faces to Michael Carrick's squad - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow. With the window running until 1 September, there's still time for another defensive signing, and Bologna centre‑back Jhon Lucumi is one of the names in the frame.

Article continues below

The Colombia international, who featured at the World Cup, is said to be keen on joining a 'big club' this summer. Bologna want £21.4m (€25m) plus £2.6m (€3m) in bonuses, and United are considering whether to match the asking price.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer

Arsenal could have Newcastle United to thank for a summer transfer boost days after raiding St James' Park to sign Bruno Guimaraes

View 2 Images Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United for £75m but could recoup millions (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal could be set to recoup some of the £75m transfer fee they paid for Bruno Guimaraes just days later, thanks to a shrewd transfer clause included as part of Joe Willock's switch to Newcastle United. The Gunners negotiated a sell-on clause with the Magpies when Willock moved to St. James' Park back in 2021.

‌



The 26-year-old left the Emirates Stadium in a deal valued at £25million after an impressive loan spell with the Magpies, but his five-year stay in the North East may be coming to an end. Willock is now believed to be close to a £17.4m move to Turkish Super Lig outfit Besiktas, with Newcastle having turned down a £10m bid earlier this summer.

‌



Our sister title ChronicleLive reports Willock's representatives have travelled to Turkey to negotiate a move with Besiktas, reportedly reaching agreement on personal terms. The former Arsenal midfielder is entering the final 12 months of his contract at St. James' Park and Newcastle are keen to recoup a fee.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

That's positive news for the Gunners, who secured a sell-on clause rumoured to be around 20 per cent, though the precise percentage remains undisclosed. Arsenal spent £75m to take Guimaraes to north London and could bank millions from Willock's prospective move, recouping some of the money paid for the Brazilian.

Gunners fans got a first glimpse of the new midfield addition ahead of the Emirates Cup clash with Borussia Dortmund at the weekend. As for his former Magpies teammate, Willock has featured 168 times for Newcastle, netting 11 goals since his departure from the Gunners.

‌



He broke into the Arsenal first team in 2017 and memorably scored on his Premier League debut against Newcastle in April 2018. Willock racked up 78 appearances and registered 11 goals during four campaigns at the club.

View 2 Images Willock found a new home in the north east (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

The clause now ensures Mikel Arteta's side will profit financially. Arsenal are looking to bolster their squad ahead of their Premier League title defence, having already brought in Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Guimaraes.

‌



The additional funds will provide a welcome boost in their bid to secure further signings this summer, with the Gunners actively seeking a new left-winger.

Arsenal had been linked with moves for Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, however Chelsea swooped in to snap up the England international, while Real Madrid tied down the Brazilian star to fresh terms.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup fixture chaos as Chelsea embroiled in crazy eight-game domino effect

Chelsea will take on Luton Town at Stamford Bridge in the second round of the Carabao Cup as Premier League clubs enter the competition

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso's Chelsea will take on Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup. (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

There could be a major fixture list shift following the second round Carabao Cup draw. The Premier League kicks off in just under two weeks, with Chelsea travelling to take on Fulham in the final fixture of the weekend on Monday, August 24 (8pm kick-off).

‌



The match is being played on the Monday night after being selected for live TV coverage on Sky Sports. But it is now set to impact a few other fixtures, with both Chelsea and Fulham in action in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

‌



Chelsea will face League One side Luton Town at Stamford Bridge on the week commencing August 24. Fulham, meanwhile, have been drawn at home against AFC Wimbledon.

‌



Jamie Vardy could be offered return to English football aged 39 after £15m bid rejected READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Typically, these matches are played on Tuesday or Wednesday evenings, but the Monday night clash between Chelsea and Fulham on the Premier League's opening weekend means that both fixtures are likely to be pushed back to Thursday, August 27.

With Chelsea's fixture against Brighton, and Fulham's clash against Sunderland the following weekend already confirmed for Sunday, this shouldn't present any issues. There is, however, another potential complication for schedulers to navigate.

‌



Policing constraints typically prevent Chelsea and Fulham from hosting matches on the same day. This will either need changes to existing regulations, or an alternative solution will need to be found by the EFL.

While both Chelsea and Fulham don't return to action until the following Sunday, the same cannot be said for their respective opponents. Both Luton and AFC Wimbledon are scheduled to fulfil League One commitments against Mansfield Town (A) and Wigan Athletic (H) on the Saturday, less than 48 hours after the potential Thursday night fixture.

View 2 Images Jack Wilshere's Luton will take on Chelsea in the second round of the Carabao Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh/Getty Images)

‌



Clubs are generally granted a minimum of 72 hours' rest between fixtures, suggesting those matches are likely to be postponed by approximately 24 hours. Nevertheless, this will then create a domino effect on their midweek commitments.

All four sides are set to feature in league action on Tuesday, 1 September. Those encounters will consequently need to be rescheduled by 24 hours to the Wednesday evening to ensure the teams receive sufficient rest between the two fixtures, meaning up to eight games will need to be moved.

Sports.content:
Aston Villa's dream attack as Endrick joins Ollie Watkins and £95million duo

Aston Villa are set to have a new-look attack next season and have been linked with a high-profile move for Real Madrid forward Endrick

View 2 Images Aston Villa have been linked with a move for Endrick (Image: Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Aston Villa have been linked with a shock move for Real Madrid star Endrick as Unai Emery continues to reshape his squad. The Villans have previously had a stable side but selling Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers means that fans will be watching a new-look team next season.

‌



Villa capped off their Europa League victory by finishing fourth in the league last term, though success also led clubs to target their key players. The further sale of left-back Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain, plus Amadou Onana sustaining an injury at the World Cup, has forced Villa into a reshuffle.

‌



Joao Gomes is expected to partner Boubacar Kamara in midfield after his £35m move from Wolves. In attack, Villa fans already have reasons to be hopeful after signing Johan Manzambi, who starred for Switzerland at the World Cup, as Rogers’ replacement from Freiburg for an initial £52m. Meanwhile, Emery will be determined to help Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho fulfil his potential.

‌



Villa supporters’ pre-season excitement has been ramped up by the club reportedly expressing interest in a loan move for Endrick, as the Real Madrid forward searches for regular minutes. Here is a look at how Villa’s attack could line up, in the dream scenario that the Brazilian does arrive at Villa Park.

Spanish publication AS reports that the 20-year-old is listening to loan offers after finding himself down the pecking order at Los Blancos, both as a wide option and a centre-forward.

‌



Endrick flourished as a winger during his recent Lyon loan spell, scoring eight goals and providing eight assists in 21 games. While his versatility could offer Emery another option up front, the Madrid star will also face fierce competition for his spot on the wing from club captain John McGinn. Whether at Endrick’s expense or otherwise, few would bet against the skipper quickly forcing his way back into the team.

Johan Manzambi will take up the mantle of replacing Rogers, who joined Chelsea for an eye-watering £117m, in the attacking midfield role. The Switzerland international, who is currently out injured, faced many of his new team-mates in the Europa League final.

Sports.title: Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours
Sports.content:
Forgotten ex-Man Utd star reveals Bruno Fernandes gesture that shows his true colours

Bruno Fernandes has been a key player for Manchester United since joining the club in 2020 and a former team-mate has spoken about a classy gesture

View 3 Images Brandon Williams says ex-Manchester United colleague Bruno Fernandes still checks up on him (Image: Getty)

Brandon Williams says former Manchester United team-mate Bruno Fernandes still messages him and helps him get match tickets. Williams is currently without a club after leaving Hull City in February.

Since 2023, Fernandes has been United's skipper and for all intents and purposes, the face of the club. But it's not just on the field where he is influential.

Defender Williams, who joined the club's academy ranks at the age of seven, left United in 2024 after the expiration of his contract and has faced legal trouble in the years since. But the 25-year-old is still in contact with some of his former team-mates at Old Trafford and Fernandes in particular showed his class with a kind act.

Williams told The Athletic how Fernandes still keeps in touch with him and arranges match tickets. He said: "That's why he's the captain, he's an unreal guy."

The left-back is presently a free agent. He worked his way through United's youth set-up before making his senior debut in 2019. That season, with Luke Shaw and Ashley Young battling fitness problems, he secured meaningful minutes and penned a fresh four-year contract in 2020.

A loan switch to Norwich City in 2021 was followed by another temporary stint with Ipswich Town. While he failed to truly shine during these spells, his career trajectory shifted in 2023.

View 3 Images Williams played 51 times for United (Image: Getty)

Williams was charged and subsequently found guilty of dangerous driving and driving without third-party insurance following a traffic collision on the A34 near Wilmslow/Handforth.

Eyewitnesses described seeing him drive recklessly, tailgating, braking sharply and holding a balloon to his mouth, although prosecutors emphasised there was no proof he was legally impaired. He lost control and smashed into a Ford Fiesta at around 74mph before careering into the central reservation.

He originally denied the charges but admitted guilt in March 2025 and was sentenced in May to 14 months' imprisonment, suspended for two years, a three-year driving ban and an unpaid community work order of 180 hours. As Williams tries to rebuild his career, he claims that if he still fancies going to watch his boyhood club, Fernandes can lend a hand.

Williams revealed that he also remains in touch with fellow former team-mates Marcus Rashford and Harry Maguire. His United contract ran out in 2024 and following a short break, he penned a one-year deal with Hull last year.

View 3 Images The defender committed the offences whilst on loan with Ipswich (Image: Getty)

Having been without a club since February, Williams has been training with League Two outfit Rotherham but remains uncertain whether he'll land a contract. Looking back on his career, he added: "I've only just started to look back and be like, 'I actually did something.' I actually played for United 51 times. It's something to be proud of.

"My nan is on at me because she's got a frame where it's me playing at 18, 19, 20 and 21. Every time I go and see her, she points at it and says, 'I want you to be doing that again.' That's my motivation.

"I know it's not going to be a quick process, I know I'm not going to be in the Premier League next year. I'm ready to climb the mountain and get back to the top of it."

Sports.title: Trump warns of 'terrible mistake' if FIFA replaces Infantino
Sports.content:
US President Donald Trump has warned FIFA would be making a "terrible mistake" if it got rid of Gianni Infantino as head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men's World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the FIFA president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: "FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20 per cent to private investors.

But UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC hit out at "deception" and a "fundamental breach of trust" around Infantino's botched plan, the three continental associations each signing a new open letter to the "football family" on Monday, without naming Infantino specifically but referring to a leader who "abandoned their duty" by breaking trust "through deception".

In the three-page document they again criticised the president's World Cup sale plans and rejected FIFA's claim that they had been a "mistake", adding: "There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment - not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol on whether Infantino can continue as the president of FIFA

UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC had been the three confederations to reject Infantino's plan before it was scrapped, while UEFA went further and announced a boycott of FIFA competitions - and last week confirmed the threat remained while Infantino is still in post.

The associations also hit out at the manner of a FIFA management committee meeting held in Morocco last Wednesday - a meeting which ended with a statement publicly backing Infantino - for not instead addressing FIFA's wider senior leadership at its base in Switzerland.

"It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him," the letter read. "There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness."

US Soccer and Canada Soccer - two of the three federations which hosted the World Cup - also called for meaningful change.

A US Soccer statement read: "US Soccer, Canada Soccer, CFU (Caribbean Football Union) and UNCAF (Central American Football Union) stand together, along with our colleagues around the world, in calling for meaningful change that strengthens FIFA's governance, transparency and accountability."

The UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC letter came around 24 hours after FIFA itself had hit out at "a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine" the governing body and president Infantino over claims surrounding his conduct at UEFA.

UEFA confirmed on Saturday a "departure payment" was made to a female employee alleged to have been in a relationship with Infantino when he was the European organisation's general secretary.

The Daily Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum and UEFA confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, adding it was "in line" with regulations at the time.

The allegations intensified the position of Infantino, who worked at UEFA for 16 years and was its general secretary between 2009 and 2016 before being elected FIFA president, following his aborted plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Image: FIFA president Infantino

While not directly referencing UEFA's statement, FIFA accused Infantino's critics of trying to weaken his authority and have him removed from his role without a due re-election process.

A statement said: "It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its president.

"Those who do not have the support of FIFA's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through FIFA's established democratic processes.

"Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning FIFA and its president. Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

"The FIFA president has dedicated more than 30 years of his professional life to European and world football, contributing to significant change in the game and, in particular, to broadening access, resources and opportunity across world football

"Change inevitably challenges established interests, but disagreement with that change cannot justify efforts to undermine the democratic mandate of FIFA's president or the institution he was elected to lead.

"FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, FIFA will challenge it directly and vigorously.

"FIFA's responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global. Through the FIFA president and the FIFA administration, our focus remains firmly on that mission, and we are more determined than ever to fulfil it."

Sports.title: Refreshed Rory returns for FedExCup Playoffs as he targets fourth title
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy returns to action at the FedEx St. Jude Championship this week, live on Sky Sports, with the world No 2 targeting a big finish to the PGA Tour season and a record-extending fourth FedExCup title.

McIlroy heads into the first of three FedExCup Playoffs 12th in the season-long standings, with only the top 50 after this week progressing to the BMW Championship and then the top 30 qualifying for the season-ending Tour Championship.

The back-to-back Masters champion skipped last year's FedEx St Jude Championship but is part of this year's 69-man field at TPC Southwind in Memphis, where world No 1 Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Justin Rose also feature.

FedExCup Playoffs schedule All tournaments live on Sky Sports August 13-16: FedEx St. Jude Championship (TPC Southwind, Memphis, Tennessee) August 20-23: BMW Championship, (Bellerive Country Club, St. Louis, Missouri) August 27-30: Tour Championship (East Lake Golf Club, Atlanta, Georgia)

McIlroy has only played six events - and three outside of the majors - since successfully defending his Masters title in April, claiming tied-19th at the Truist Championship, tied-12th at The Memorial and a share of seventh at the Genesis Scottish Open.

But Brad Faxon, McIlroy's putting mentor, told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast that the 37-year-old has earned the right to cherry-pick his tournaments.

Faxon said: "After back-to-back Masters titles, he is like, 'not only financially can I afford to do this but mentally, too'.

"Rory is not physically tired after playing a round of golf but it is the mental fatigue of always being on, always in the spotlight, never getting a break. Whether it's walking into the gates or going to dinner at night, somebody is always coming up to you.

Image: McIlroy is a three-time FedExCup champion

"I have never seen anybody more patient in that situation than Rory but for him to go to the Greek islands with some of his closest friends, that's a way to get away from the game.

"When Rory said to his daughter, 'Poppy, I need to go and practise. Her great quote was, 'you already know how to play, daddy'. Rory hasn't forgotten how to play and had a pretty good track record in the playoffs.

"In the brutal summer months that you get in the south, you are going to have to be in very good physical shape these next few weeks to contend for the FedExCup."

How do the FedExCup Playoffs work?

Image: World No 1 Scottie Scheffler heads the FedExCup standings, ahead of Mathew Fitzpatrick, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark and Chris Gotterup

All season long, players have earned points based on how they have performed in PGA Tour events, with extra points available for the signature events and majors.

Only the top 70 in the standings have reached the FedEx St Jude Championship (August 13-16), with just the top 50 then progressing to the BMW Championship (August 20-23) and then only the top 30 making it to the finale, The Tour Championship (August 27-30).

Winners of the first two play-off events earn 750 points apiece - the same as The Players and the majors - before the points reset to zero ahead of the Tour Championship.

In the closing event, all players begin at even par with the starting-strokes model based on FedExCup placings at that point axed in 2025.

The winner of the Tour Championship becomes FedExCup champion for 2026, earning $10m (£7.4m) dollars and a five-year PGA Tour exemption.

What else is at stake?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Brennan wrapped up a FedExCup Playoffs spot with victory at the Wyndham Championship on Sunday

Those who have qualified for the FedEx St Jude Championship are guaranteed to retain their PGA Tour card for 2027 and also clinch a spot at The Players, while the 50 to make the BMW Championship earn places in next term's signature events.

For the 30 who make it to the Tour Championship, they can look forward to a two-year PGA Tour exemption and teeing it up at the Masters at Augusta National. Spots in the US Open and Open are also set to come their way.

Why you should keep an eye on Koivun

After winning the 3M Open in just his third start as a pro after staying cool amid a charge from Scheffler, Jackson Koivin, 21, went on to wrap up a FedExCup Playoff spot after just five events, matching Tiger Woods' record.

Faxon added of the hot prospect, who he says would be great fit for USA at the away Ryder Cup in Ireland next September: "Koivun dominated college and he is the hardest working kid I have ever seen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jackson Koivun, 21, won the 3M Open a few weeks ago

"He comes blessed with a great putting stroke and a great putting attitude.

"I spend a lot of my time at the Titleist Performance Institute, where you can do all the testing of your equipment. I first met Jackson there and talked about his game.

"Every single guy who did the club fitting and ball fitting, was saying, 'nobody is close to what this guy is doing'. We have seen how good he hits the iron as well so I am excited for him.

"I am a long-term believer in Jackson Koivun."

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest sign defender Diomande in £34m deal
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have signed Ivory Coast defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting on a four-year deal.

Forest will pay a fixed fee of around £34.3m (€40m) for the 22-year-old centre-back after weeks of negotiations.

Head coach Oliver Glasner drove the club's interest in Diomande after trying to sign him at his former side Crystal Palace.

Diomande has spent the last four seasons at Sporting, playing 132 times, scoring seven goals and winning the Primeira Liga twice.

He helped Sporting reach the Champions League knockout stages and win a domestic double in the 2024/25 season, while being part of the Ivory Coast squad that won the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations for the first time in eight years.

Diomande has earned 15 caps for his country and made one appearance at this summer's World Cup.

On signing for Forest, Diomande said: "I am very happy to be here. It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

"I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season."

Chief football officer George Syrianos added: "We have been very clear on the profile of player we want to add to the squad, so we are excited to welcome Ousmane to the club.

"He has fantastic experience for a defender of his age. Playing a crucial role in title-winning teams and going into the latter stages of the Champions League puts him in a great position to integrate well here at Forest.

"Ousmane is a powerful, commanding defender, and arrives here with a winning mentality. He shares the same ambition for success we have, and we are excited to see the impact he can have in a Forest shirt."

Sports.title: How concerned should Liverpool be after another pre-season collapse?
Sports.content:
How much does pre-season mean? It depends who you ask.

Fans itching for the return of football after a summer forced into other past-times are left yearning to see new players in action and the tangible feel of momentum building ahead of the new season.

But at Anfield, that pre-season buzz has come to a crunching halt both on and off the pitch.

There is no empirical formula to the importance of pre-season results. Take last summer when Arsenal were beaten by Thomas Frank's Tottenham in Hong Kong and lost at home to Villarreal in their penultimate friendly.

Within nine months, Frank was out of a job and they were crowned Premier League champions and were a penalty shoot-out away from winning the Champions League.

By that logic, Liverpool's back-to-back two-goal collapses to Leeds and Monaco can be waved away. And there are positives for Andoni Iraola, with Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - who endured testing first seasons on Merseyside - flourishing in pre-season. Both were on the scoresheet against Monaco on Sunday.

But there is a wider context growing and concerns already sufficient for the new head coach to publicly highlight with less than two weeks left before their season opener with Newcastle, live on Sky Sports on August 23.

Newcastle United

Liverpool Sunday 23rd August 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

What those collapses do achieve is to shine a light on one of Liverpool's most pressing concerns - fitness.

No side in the Premier League completed more sprints than Iraola's Bournemouth last season and the high-pressing, physically intense football he demands is well-established.

Those requirements are perhaps even more keenly felt by a Liverpool squad which attempted the third-fewest pressures and second-fewest opposition-half high pressures last season.

Of course the club are, more generally, well-used to pressing football under Jurgen Klopp and many of his former players remain at Anfield. But this u-turn from his successor Arne Slot has a long way to go to be completely unpicked mentally and, more crucially, physically with the season less than a fortnight away.

After Monaco, Iraola made the stark admission his players may only have the capacity to implement his methods for as little as half an hour at a time at present. "We played well in the first half, especially the first 30 minutes, but right now probably we don't have much more in terms of the level required to play like this," he told club channels after the game.

It said as much about his players' game time. Liverpool's rivals are beginning to prioritise match cohesion over squad rotation, and Manchester City, Arsenal and Aston Villa - all fellow Champions League qualifiers - each left five or more outfield starters on for at least 75 minutes in their respective friendlies last weekend. Just three of Liverpool's managed even an hour.

Even looking at Liverpool's opening opponents, Newcastle gave six players at least 67 minutes against Valencia on Saturday, even with the enforced first-half withdrawal of Jacob Murphy due to injury.

The majority of the Reds' line-up on Sunday could conceivably begin the season opener at St James' Park, and it was those starters who raced into a 2-0 lead against Monaco and showed glimpses of what Iraola is trying to build.

But with Liverpool playing catch-up on their rivals' fitness, the importance of squad depth will only become heightened - and here the head coach is instead presented with compounding issues.

While Chelsea's depth allowed them to call on Nicolas Jackson, Geovany Quenda and Estevao from the bench to beat AC Milan 3-0 on Saturday, Liverpool were left with a centre-back pairing of Wataru Endo and Luke Chambers, who spent last season on loan at Charlton, for most of the second half against Monaco 24 hours later.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the pre-season friendly match between Liverpool and Monaco

Victor Munoz and Milos Kerkez aside - both likely starters against Newcastle - Liverpool's eight second-half additions managed just eight top-flight starts between them last season, and five of those came from 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha alone.

Iraola is not blind to his thin squad and within weeks of his appointment was already throwing down the gauntlet to the club that further reinforcements were needed, but it has not proven the catalyst he hoped.

He would have liked to avoid the departure of Michael Edwards last month and continuing rumours over Richard Hughes' future, but that will provide little excuse if the season gets off to a slow start.

The surprise arrival of Ronald Araujo is more helpful but even with him on board Liverpool still only have two fit senior centre-backs. Conor Bradley remains "months" away from a return according to Iraola. It is perhaps a relief that at least Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez are both fit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool's new signing Ronald Araujo says he had no doubts about joining the club from Barcelona on loan with an option to buy

Further forward Liverpool need more than Victor Munoz to replace Mo Salah while Cody Gakpo is of interest to Tottenham and Curtis Jones sat out Sunday's defeat entirely with Inter Milan still hopeful of signing the England midfielder.

After spending comfortably in excess of £400m last summer - even ignoring outgoings, still a gargantuan sum - it is reasonable to feel that Liverpool should not still find themselves short in multiple positions.

Not all of those are self-inflicted, and the issues at centre-back in particular owe more to an unfortunate succession of injuries to Jeremy Jacquet, Giovanni Leoni and now Joe Gomez than poor planning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charlie Austin believes that Liverpool need 'four or five' signings to add to their squad depth ahead of the season where 'top four is the bare minimum'

But with only Alexis Mac Allister to return from World Cup duty, if pre-season is serving Iraola any purpose it is to expose the holes in his squad. Those are most obvious both in wide-forward areas and midfield and time is running out to address them - especially if further outgoings do follow.

Few expect a repeat performance of Slot's debut season or the Premier League trophy to be anywhere near Anfield come the end of next May.

But exactly how far off Liverpool will be, and how successfully Iraola can implement his style, will owe a lot to the comings and goings at Anfield in the three short weeks remaining of the transfer window.

Sports.title: England's World Cup place guaranteed but West Indies need to qualify
Sports.content:
Panic over, England fans - your team will NOT have to qualify for the 2027 Cricket World Cup.

England's drop-off in 50-over cricket had seen them plummet down the rankings and leave them at risk of missing out on automatic entry into next autumn's event in Africa.

However, the rot was stopped with successive come-from-behind series wins - over Sri Lanka earlier this year and then at home to India in July - leaving Harry Brook's men inside the required top eight in the rankings ahead of the September 30 cut-off.

Zimbabwe are in, too, as they are another of the competition's co-hosts.

India, New Zealand, Australia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan - who secured their place with victory over Ireland - are the other guaranteed entrants.

That means two-time champions West Indies, ranked 10th, will have to take part in the qualifying event for the third successive 50-over World Cup.

West Indies - World Cup winners in 1975 and 1979 - successfully reached the 2019 edition in England but then lost in qualifying for the 2023 showpiece in India.

The Caribbean side still have two more ODIs, in India, before September 30 but even if they win those two matches, they cannot move into the top nine in the rankings.

Image: Scotland will be in the qualifying tournament next year

West Indies are now headed for the qualifier in February and March, alongside Ireland, Netherlands, Scotland, USA and five yet-to-be-determined teams.

Under ​a new format for 2027, the ​winner of the qualifier will advance directly ​to the second stage of the World ⁠Cup, while the teams placing second, third and fourth will feature in the first round known ⁠as the Super Series.

That late switch was criticised in a joint statement from the Scottish and Dutch cricket boards, who accused the ICC of "weakening the integrity and credibility of international cricket."

Sky Sports News has contacted the ICC for comment.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brentford
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 8th (NB: this is not necessarily John Brewin’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 9th

Prospects

If the upward trajectory of the Brentford project continued last season, with Keith Andrews proving a capable replacement for Thomas Frank, it ended with disappointment. On the final day, there was a chance of European football for this season, only for a draw at Anfield to deny the club the opportunity to capitalise on Brighton’s loss to Manchester United, an inferior goal difference meaning they finished ninth rather than eighth. A win would have secured a place in the Europa League. Dango Ouattara’s late headed miss will have been relived many times over the summer.

Perhaps the lack of European football may prove a blessing. Smaller clubs being stretched by a heavier schedule is a story often told, both in physical and financial terms, but the continental football dream will not be far from minds if Brentford’s progress sustains. The loss of Jordan Henderson to Chelsea’s new senior citizens’ collective will be felt more in terms of his leadership qualities than his playing influence; he started 22 matches last season in a midfield where a more youthful energy was preferred.

Can Igor Thiago replicate last season? He did enough to win a World Cup selection for Brazil, but hit flat spots even while making such an impression; he scored once in his team’s final six matches, just when they might have needed him most. He will be supported this season by the experience of Callum Wilson, signed as a free agent, while Jaidon Anthony has joined the forward line from Burnley.

Continuity remains a key tenet, building on the foundations laid by the owner, Matthew Benham, and the long-serving sporting director, Phil Giles, that made and sustained Brentford as a top-division club. Each season of the club’s five in the Premier League has seen peaks and troughs ridden out and further progress made. That has to be the coming season’s expectation.

Off-field picture

The published accounts for 2024-25, Frank’s last in charge, showed a £21m loss that was significant, but relatively small potatoes compared to Premier League peers. The sales of Bryan Mbeumo and Yoane Wissa eased finances last summer, but extra revenue streams are being sought. A public consultation is being carried out in view of hosting six live music events at the Gtech. The stadium is built in a residential area, apartment blocks towering over the stands. A sleeve sponsorship deal was renewed with Cazoo, the west London automobile e-commerce dealership. Indeed, the job website, has replaced the previous, South African betting company that adorned the shirts as the main sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Just like his former associate Tony Bloom at Brighton, Benham has provided the analytical expertise and the finance to sustain Brentford’s development. For that, fans who grew up as supporters of one of the capital’s smallest clubs, and those who have been attracted more recently, will be for ever grateful. After last year’s arrival of Gary Lubner and Sir Matthew Vaughn as minority shareholders, Prakash Melwani, investment banker, and Sir Lucian Grainge, music mogul, took similar slices of the pie. A formerly parochial club, one still close to its grassroots support, is now helmed by big-hitters from the business world.

The manager

Andrews showed he is far more than the set-piece specialist he was previously employed as. For the difficult second album, he will be aware that opposing managers and their scouts will be better prepared. An adept media performer, he has explained the relative lack of business with typical calm. “We won’t sign players unless we feel they’ll fit into the fabric of the club and the culture and values that we have as a group of people working together on a daily basis,” he said from a pre-season training camp in Portugal. Having confounded doubts as the rookie manager who ended last season with claims on end-of-season awards he now has to prove it was not beginners’ luck.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen New signing Mamadou Sangaré warming up before Brentford’s 4-2 pre-season friendly victory against Rennes. Photograph: Lucas Bronchart/Icon Sport/Getty Images

When Lens went close to denying Paris Saint-Germain the Ligue 1 title last season, Mamadou Sangaré was at the heart of their midfield. He was named in the division’s team of the season. Brentford’s midfield has lost Henderson and Christian Nørgaard over the last two summers, though Sangaré will offer different strengths. Opta stats from last season showed only Elliot Anderson and Bayer Leverkusen’s Exequiel Palacios averaged more possession regains in Europe’s top five leagues. Brentford are at their best and most effective when pressing hard and high and Sangaré appears ideal. “He adds qualities that we don’t have,” said Andrews of the club-record £35m signing.

Stat attack

Brentford scored 10 set-play goals last season – it was their joint-fewest in a Premier League campaign and only three teams in the division had a worse record. Yet no club in the division was more reliant upon free-kicks, corners and throw-ins to generate shots. They either need to be more productive in open play or more efficient with their set pieces. Both wouldn’t go amiss.

Set for a breakthrough

To follow Thiago’s successful signing from Belgium, Kaye Furo was bought from Club Brugge in January. Making his debut as Macclesfield were negotiated in the FA Cup in February, he made one Premier League appearance, in May against West Ham. As has been customary at Brentford for new additions, he may have to wait for his turn, particularly with those experienced additions to the forward line. Brentford’s first-mover advantage via analytics and scouting remains widely admired and has delivered more hits than misses to help finance further dealings. Kaye is the son of Furo Iyenemi, who captained Nigeria at the 2000 Olympics.

World Cup impact

The now-departed Henderson played a patrician role within the England squad. Kristoffer Ajer, whose Norway team were beaten in the quarter-finals by England, travelled furthest in the tournament of those who remain. Ajer’s header hit the crossbar in those frantic final moments in Atlanta. To get there, Norway pulled off an historic victory over Brazil, where Thiago was an unused substitute, having made his single, ineffective appearance in the opening 1-1 draw with Morocco. Aaron Hickey’s participation was just as brief, confined to Scotland’s grinding opening win over Haiti before succumbing to injury, unable to contribute as the campaign lurched into familiar disappointment.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Manchester United as left-back solution
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Manchester United as a potential left-back option, with Arsenal wishing to recoup some of the £75m paid to Newcastle for Bruno Guimarães.

Chelsea, it is understood, have also been made aware of the availability of the 19-year-old, who won the Premier League under Mikel Arteta last term. Whether the west London club will make a move for Lewis-Skelly is unclear.

Lewis-Skelly, who made only five league starts and a total of 36 appearances in all competitions in 2025-26, signed a five-year contract last summer. His prospective price is thought to be in the region of £45m.

This is within the range of finance United have so far spent this summer, following Youri Tielemans’s £35m move from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos’s arrival for £48m plus £2m of add-ons from Chelsea.

Newcastle’s Lewis Hall remains of prime interest for United but after losing Guimarães, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham, and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, the new Newcastle manager, Matthias Jaissle, is intent the 21-year-old England international does not also depart

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Nottingham Forest seal £34m deal for Sporting’s Diomande
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have signed Côte d’Ivoire defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for an undisclosed fee, reported to be £34.2m.

The 22-year-old centre-half, who featured in the Côte d’Ivoire’s World Cup squad, has agreed a four-year deal with Forest, who have an option for a further year.

Forest’s chief football officer, George Syrianos, said: “He has fantastic experience for a defender of his age. Playing a crucial role in title winning teams and going into the latter stages of the Champions League puts him in a great position to integrate well here at Forest.”

Diomande began his professional career in Denmark with FC Midtjylland and after joining Sporting in January 2023 he made 132 appearances for the Portuguese club in all competitions.

He played a key role in Sporting’s run in the Champions League last season, starting both legs in their quarter-final defeat by Arsenal, and also played the full 90 minutes in Côte d’Ivoire’s World Cup group win against Curaçao.

Fulham have signed midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton for a reported £30m fee, which would be a record deal for a Northern Ireland international. Charles, 22, has agreed a five-year contract, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

“It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager [Alvaro Arbeloa] explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege,” Charles said. “I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.”

Filip Jorgensen has joined Strasbourg on a season-long loan from Chelsea. The 24-year-old goalkeeper arrived at Stamford Bridge in 2024 from Villarreal and has made 36 appearances for the Blues.

Jorgensen started all but one of Chelsea’s games in the Conference League last year and featured 12 times in all competitions. He will now spend the 2026-27 campaign with Strasbourg, who finished eighth in Ligue 1 last season.

Sports.title: League Two 2026-27 preview: the contenders, hopefuls and strugglers
Sports.content:
Contenders

Salford meekly lost the playoff final and that was the end of days for Karl Robinson as he was sacked. Peter Cklamovski was not the obvious replacement, but the Australian left behind the Malaysia national side for a crack at League Two with the rebranded Ammies, who are back in their traditional orange. Macaulay Langstaff has arrived with the task of providing the goals to finally get Salford up and few would bet against the striker.

Chesterfield fell short in the playoffs, too, but Paul Cook remains one of the best managers at this level, although the loss of Armando Dobra could be significant. Securing the veteran forward Andy Cook was important for Grimsby as they seek to push on and his influence could be telling if he plays enough games. Lee Grant did not get much chance to prove himself at Huddersfield so will be desperate to do so at Walsall, especially after a promising start by knocking Championship side Bristol City out of the EFL Cup. The former goalkeeper will be hoping he is the man to ensure the Saddlers do not stop playing in winter, as has been the case in recent years.

Of those who have dropped down, Rotherham are the more intriguing bet, having brought in Steve McClaren as director of football and Alex Bruce as head coach in an attempt to revitalise the club. Losing Sam Nombe was a blow, but his transfer fee should allow investment. Jon Brady knows what he is doing and could do nothing to keep Port Vale up, but arguably has the most complete squad at this level with Max Watters and Kyle Dempsey standout summer signings.

View image in fullscreen Rotherham will hope to utilise the experience of their director of football Steve McClaren to bolster their chances of promotion into League One. Photograph: WhiteRosePhotos/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Hopefuls

An end‑of‑season slump kept Crewe out of the playoffs last time round, but the returns of Luke Offord and Joe White provide much‑needed quality. Barnet were two points off eighth having returned to the EFL and have kept their developing squad together – apart from Ryan Glover who was sold to Stockport – to give Dean Brennan real belief that his side can improve. Oldham made a steady return to the fourth tier and have added the guarantee of Elliott Nevitt’s goals alongside Oliver Norburn, who was a key member of the Notts County side that went up from this division.

Colin Kazim-Richards has his feet fully under the table at Crawley and has overseen one of their traditional busy summers in an attempt to avoid a relegation battle. The former Sunderland goalkeeper Vito Mannone was an eye‑catching signing, while the talented Malcolm Ebiowei will be aiming to turn his career around. If these two shine, it could make them a surprise package. Relegation and problems off the pitch have put Exeter on a downward spiral, which does not look like being arrested without further incomings. “Absolute tinpot garbage” was Ian Holloway’s view of Swindon’s friendly performance against Bristol City, which suggests the team still have levels to go. Gareth Ainsworth wants high‑pressing Gillingham to maintain energy levels over the course of the campaign to give them an outside chance of challenging.

Quick Guide PFA takes EFL to high court over changes to salary cap rules in League One Show The Professional Footballers’ Association has begun high court proceedings against the English Football League over changes to the salary cap rules in League One. The division’s clubs approved changes to the existing Salary Cost Management Protocol (SCMP) rules in May, with “the aim of reducing losses and the reliance on owner funding in the division”. The changes reduced the amount League One clubs will be allowed to spend on wages from 60% to 50%, with manager salaries also now to be included in SCMP calculations. But the players’ union believes all parties within the Professional Football Negotiating and Consultative Committee (PFNCC) – the Premier League, EFL, PFA and the Football Association – were not properly consulted. A PFA spokesperson said: “The PFA have begun high court action against the EFL in relation to new wage restriction rules adopted by clubs in League One and introduced this season. “We believe that the process through which clubs have voted to bring in these new measures, which will artificially restrict and tighten what clubs can spend on player wages, was not in line with the consultation and agreement process required by the EFL’s membership (alongside the PFA, FA and Premier League) of the Professional Football Negotiating and Consultative Committee (PFNCC).” In response, the EFL said it is “concerned and disappointed at the position adopted by the PFA”. The EFL said: “The proposed changes have been discussed at length through the PFNCC process, including with the PFA, and the EFL has taken those discussions into account. “The PFA has argued that the league cannot implement the changes unless there is full agreement through the PFNCC. The league does not accept that the PFA’s position is correct.” The EFL added: “The EFL will continue to engage constructively with the PFA and other stakeholders. But it cannot ignore the financial pressures facing clubs or accept further delay when the risks to the game are increasing. Our priority is clear: a fair, competitive and financially sustainable league system that protects clubs, players, supporters and communities over the long term.” Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

George Burley’s son-in-law Chris Hogg joined Northampton in May for his first managerial role and, after sunning himself in Greece, is primed to test himself, but the Cobblers may rue the departure of Cameron McGeehan as they aim to rebuild after relegation. Gavin Cowan transformed Shrewsbury from no-hopers to comfortably staying up but he faces a tricky second album.

John Terry is not the Colchester owner, as the sale of the club rumbles on without a solution. Steve Evans will ensure Bristol Rovers are competitive, but whether that means they can push themselves higher than 14th place last season remains to be seen.

Strugglers

The promoted teams start on the backfoot after managerial changes, as Rochdale lost Jimmy McNulty, while York decided to sack Stuart Maynard midway through preseason, much to the consternation of the fans. Diligence in recruitment, however, gives them optimism, especially Dale bringing back Cian Hayes.

Tranmere survived by a couple of points last time round but will be hoping for an uplift under Darrell Clarke, who has persuaded Will Vaulks and the former Watford winger Tom Ince that Prenton Park is a sensible place to continue their careers. Newport County were also forced into a change in the dugout when Christian Fuchs decided Rodney Parade was not the place he wanted to call home having kept the team up, leaving the club in flux as Chris Todd oversaw preparations for the campaign. The Exiles brought in plenty of experience in the shape of Harrison Biggins and Christian Doidge to strengthen the squad.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The inexperienced Matt Lawlor is set for a challenging first full season in charge of Fleetwood, who are boosted by the signing of Andy Cannon from Wrexham. Steve Cotterill revitalised Cheltenham almost a year ago, but five of their first six summer signings were relegated in May, which does not inspire confidence. After finishing comfortably in midtable, Accrington Stanley may not fear the drop and Cole Stockton is a clever signing but there is a nagging doubt about the club’s efficacy.

View image in fullscreen Managerial inexperience may prove challenging for Matt Lawlor (left) who has much to prove in his first full season at Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Phil Oldham/Shutterstock

Ones to watch

Maldini Kacurri, Grimsby, 20 After starting last season on loan at doomed National League side Morecambe, the Albania international may have wondered if life outside Arsenal was really for him. The defender shone when he stepped up to League Two with Grimsby, guided by David Artell, proving himself capable of coping with the physicality in the lower tiers.

Patrick Mlynarski, Crewe, 18 A Wales youth international, the recently-turned 18-year-old is now in his first year as a professional. The winger made his debut in the EFL Trophy last season, but is yet to feature in the league. Previously part of Everton’s academy, Mylnarski is skilful and powerful, playing on the left, possessing the ability to cut in or beat defenders on the outside.

Will Gray, Shrewsbury, 17 The midfielder made four starts last season and signed his first professional contract in the summer. His manager, Gavin Cowan, has praised his mentality and ability to keep things simple in the centre of the park.

Sports.title: Chelsea face Real Sociedad in WCL third qualifying round with riches at stake
Sports.content:
Chelsea will face Real Sociedad in the Women’s Champions League’s third qualifying round, needing a victory over two legs to earn a place in the main league phase of the competition.

The 2021 runners-up and six-time European semi-finalists are taking part in the qualifying stage by virtue of their disappointing third-placed finish in the Women’s Super League last term – their lowest league finish since 2019 – and they will be the favourites against the Spanish side.

Chelsea could have faced Ajax, Inter, Eintracht Frankfurt or the Austrian side St Polten. They were unable to meet the big-name sides such as Real Madrid, Wolfsburg, Juventus or Paris Saint-Germain at this stage because of seedings. Sonia Bompastor’s side will hope to join Arsenal and Manchester City in the main phase of the competition.

The potential financial implications of missing out on qualification are significant. All 18 clubs that take part in the league phase will receive a guaranteed minimum of €505,000, plus a further €60,000 for every league phase fixture they win and €20,000 for every draw, as well as prize money ranging from €10,000 to €180,000 depending on where they finish in the table, rising by €10,000 per position.

Additionally, the eventual champions would receive €1,050,000 in prize money across the course of the knockout phase – including €500,000 specifically for winning the final – as there are six-figure sums on offer for each knockout-phase fixture.

Chelsea will be at home for the first leg, which is scheduled to be played on 26 August, with the second leg in Spain scheduled for 2 September, three days before Chelsea’s WSL season opener, which is at home against Aston Villa on 5 September.

Chelsea have been strong contenders for the European title in recent years, reaching the semi-finals in three of the past four campaigns, but they lost to their rivals Arsenal in a dramatic quarter-final last term.

Real Sociedad, based in San Sebastián, finished third in Spain’s top division last term behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. The qualifying draw was split into two sections, with a “champions path” for winners of their domestic divisions drawn separately to the “league path” which contained domestic runners-up and third-placed sides such as Chelsea.

Køge, who eliminated the Scottish champions Hearts earlier in the qualification process, were pitted against PSV Eindhoven, while the most eye-catching tie of the round will see Ajax take on Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton seal Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of messing with his mental health after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, have agreed four-year contracts with the option of a further 12 months.

“There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in,” said Johnson. “You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I’m a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.”

McNeil, who had entered the final year of his Everton contract, appeared to be moving to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season.

They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League, but then pulled out. McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, wrote an emotional post on Instagram saying there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been affected.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s OK to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

On Tuesday the Palace chair, Steve Parish, said: “It is wonderful to finally welcome Dwight – a player with proven ability in the Premier League – to South London. I’m looking forward to seeing him in action at Selhurst Park.”

Johnson had been disappointing at Palace, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given he signed a four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid, but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.
