Palace are also finalising a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body.

Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

But in a post on his Truth Social social media site early on Tuesday, Trump said removing the Fifa president would be a costly move.

The US president wrote: “Fifa would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing president Gianni Infantino.

“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”

Uefa and two other confederations have held initial talks about organising competitions themselves amid the backlash against the embattled Fifa president.

Europe’s governing body, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf, which oversees football in the ‌Caribbean, North and Central America, have accused Infantino of “deception” and while it is understood they want to give him the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election in March next year, they want to insulate themselves from the unfolding crisis.

Uefa has previously threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions.

Infantino apologised for his proposal to create Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company to run the commercial and operational aspects of Fifa’s tournaments, with an idea to sell off around 20% to private investors.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But an open letter signed by the heads of Uefa, AFC and Concacaf has urged Fifa to hold an independent review into Infantino’s scheme, while not naming the Swiss directly.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” the letter said. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 3: Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

It was the day after the final game of last season at Bournemouth’s secluded, swish training base and, before clearing his belongings on his last day in the building, the departing head coach, Andoni Iraola, spent a couple of hours in his office chewing the fat with his successor, Marco Rose, talking players, pubs and tactics. The story goes that, with time moving on, Tiago Pinto, the club’s sporting director, knocked on the door to advise them there were other things to tackle.

It was an interesting scenario that speaks volumes of the respect between the pair. Long before joining Bournemouth, Iraola cited Rose’s Borussia Mönchengladbach side as one of his favourite teams to watch, the German’s “vertical football” helping them qualify for the Champions League in Rose’s first season in charge.

Rose accepts that Iraola, in absorbing the sales of key players totalling more than £250m last season and qualifying for Europe for the first time, has set a high bar. Remarkably, Bournemouth did not lose a game after the sale of Antoine Semenyo in the second week of January. Rose put it succinctly during pre-season in Austria. “Andoni didn’t leave a lot of space to improve,” he said. “Pressure’s on.”

In his first session, Rose told the players he loved the way they attacked the Premier League last season. Playing in the Europa League, however, represents uncharted territory for a team in the second tier as recently as four years ago. It is why Bournemouth’s hierarchy contacted peers at Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest to understand the realities of juggling the Thursday-Sunday rhythm the competition will bring. Rose is close friends with Oliver Glasner, who is now at Forest, but won the Conference League last season with Palace. “We are not going to Europe just to enjoy, we want to be competitive,” Rose said. “We are not there just to watch.”

Unlike last summer, so far they have retained all key players, chiefly Alex Scott, Rayan and Eli Junior Kroupi, the 20-year-old forward who breezed into double figures in his debut Premier League season and the club consider a generational talent. Kroupi attracted serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, among other European superpowers, but a freak foot injury during a pre-season drill means he is sidelined for at least three months.

At the end of the season, Bournemouth earmarked a centre-back to replace Marcos Senesi and a striker to compete with Evanilson as key priorities and by the start of August the club had recruited Álvaro Rodríguez, whom Rose wanted to sign at Leipzig, and António Silva from Elche and Benfica respectively. Juanlu Sánchez joined from Sevilla to provide competition for Adam Smith, the evergreen 35-year-old into his 14th season at the club, and will also fill the void left by Álex Jiménez, who has joined Fiorentina on loan with an option to sign permanently because he remains suspended in England while under investigation by the Football Association.

Off-field picture

The smallest stadium in the Premier League has been a building site this summer, with the club working to ensure their 11,357-seater ground complies with Uefa regulations. There has been a wider facelift, too, with every seat being replaced, while they are filling in two corners to increase the capacity by 800 this season. Playing in Europe brings the challenge of meeting Uefa’s squad-cost ratio (SCR) rules, which caps on-pitch spending at 70% of a club’s revenue. Bournemouth finished the 2025-26 season at 82% and they continue to work towards meeting the threshold. Last month the academy was awarded category one status, four years after being category three.

Owner-fan relationship

The American billionaire Bill Foley described himself as a dictator upon buying the club approaching four years ago, but supporters are grateful for his naked ambition. Foley, who made his fortune in insurance, is forthright and somewhat prophetic. In 2023, he said the club would play in Europe within five years – and achieved it in three. It was a similar story with Vegas Golden Knights, whom he vowed would win the Stanley Cup within six years of him launching the ice hockey franchise in 2017 – they won it in their sixth season. Foley recently added rugby union’s Exeter Chiefs to his sporting stable, which extends to Lorient, Auckland FC and Moreirense. Not every decision is universally popular but Foley, who turns 82 in December and predominantly splits his time between California and Vegas, puts his money where his mouth is.

The manager

As a defender, Marco Rose was schooled by Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel at Mainz, and Ralf Rangnick at Hannover, so had quite the education before beginning his coaching career at home town club Lokomotive Leipzig. Klopp told Rose, after promotion to the Bundesliga in 2004, that he would excel in the dugout and he has since managed some of the biggest names: Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham at Borussia Dortmund, Dominik Szoboszlai and Dani Olmo at RB Leipzig. Rose has been compared to Klopp and, naturally, Iraola, given his appetite for high-energy tactics. Bournemouth routed Genoa 10-1 in pre-season so, could his style be even more aggressive than Iraola’s? “I would say [to be] even more aggressive than Andoni is quite difficult,” came the reply. His grandfather, Walter Rose, represented Germany in 1937.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen António Silva has all the attributes to be a bargain buy for Bournemouth. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

These days, £50m is about the going rate for an elite defender. Tottenham paid £52m to sign Jan Paul van Hecke. Chelsea paid the same fee to take Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace. Bournemouth pocketed £50m when Dean Huijsen joined Real Madrid last year, though that price was set by a release clause. They are deals that make Bournemouth’s £25.7m purchase of António Silva, a 22-year-old who has been a regular at Benfica since breaking into the team and has experience in the Champions League, Europa League and 20 caps for Portugal, appear a snip. Silva, who is right-footed but prefers to play as a left-centre back, is a direct replacement for Senesi.

Stat attack

Bournemouth scored nine goals from Opta-defined counterattacks last season, the joint most in the Premier League. But their threat was varied; in only two of their preceding eight top-flight campaigns did they score more set-piece goals than the 14 they managed in 2025-26. It is very rare for a team to be so productive on both fronts.

Set for a breakthrough

It was a November night of ecstasy when Scotland qualified for the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, but for Ben Gannon-Doak it was a bittersweet evening and one that curtailed his club season. The 20-year-old was forced off after 21 minutes, replaced by Kenny McLean who capped the scoring in style. A £25m arrival from Liverpool last August, Gannon-Doak featured in all three of Scotland’s World Cup matches, starting the first and last, and has impressed in pre-season. After being limited to 113 minutes in eight league appearances as a substitute last campaign, there is optimism Gannon-Doak will make his mark.

World Cup impact

Rayan became the first Brazilian teenager to start a World Cup match since Marco Antônio in 1970 when he was named in Carlo Ancelotti’s starting XI for their Group C game against Scotland. The then 19-year-old, signed from Vasco de Gama in January, set up Vinícius Júnior for Brazil’s opener in the 3-0 win and afterwards swapped shirts with Gannon-Doak. Tyler Adams enhanced his reputation, impressing for the USA en route to the last 16. Two new members of Bournemouth’s coaching staff, the set-piece coach, Nicolas Gagnon, and goalkeeping coach, Frederic de Boever, worked with Canada and Belgium respectively. Alex Scott’s inclusion in Tuchel’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida spoke volumes of the Guernsey-born midfielder’s wider standing.

Sports.title: Declan Rice’s cousin joins EFL club on loan as statement released
Sports.content:
Declan Rice's cousin Finley Munroe has joined Blackpool on loan for the season from Middlesbrough.

The Seasiders confirmed the arrival of the 21-year-old on Monday as he prepares to play in the third division for the first time in his career.



3 Rice and Munroe are cousins and both came through the Chelsea youth system Credit: Getty

Munroe can play at left-back or centre-back and has been on loan at Real Union and Swindon Town so far.

He joined Boro in January from Aston Villa, but the club have now sent him out on another temporary deal.

This is, though, another step forwards in his career, and he joins up with Ian Evatt's side.



Speaking to the club's website at his unveiling, he said: “I’ve had some really positive discussions with the gaffer.

“The way he wants to play and the ambitions he has for this season really attracted me to the club. I think it’s a good fit for me.”



And Evatt is looking forward to getting him involved as well.

He said: “We are delighted to have added Finley to our ranks, providing further quality to our back line ahead of the league campaign kicking off this weekend.

“He is someone who has undoubted quality and is keen to progress even further here at Bloomfield Road.



“I believe he will be a key player for us on the left-hand side of our team and I can’t wait to start working with him.”

3 Rice and Munroe are from Kingston-upon-Thames in south west London Credit: Getty

Munroe's career so far

Munroe is one of many Chelsea academy graduates who moved on before getting a chance with the first team, much like his cousin Rice.

At 16, he headed to the Midlands to join up with Villa and progressed through the ranks there.



He did manage two senior appearances while at Villa Park due to his ability to play anywhere across the left of the defence.

During his final loan spell while at Villa, Munroe worked under former Blackpool boss Ian Holloway at Swindon Town.

That gave him a first taste of men's senior football in England before Boro swooped and agree to pay around £300,000 for him.

He impressed that much on loan with Swindon that the Championship side decided to take a punt.



Now, he has the chance to show what he can do in League One before potentially getting a crack in the Premier League.

3 Munroe made three Championship appearances for Boro last year Credit: Getty

Rebuilding

Blackpool start their league campaign at home against Wycombe Wanderers on Saturday, and Munroe will be pushing for an immediate debut.

The Tangerines beat Grimsby 3-1 in the EFL Cup on Saturday as the tournament got domestic football under way and they will now face Lincoln in the second round.



They finished the previous campaign well under Evatt as he took over from Steve Bruce.

However, pre-season saw mixed results with losses to Tranmere, Barrow, and Port Vale, but a draw with Blackburn Rovers.

Blackpool also lost Ashley Fletcher, who scored 15 goals for the League One side last season, to Huddersfield Town.

Striker Dion Charles has moved in the opposite direction on loan, while Karoy Anderson, Ilmari Niskanen, and Jordan Williams are also arrivals.

Sports.title: West Ham could sell another star player to Premier League club in deal worth up to £40m
Sports.content:
West Ham could sell another star player to Premier League club in deal worth up to £40m

Brentford are set to launch an improved offer bid for West Ham star El Hadji Malick Diouf, talkSPORT understands.

This deal, which could be worth as much as £40million comes after the Bees previously had an undisclosed bid rejected for the left-back, with the Hammers insisting he would not be sold.



5 El Hadji Malick Diouf looks set for an immediate return to the Premier League Credit: Getty

Diouf was one of the Irons' standout performers last season, as they were ultimately relegated to the Championship.

The Senegal international impressed in his debut campaign in the Premier League after joining in a £22m deal plus add-ons from Slavia Prague.

This led to him being linked with a summer exit, with Manchester United showing an interest back in April.



Brentford to bid again

Brentford joined the race for Diouf in July by putting in an offer, only for West Ham appearing to shut down any possible departure by insisting he would not be sold.

But now, with just days until their Championship season opener against Burnley, their resolve will be tested again.



The Bees are understood to be launching a deal worth up to £40m to bring the 21-year-old to west London.

It represents another big-money move for Keith Andrews' side this summer, who recently smashed their club transfer record with the arrival of Mamadou Sangare from Lens.



While the exact fee was undisclosed, Brentford said it surpasses the £42.5m paid to sign Dango Ouattara from Bournemouth in 2025.

And if Diouf's deal goes through this would place him high up in the club's all-time transfer list.

The Senegalese could be set for an immediate return to the Premier League, as he becomes the second player to head to the Gtech Community Stadium after leaving West Ham.

5 Keith Andrews will have greater security at left-back by pulling off the signing of Diouf Credit: Getty



5 Diouf featured three times for Senegal at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

Callum Wilson also moved to west London on a one-year deal following the expiry of his contract at the London Stadium.

Diouf's potential arrival would represent a much-needed addition at left-back for Brentford.

While Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey are both specialists in the position, the pair have struggled with injuries in recent years.



Scotland international Hickey spent almost two years out with a hamstring problem before returning last October.

Meanwhile Henry is currently out with a hamstring issue, after making 25 Premier League appearances last term following his return from an ACL injury.

In their place, winger Keane Lewis-Potter has deputised well, but could now return to his natural position should Diouf's move go through as expected.

5 Nuno Espirito Santo will now have to find alternatives to Diouf in the left-back position Credit: AFP



5 Diouf is set to join Freddie Potts by departing the London Stadium days before West Ham's season begins Credit: Getty

West Ham's summer transfers exodus

West Ham are now set to lose another key player as Diouf could leave, despite their previous not-for-sale stance.

Earlier this summer, Mateus Fernandes joined rivals Tottenham in a £85m deal, before Crysencio Summerville signed for Saudi outfit Al Hilal for £68m.

The Hammers recouped £153m from the two departures, and was thought to leave them under no obligation to more offload players.



In-demand captain Jarrod Bowen penned a new contract with the club in a major boost, as he prepares to spearhead their promotion charge in the upcoming Championship season.

However, Nuno Espirito Santo's side were dealt a fresh blow when academy graduate Freddie Potts completed a £10m move to Belgian side Club Brugge.

And with Irons set to kick off their season against Burnley on Sunday, they also look set to be without Diouf for the Turf Moor clash.

Sports.title: Ryan Reynolds makes savage comment as couple move from Texas to Wrexham after watching documentary
Sports.content:
Ryan Reynolds makes savage comment as couple move from Texas to Wrexham after watching documentary

An American couple are set to move from Texas to Wrexham after watching the club's Disney Plus documentary.

The Championship outfit features in the Welcome to Wrexham series on the streaming platform.



3 A couple are set to move to Wales from Texas after watching Welcome to Wrexham Credit: Getty

Having first aired in 2022, the show released its fifth season earlier this year and has already been extended for three more editions.

Documenting the goings on at the club since Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney's takeover in 2020, it has brought in fans from around the world.

Among them are Jeff and Janice Ivey from New Braunfels, Texas, who are now set to move to the Welsh city.



The couple have visited Wales seven times in the last two-and-a-half years since first watching the show.

Jeff is already in Wrexham house-hunting ahead of their permanent move to the area.



He already holds UK citizenship through his Scottish ancestry, whilst Janice remains in the USA selling their home and awaiting her visa.

Reynolds reacts to Wrexham move

News of their impending move quickly went viral on social media, with Wrexham co-owner Reynolds even spotting the story.



The Hollywood star could not resist providing his own response to the move.

Writing on X, he joked: "Thank God they didn't watch Chernobyl," in reference to the 2019 series.

The show centred on the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, which occurred near to the now abandoned Ukrainian city of Pripyat.

3 Reynolds could not resist making a savage comment in reaction to the news Credit: Getty



Reynolds is no stranger to social media antics in relation to the club.

He even shared his X-rated reaction to drawing Chelsea in the FA Cup last season alongside fellow actor Hugh Jackman on X.

Wrexham ready for new season

Since buying the club with McElhenney six years ago, they have overseen a remarkable change in fortunes for the Red Dragons.

Wrexham won three successive promotions to reach the Championship in 2025.



It marked their first appearance in the second-tier of English football for 43 years.

Phil Parkinson's side subsequently finished seventh last season, missing out on the play-offs by just two points.

3 Reynolds has overseen three promotions since buying Wrexham with McElhenney in 2020 Credit: AP

They are set to begin the new league campaign this weekend following a Carabao Cup exit to Middlesbrough on Friday.



Wrexham visit Welsh rivals Cardiff City on Monday, August 17 at 8pm, live on talkSPORT 2.

Sports.title: Kalvin Phillips set for another EFL loan with two years still left on lucrative Man City contract
Sports.content:
Kalvin Phillips set for another EFL loan with two years still left on lucrative Man City contract

Kalvin Phillips is nearing a return to Sheffield United on loan, talkSPORT understands.

The Manchester City midfielder spent the second half of last season at Bramall Lane but only managed three appearances before a knee injury brought an early end to his stint.



2 Phillips was sent off in his most recent appearance for the Blades Credit: Getty

However, the injury has not proved to be enough to put off Blades boss Chris Wilder from wanting to bring Phillips back.

Should the deal be completed, it would mark yet another loan for Phillips, who has no future at City despite having two years to run on his reported £150,000-a-week deal.

The 30-year-old was not included in City's squad for their pre-season tour of Asia, where they took on Inter Milan, Atletico Madrid and the K League All-Stars.



How many games has Kalvin Phillips played for Manchester City?

Phillips' omission from the touring party represented the latest low in what has been a difficult spell at the club since his £42million arrival from Leeds in July 2022.

To date, Phillips has made just 32 competitive appearances for City, with only six of those being starting berths.



The difficulty to break into City's line-up led to Phillips spending time on loan at West Ham and Ipswich Town.

However, neither spell helped Phillips rediscover the form that made him a 31-time England international.



What has Chris Wilder said about signing Kalvin Phillips?

Yet Wilder is convinced Phillips can still be an asset and stated in April he hoped the club would 'love to be an option' for the midfielder this summer.

"We brought a really good pro in," Wilder said.

"He was unlucky with his injury – he passed a tough medical.

2 Wilder remains an admirer of Phillips despite the midfielder's struggles over the years Credit: Getty

“He's not played as much as he wanted to play but he’s been in around the place.

"I've just basically said to him: ‘We'd love to be an option for you, your agent and your parent club.’



“He certainly ticks the boxes in terms of personality and characteristics.

“He's been to every one of our home games and in here for 90 per cent of his rehab. He's been in player meetings he didn't have to be. That's invaluable for us.”

Wilder's side enjoyed a winning start to the 2026/27 campaign courtesy of a 3-0 victory over Mansfield Town in their Carabao Cup first round encounter on Sunday.

Goals from Patrick Bamford, Mark McGuinness and Callum O'Hare did the business for the Blades, who will face Blackburn Rovers in the next round.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026/27 opening weekend fixture dates and kick-off times in full
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 Premier League season is now just days away.

With the World Cup over, the top-flight is ready to return and the countdown is on for the opening game of the campaign.

4 Mikel Arteta's champions face Coventry on the first day of the new season Credit: Getty



And Coventry will get things underway with their first game back in the Premier League for 25 years, facing champions Arsenal.

All 380 games for the 2026/27 season were confirmed in June and also see newly-promoted Hull City hosting Michael Carrick's Manchester United on the opening weekend.

Liverpool, under new manager Andoni Iraola, travel to Newcastle with a fit-again Alexander Isak, who swapped the north east for the north west in a £125million transfer last summer.

Meanwhile, Tottenham travel to Brentford and feel they have the right manager in charge in Roberto De Zerbi, who guided them to safety on the final day of the 2025/26 season.



And Xabi Alonso's first game as Chelsea boss takes him to Fulham on Monday night, while it could be a changed Man City side that takes on Bournemouth with Elliot Anderson in the middle.

When does the Premier League season begin?

Arsenal, winners last season, begin the new season on Friday, August 21 as they take on Coventry at the Emirates at 8pm.



The top-flight opener will be exclusively live on talkSPORT.

Hull host Man United at 12:30pm on the first Saturday of the season - also on talkSPORT - while Brentford vs Tottenham is the 5:30pm match and there are a trio of 3pm games.

Newcastle vs Liverpool is the first 4:30pm Sunday match of the new campaign.



And Fulham vs Chelsea rounds off the opening weekend on Monday night, again live on talkSPORT.

Opening day fixtures Friday, August 21 Arsenal v Coventry City, 8pm - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE Saturday, August 22 Hull vs Manchester United, 12:30pm - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE

Everton vs Crystal Palace, 3pm

Man City vs Bournemouth, 2pm

Who do the promoted clubs play?

Ipswich are back in the big time, having last played against West Ham in 2025 and losing 3-1.

Their first home game is against Sunderland and it will be new manager Gary O'Neil's opening competitive match in charge.

Hull, who were beaten by Tottenham 7-1 in their last Premier League game in 2017, won't have it easier against a revitalised United side led by Carrick, who was given the manager's role having guided them to third place last season.



"What a great game for us," Hull assistant manager Dean Holden told talkSPORT. "We had an incredible season last year to get promoted.

"I was sat doing an interview at a similar time last year talking about the Championship fixtures, and people were having us as one of the relegation favourites.

"So, what the club did to get promoted is nothing short of incredible. And to then see the fixtures come out this morning, it just all seems very real."

4 Hull City celebrate their return to the top tier by hosting Man United on the first Saturday game of the season, which is live on talkSPORT Credit: Getty



4 Lampard's Coventry go to Arsenal on the opening day and he hosts former club Chelsea in December Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Elsewhere, it has been a long time coming for Coventry, whose last Premier League game was in May 2001.

A trip to Arsenal first will delight manager Frank Lampard, who will relish the test of playing the champions.

Opening weekend live on talkSPORT

talkSPORT will be across all of the opening weekend's action with three games to be broadcast live on the station.



Our dedicated team will be at the Emirates as Arsenal kick off their title defence against Coventry.

Likewise, fans can catch all of the action from the MKM Stadium when newly-promoted Hull host United at Saturday lunchtime.

But there will be no such controversy this time around with multiple games expected to be televised on the day, pending broadcasting picks.

Sports.title: Premier League rival of Liverpool consider shock move for Alexis Mac Allister
Sports.content:
Manchester City have shortlisted Alexis Mac Allister as they look at potential Rodri replacements, talkSPORT understands.

The Citizens are preparing to lose influential midfielder Rodri imminently, who is closing in on a move to Barcelona.

5 Alexis Mac Allister recently returned to Liverpool after helping Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands a deal to take Spain's World Cup-winning captain to the Camp Nou is now advanced, with an agreement over a £55million package expected to be reached in the coming days.

While losing Rodri would represent a huge blow to City, replacing him has been a focal point of their summer transfer strategy.

Elliot Anderson was signed for £116m at the start of the window, while they are now in advanced talks with Lille over Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, with personal terms agreed.

However, City could look to strengthen further in midfield should Rodri's departure go through, with several options being considered.

Surprise switch?

talkSPORT's Ben Jacob has revealed Liverpool star Mac Allister is among the potential options being explored by City.

The Argentina international has been a mainstay in the Reds' midfield since his arrival from Brighton in 2023, and has now entered into the final two years of his Anfield contract.

Despite starring for Liverpool in their Premier League title win in 2025, he experienced a dip in form last term as Arne Slot's side finished a disappointing fifth, and faced calls to be dropped.

However, Jacobs revealed Mac Allister could be more affordable option for City this summer in comparison to other potential targets Adam Wharton and Enzo Fernandez, who previously worked with new boss Enzo Maresca at Chelsea.

Jacobs told talkSPORT's Transfer Insiders: “I know internally Alexis McAllister has been mentioned, but there's been no contact yet, or developments with Liverpool.

"So that's just more part of a shortlisting process than anything to get excited about.

5 Rodri seems destined to depart Man City, and his exit could pave the way for more business Credit: Getty

5 A move to rivals Manchester City for Mac Allister would certainly rumble Liverpool fans

“Some people have mentioned Adam Wharton to me as well.

"So possibly in a perfect world, if Enzo Maresca had his say, he might choose to move for Enzo Fernandez. We can't entirely discount it, but the price is a massive stumbling block.

"And at the moment, City's focus is on trying to get Bouaddi over the line.”

Despite a challenging campaign last term, Mac Allister has proven his value in title-winning sides in recent years.

He played a crucial role in Argentina's 2022 World Cup win, before scoring five goals from midfield as Liverpool won the 2024/25 Premier League title, and was named in the PFA Team of the Year for his performances.

Mac Allister joined Liverpool for a £55m package deal in 2023, and while any asking price is currently unclear, it is likely to be far less than City's other potential targets in Fernandez or Wharton.

5 Enzo Fernandez scored 10 Premier League goals from midfield last term Credit: Getty

Enz game?

Chelsea star Fernandez has been one of the most talked about players this summer, having previously fuelled rumours of his exit.

The 25-year-old heavily hinted at a move to Real Madrid towards the end of last season, only for the Spanish giants to shut this down in a statement saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

However, his future in west London remains unclear, and a move to Man City could be appealing for the Argentine, which would offer him a reunion with former Blues boss Maresca at the Etihad.

Maresca left left Stamford Bridge on New Year's Day after a breakdown in relations at the club, a decision which Fernandez later appeared to criticise the Chelsea board over.

But with Fernandez boasting a huge £120m price tag, Jacobs revealed City could stop short of another nine-digit transfer, with Bouaddi's arrival from Lille also likely to cost in the region of £100m.

He explained: "Chelsea's asking price was £120m. Now, maybe that's higher if you consider the fact that other deals, like Elliot Anderson - £116m.

5 Maresca and Fernandez shared a close bond while at Chelsea Credit: Getty

"And Chelsea may argue that Enzo Fernandez should be more. He's a World Cup winner after all, and he was the vice-captain and captain at times of Chelsea.

“So Chelsea are calm about the situation, and they have every intent, if the window shuts, to try and get Enzo Fernandez on one extreme to sign the new deal.

“And yet, if their valuation is met, an exit is possible.

“We know that Enzo Fernandez has flirted with a move to Real Madrid. But if we take the public statement at face value, even with Rodri heading to Barcelona, the expectation is that Real won't move. You can never say never with Real, but they were put off by that asking price, according to my information.”

“So yes, City - specifically Enzo Maresca - do appreciate Enzo Fernandez. Are they going to find that budget questionable?

"If Bouaddi is nearly £100m, Elliot Anderson £116m, and then Enzo Fernandez at least £120m, that's a huge outlay in the centre of the park. There might be some more economical options.”

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to two Premier League rivals by Arsenal in surprise transfer update
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to two Premier League rivals by Arsenal in surprise transfer update

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Premier League clubs by Arsenal, talkSPORT understands.

The 19-year-old is free to leave the Gunners following the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

3 Arsenal have offered Lewis-Skelly to multiple clubs this summer Credit: Getty

Lewis-Skelly has been offered to multiple clubs in a bid to secure a move for the academy graduate.

Amongst them are Premier League rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The Blues previously handed a young Lewis-Skelly a trial before he joined Arsenal's famed Hale End academy.

Both clubs had previously been made aware of Lewis-Skelly's availability, with United showing interest in a move.

However, fresh contact has been made since the signing of Guimaraes.

The Brazil midfielder joined the Premier League champions in a £75million deal on Saturday.

Guimaraes further adds to Mikel Arteta's extensive midfield options in north London.

The Arsenal boss also has the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Declan Rice, Mikel Merino, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze at his disposal.

Lewis-Skelly's Arsenal career

It leaves Lewis-Skelly's future at the Emirates Stadium in doubt just over a year after he was handed a new long-term deal.

He penned a five-year contract through to 2030 in June 2025 before helping the Gunners win the Premier League title last term.

3 Fresh contact has been made with Chelsea and United over a move for Lewis-Skelly Credit: Getty

Lewis-Skelly featured 20 times during their title-winning campaign, with a total of 36 appearances in all competitions across the season.

The versatile youngster, who has been deployed at both left-back and in midfield, also started the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in May.

A move this summer would end Lewis-Skelly's 11-year stay at Arsenal.

He first joined the club's academy at Under-9 level in 2015 following trials at both Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur.

After featuring for the Under-18s whilst still aged just 14, he was handed his first-team debut by Arteta three years later.

His maiden appearance came against Manchester City in November 2024, four days before his 18th birthday.

3 Lewis-Skelly has made 75 appearances for Arsenal since making his debut aged 17 Credit: Getty

Lewis-Skelly has since featured 75 times for the Gunners, scoring once and providing six assists.

He was also handed a senior England debut in March 2025 by Thomas Tuchel, scoring in a 2-0 win over Albania.

Although Lewis-Skelly has gone on to amass six caps for the Three Lions, he was not part of their World Cup squad this summer.

Having not been included by Tuchel since October, he instead made two appearances for the Under-21s earlier this year.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes urges Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for 'nutcase' Cristian Romero - despite calling him 'an absolute clown' who 'does stupid things'
Sports.content:
Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to gazump Atletico Madrid's £34million move for Cristian Romero, despite branding the Tottenham captain a 'nutcase' and 'absolute clown' in his sales pitch.

The Argentina defender, 28, is expected to leave Spurs this summer after being given the green light to join LaLiga heavyweights Atletico Madrid, who are deep in talks with the north London outfit and only a few million apart in negotiations.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils are eagerly exploring options to bolster Michael Carrick's squad ahead of the new campaign, which will see United compete in the Champions League after finishing third in the Premier League last season.

Scholes, who has previously criticised Romero's rash and ill-disciplined approach to defending at Spurs, has surprisingly called for United to hijack Atletico's pursuit.

'This is one you might laugh at. Cristian Romero from Tottenham,' he said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast while discussing potential transfer targets for United.

'I know it might sound stupid, but I just think... I like him. I think he's a nutcase. He's a very good defender that does some stupid things. He is an absolute clown.

Paul Scholes has urged Man United to hijack Atletico Madrid's £34m move for Cristian Romero

Scholes branded the defender a 'nutcase' but still thinks he would bring something to United

'But I think if someone could get hold of him, like Michael Carrick, who is very calm and relaxed, he might be able to [help him].

'He seems like a bit of a cult hero defender, really. I know it might sound strange, but I think the fans at Old Trafford would like him.

'There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him and he's cheap, £30-40million.'

Carrick has a string of defensive options at centre-half heading into the season, with Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Ayden Heaven and Romero's international team-mate Lisandro Martinez among those who operate at the heart of defence.

Scholes believes, despite the options available, that United need to bolster that department in particular if they plan to kick on in the future.

'I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing],' he added. 'You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You’d like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

'Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They’ve got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he’s still going to make mistakes. He’s young.

'Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league].'

Manchester United's first test in the Premier League is a trip to newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday, August 22.

Sports.title: Defiant James McClean turns up for training at Derry City after poppy protestor's hometown club tried to rip up his contract
Sports.content:
James McClean rocked up for training at Derry City on Tuesday morning - despite the Northern Irish club reportedly trying to rip up his contract.

The 37-year-old rolled up in a black Range Rover despite a report in the Irish Independent claiming that Derry want to cancel his deal due to his supposed lack of 'physical capacity'.

Asked by reporters whether he was still a player with the club, McClean simply replied: 'Clearly.'

McClean signed for his hometown club at the start of the 2026 season and has two years left on his deal, but has only started 12 of their 27 league games after leaving Wrexham.

The club reportedly claim that he is unable to fulfil his contract's terms because he is not fit enough to play or train.

However the star - who has regularly made headlines for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations - is expected to insist that a contract cannot be cancelled unilaterally and that an independent physician must determine his fitness.

James McClean has turned up for Derry City training despite them reportedly trying to rip up his contract

WATCH. James McClean arrives at Brandywell Stadium for training amid reports Derry City has terminated his contract pic.twitter.com/db454kWy7U — Simon Collins (@SimonCollins82) August 11, 2026

Derry sit sixth out of 10 teams in the League of Ireland Premier Division, a disappointing campaign after finishing runners-up in 2023 and 2025.

In June, McClean hinted at his unhappiness following his return home after a 15-year spell in English football.

'Family (are) enjoying being home – probably not so much myself, if I’m being honest,' McClean said during a punditry appearance on RTE.

'You know, you have a lot of conversations on the phone, and then you come home and you quickly realise that what you hear on the phone is not what you see in reality.

'There’s a lot of factors that’s contributed to that, but we’ll leave them for another day.'

McClean has previously spoken out about his reasons for not wearing the poppy, a decision he first made while playing for Sunderland in 2012. He maintained that stance throughout his career in England, despite being regularly targeted with abuse.

'The poppy which originally stood for World War 1 and 2 has now been adopted into honouring and remembering British soldiers that have served in all conflicts throughout the world including those who opened fire and murdered 14 innocent civilians on Bloody Sunday Jan 1972, in my home city, as well many other brutal crimes throughout Ireland,' McClean said in 2024.

'That is why I never have and never will wear a poppy. If the poppy’s sole purpose was to honour World War 1 and 2 then I would have no issue wearing it, but that’s not the case.

McClean has regularly made headlines throughout his career for his refusal to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations

'I respect those who do as I am fully aware we have different beliefs and upbringings, I would never force my beliefs on others, I’m not naive or stupid enough to expect the matter to be reciprocated, especially as the poppy is forced now on everyone in the UK and god forbid someone doesn’t wear it, the abuse they have to endure. The irony of all of this is that the poppy originally stood to honour those who fought for the right of freedom in both World Wars.

'Some people, no matter what, will not educate themselves or want to educate themselves, so to those who throw abuse about (matters they know nothing about), with insults like ‘hates our country’ – well I don’t. Some of my best relationships I’ve made through the years are with people born and raised in England and have completely different beliefs to me ... One thing I never have and never will do, is bend the knee to compromise my convictions.'

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland whom he represented in the Under 21s, said he had received 'death threats' for his stance over the poppy.

Last October, speaking during an episode of Virgin Media's Living with Lucy, he told presenter Lucy Kennedy how his family feared he would be shot while away on international duty after he first refused to wear a poppy on his shirt in 2012.

'I was getting death threats, people were saying I should be shot,' he said. 'I was getting bullets in the post, bullets sent to the club.

'That night, I met up with Ireland. The club had received threats that basically I was going to be shot. The game was on TV. I was going to be shot, this and that. (My wife, Erin) is back up in Newcastle, she’s panicking, she’s s*****g herself. They had to put security outside my hotel room door the whole night.

'Then, obviously, we’re playing the game, Erin’s watching the game, she’s panicking, she’s thinking, "He’s going to be shot on TV". Thankfully, nothing happened or nothing ever has happened.'

He added: 'I was getting death threats, people were saying he should be shot and dragged across the Cenotaph.

McClean, who has won 103 caps for the Republic of Ireland since choosing to play for them rather than Northern Ireland, said he has received 'death threats' for his poppy stance

'I could have easily just said, "I'll wear a poppy," and sold myself out and be known for my football or "I'll not wear a poppy" and be known as that but I've stayed true to myself.

'Six or seven people from the Creggan estate (where he grew up) died on Bloody Sunday that day so for me to wear a poppy in support of the people who carried out those atrocities...

'It frustrates me how people can’t see that. How is it even a debate of why I should wear the poppy?'

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly offered to Chelsea and Man United with Arsenal looking to sell after £75m Bruno Guimaraes capture
Sports.content:
Arsenal midfielder Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United following the Gunners' capture of Bruno Guimaraes.

The 19-year-old signed a new deal last year following his breakout season, but after limited minutes in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign, there is belief the champions may be willing to move the Hale End product on.

There has been fresh contact with both the Blues and United, among other Premier League clubs, who are assessing whether to make a move for the versatile player.

Lewis-Skelly's minutes at Arsenal could be further limited in the upcoming season, with Guimaraes completing a £75million move from Newcastle last week.

Chelsea are understood to have long held an interest in Lewis-Skelly, but it is unclear whether they will put down an offer.

The academy product only managed 19 starts in all competitions last season, with Arteta giving him a rebirth in the middle of the park toward the end of the campaign, which led to a start in the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

Arsenal star Myles Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United

Chelsea and United could both test Arsenal's resolve with a high enough offer for Lewis-Skelly

But with the Brazilian now expected to leapfrog Lewis-Skelly in the midfield pecking order, and opportunities already limited at left-back, there is a feeling that a move could be on the cards.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months. He adds serious talent and depth to Arsenal's midfield, which already contains names such as Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

A move to Chelsea would also see Lewis-Skelly face competition for minutes, with the Blues boasting a contingent of Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez – who has been linked with a move away – Romeo Lavia, Dario Essugo, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with new boss Xabi Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light.

The Blues have already made a series of statements in the transfer market, with Maxence Lacroix joining from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Teenager Lewis-Skelly has already made 75 senior appearances for Arsenal, securing a Premier League winner's medal last campaign.

He predominantly started his career at left-back, making a name for himself in Arsenal's Champions League quarter-final demolition of Real Madrid in 2025, but has since returned to his preferred position in central midfield.

The youngster has started every pre-season game for Arsenal, of which they have lost two, but is expected to be moved in place of Rice and Guimaraes once they return to action.

Sports.title: Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Romelu Lukaku agrees £5m Turkey move - with Chelsea set for a windfall -as Napoli offer £2m loan fee for Blues defender Benoit Badiashile, and Liverpool teenager wanted on loan in Portugal: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

World Cup star joins Forest

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon.

The 22-year-old centre-back has signed a four-year deal with an option for another year.

Diomande said: 'It is a historic club, and it motivates me to join such a club. I believe we can achieve very good things this season and I am looking forward to meeting the players and head coach.

Nottingham Forest have completed the £36million signing of Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon

'I will give my best and all I can to help the team. I cannot wait to meet the supporters at the City Ground and together we can have a good season.'

Forest still want to add a right-back, midfielder and striker.

Patterson completes Wrexham medical

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move to Wrexham.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed yesterday, the 26-year-old has agreed terms on a four-year deal with the Championship club.

Patterson is finalising the paperwork on his contract.

Wrexham are also in talks to sign Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt in a £4.5m deal.

Hull get their Nobel prize

Hull City have finally agreed their protracted negotiations for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

The centre back is heading over for his medical after the clubs settled on a £21million fee plus 12.5per cent sell-on clause, while his former club Real Betis receive 20 percent as part of their sell-on.

The 21-year-old Senegal international can play at centre back and left-back.

Fulham snap up Southampton's Charles

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons.

Fulham have signed Shea Charles from Southampton for £27million plus £3m in add ons

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year contract, tying him to Craven Cottage until June 2031, with a club option to extend by a further 12 months.

Southampton also retain a 20percent sell-on.

Speaking to FFCtv, Charles, who will wear the number 19 shirt, said: 'It’s a great club, with a really good vision – the manager explained that to me. To be here is a massive privilege.

'I hope to really kickstart my Premier League career. At such a good club as well, it’s perfect for me, and hopefully perfect for the fans as well.

'I’m buzzing to finally get it over the line. The club has got a really good foundation, from the bottom to the top really.'

Palace and Everton complete rare swap deal

Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil have completed their respective swaps to Everton and Crystal Palace and signed four year contracts.

Johnson, who only joined Palace from Tottenham in January for £35m, told evertontv: ‘I'm so excited to be here. The club speaks for itself – it's a massive club and one that when I first heard of the interest, I immediately wanted to come and be part of it.

Brennan Johnson has completed a move to Everton from Crystal Palace in a rare swap deal

As part of the transfer, Dwight McNeil has moved the other way to link up with the Eagles after his transfer to the club on Deadline Day in the winter window collapsed at the last moment

'There were a lot of reasons why I was so keen to join – the manager, the players, the direction the team is going in. You can see this is a club that wants to go in the right direction, and I'm a player who wants to go in that direction, too, so it feels like a really good match.

He becomes the fifth summer signing for David Moyes’ squad after Merlin Rohl’s loan obligation was activated along with the additions of Hayden Hackney, Tyrique George and Christian Norgaard.

Meanwhile, McNeil has signed his four-year contract with Palace and said: 'The lads have had some great success over the last two seasons. It’s something that I want to be a part of, so I’m really looking forward to getting started.'

Lukaku agrees Turkey move

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli.

The Belgium international has agreed a two year contract worth around £8.6m a season and has already passed his medical.

The deal includes further add ons based on performances.

Romelu Lukaku has agreed to join Turkish side Fenerbahce in a £5million move from Napoli

Chelsea are understood to have inserted a 40percent sell-on clause when they sold Lukaku for a knockdown £26m to Napoli two years ago.

He scored 14 goals in his first season but injury and the arrival of Rasmus Hojlund from Manchester United restricted him to just seven games last year.

Liverpool starlet wanted in Portugal

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move.

The 18-year-old who has joined the club from Austria Vienna in a £2.5million deal has stood out for the first team in pre-season friendlies.

But despite the promise he has shown, and Liverpool's dearth of defensive cover, post-Brexit rules mean Austria youth international Ndukwe doesn't have enough points to obtain a Governing Body Endorsement (GBE) to obtain a work visa.

He will start against Como in their last friendly but is unable to play a competitive match for the Anfield club.

Liverpool centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe is attracting attention from clubs in Portugal ahead of a loan move

Now clubs from Germany, Spain, Denmark and France have been calling to take the 6ft 6ins centre back on loan but there is a sense Portugal may be his preferred destination.

After playing alongside him, captain Virgil van Dijk said: 'Big talent, big guy and he wants to learn. I had a brief conversation with him, especially in the last couple of days. For him, it is just progressing. I know he has to go on loan I think so let's see where he ends up.'

Napoli still in the hunt for Badiashile

Napoli have offered a £2m loan fee for Chelsea's £30million-rated centre-back Benoit Badiashile with obligation to buy.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs and the player's representatives to try and find a full agreement.

Chelsea have sold Trevoh Chalobah to Como and are also looking to sell Axel Disasi who has had interest from Crystal Palace and West Ham.

Napoli are continuing talks to sign Chelsea's £30m-rated centre-back Beniot Badiashile (right)

Mamadou Sarr, who suffered an injury at the weekend, is likely to go on loan to a Premier League side.

Keeper Filip Jorgensen has completed his move to Strasbourg on loan.

Wigan Athletic are closing in on their loan move for Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh while Portsmouth want 17-year-old Chelsea winger Ryan Kavuma-McQueen on loan.

Napoli remain keen on Arsenal striker Gabriel Jesus also as talks continue. Arsenal want £20m for the Brazilian.

Villa defender wanted in Belgium

Aston Villa right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic is a target for Rangers along with Hugo Siquet of Bruges.

Nedeljkovic has had interest from a number of clubs including Osasuna but Rangers are exploring a £4million deal with initial loan for the Serbia international.

The 20-year-old had a spell with RB Leipzig last season.

Burnley after new keeper

Burnley are showing interest in OH Leuven goalkeeper Tobe Leysen.

The 24-year-old former Belgium U21 international has one year left on contract so Leuven are willing to listen to offers.

SATURDAY: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon
