Sports.title: Jerry Quarry Destroys Earnie Shavers in 141 Seconds
Sports.content:
Both fighters were 28. Quarry weighed 202 pounds, eight lighter than Shavers.

The buildup had almost guaranteed violence. Quarry predicted three rounds and believed he could finish Shavers in one if his opponent came after him. Don King, then part of Shavers’ management team, called it their easiest fight. Madison Square Garden matchmaker Teddy Brenner went further, predicting the shortest 12-round fight in history. He wasn’t far off.

Trainer Gil Clancy wanted Quarry to box, but Quarry abandoned that idea almost immediately. Instead of giving Shavers room to unleash his power, he attacked him.

Quarry drove Shavers toward the ropes and unloaded lefts and rights to the head. Shavers managed to move away, but Quarry followed him across the ring and dropped him with a left-right combination.

Shavers got back up, only to find Quarry waiting for him. Quarry poured on punches as Shavers struggled to defend himself. His eyes looked unfocused, and he was taking clean shots without answering effectively. Referee Arthur Mercante had seen enough and stopped the fight at 2:21 of the opening round. There would be no need for judges Jack Gordon and Bill Recht.

The result was stunning because Quarry had beaten the knockout artist by fighting him at his own game. George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Muhammad Ali were among the prominent names at ringside. Foreman reportedly expressed surprise that Quarry had chosen to trade with Shavers and came away impressed by his aggression.

Ali and Frazier had another reason to be at the Garden. Their January 28, 1974 rematch was already set for the same arena and was promoted during the Quarry-Shavers telecast. Frazier discussed getting his weight down and preparing for Ali before the main event, while viewers were urged to buy tickets for their second fight.

Their rematch also strengthened Quarry’s position in the heavyweight picture. With Ali and Frazier committed to fighting each other, the broadcast team noted that neither man would likely be available for Foreman until around June. Quarry’s destruction of Shavers suddenly made him an obvious candidate to challenge the champion before then.

Quarry paid a physical price despite the short night. He injured his left wrist after landing a hook high on Shavers’ head, with reports raising concern over a possible fracture.

Shavers later admitted that the first heavy blows had left him unable to recover. He regretted rising so quickly after the knockdown, believing that taking more of the count might have given him enough time to survive the remaining seconds of the round.

Nearly 15,000 spectators had come expecting to see what happened when Shavers’ frightening power collided with Quarry’s durability and experience. They barely had time to settle into their seats.

The official attendance was 14,962, producing a gate of $201,564. Quarry was guaranteed $40,000 against 30 percent of the gate, while Shavers received $30,000 against 27½ percent.

The victory strengthened Quarry’s position near the top of a stacked division ruled by Foreman, but the championship opportunity never followed. Quarry instead met Frazier again the following year and was stopped in five rounds.

Shavers rebuilt his career and eventually challenged both Ali and Larry Holmes for the heavyweight championship.

Neither man’s later career changed what happened that December night. Shavers arrived with the reputation as a devastating slugger, but Quarry never gave him enough time to use it.

For 141 seconds, Quarry simply beat him to the punch.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Wants Haney To Stew In Loss
Sports.content:
“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen. They have to sit with that loss,” Ryan told The Ring. “Why do I have to beg for it? I’m here. I’m about to beat up Conor Benn. I want Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. I have a lot of options. I’m not really worried about Haney now. If it happens, it happens.”

What happened in April 2024 remains the source of the hostility. Garcia dropped Haney three times and won a majority decision before the victory was changed to a no-contest following his positive test for ostarine.

Devin and Bill Haney have repeatedly brought up the failed test since then, refusing to treat the original outcome as a legitimate defeat. Drug testing has also been a recurring subject whenever another fight with Garcia has been discussed.

Ryan’s refusal to rush into a rematch sounds personal. He has the WBC welterweight title, a September fight with Benn, and several lucrative opponents he can pursue without giving Haney an opportunity to settle the score.

“All these guys obviously have to come to me,” Ryan said. “I’m definitely the lottery fight. If you want to be a huge name, I’m the guy to do it [against]. You have to get through me.”

That is the position Garcia believes he occupies. After two years of hearing why his performance against Haney shouldn’t count, he doesn’t seem interested in helping Team Haney put it behind them.

They can sit with it.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Rallies To Stop Harold Johnson In 14
Sports.content:
Moore weighed 173 pounds to Johnson’s 172½.

Working behind his jab, movement and counterpunching, Johnson frustrated Moore through much of the early and middle rounds. His advantage grew in the 10th when a right hand behind the ear dropped the champion.

Moore rose quickly, but referee Ruby Goldstein continued counting, overlooking that the automatic eight-count had been waived for the championship fight. Moore recovered and continued pursuing Johnson.

The challenger remained in front as the fight moved into the late rounds. Two officials had Johnson leading after 13, putting Moore in danger of losing his championship on the scorecards.

Then Moore changed the fight. He hurt Johnson late in the 13th and attacked immediately when the 14th began. A barrage of rights and lefts drove Johnson into his own corner before sending him to the canvas.

Johnson regained his feet, but he was badly hurt. Moore followed him along the ropes and continued punching until Goldstein stopped the fight at 56 seconds of the 14th round.

The comeback preserved Moore’s championship and extended his winning streak to 19 fights. Johnson had come within two rounds of taking the title from a rival he had first fought in 1949.

Moore soon resumed his pursuit of heavyweight champion Rocky Marciano. He received the opportunity the following year, dropping Marciano before being stopped in the ninth round.

Johnson never received the sixth Moore fight he wanted. Years later, he became light heavyweight champion himself.

Their August 1954 battle closed a five-fight rivalry with its most dramatic ending. Johnson had the lead, but the Old Mongoose found the punches he needed before time ran out.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Escalates Fury-Joshua Fight Over MSG
Sports.content:
“We signed for this fight in the UK,” Hearn said to Fighthype. “We are desperate to deliver this fight for UK fans. However, everybody else wants the fight in America: Turki Alalshikh, Netflix. I can’t speak on behalf of Tyson Fury; I don’t see him kicking up a fuss. Madison Square Garden. So, they’re telling us this is the place it’s going to do the biggest numbers, this is the place it’ll be the biggest fight.”

Hearn has made his preference for Britain clear for weeks. What changes the discussion is how far he now sounds prepared to push the disagreement.

“I disagree. But at the end we’ll fight, and we’ll fight, and we’ll fight to a point where they’ve breached the contract by doing it in America, or we come to an agreement.”

That is strong language considering Hearn’s business relationship with Alalshikh and the number of major events Matchroom has staged with his involvement.

Hearn also admits the people on the other side of the venue dispute are key allies, making his willingness to discuss a potential breach of agreement more surprising.

His stated reason is loyalty to British boxing fans. But if Madison Square Garden really produces the bigger commercial event, Hearn’s resistance becomes harder to explain purely as a business decision.

There is also no indication that Fury shares Hearn’s resistance to New York. Hearn concedes he doesn’t see Fury “kicking up a fuss” about Madison Square Garden, potentially leaving Matchroom as the strongest opposition to the proposed move.

The dispute has therefore moved beyond a simple choice between Britain and New York. Hearn is now openly discussing how far Matchroom will go to enforce the agreement it signed.

Sports.title: Conor Benn Embraces Underdog Role Against Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Eubank was already in his mid-30s for those fights, yet bookmakers still favored him. That was understandable given how thin Benn’s resume was against top opposition before their rivalry.

The rematch also came with weight conditions affecting the naturally larger Eubank. More importantly, Eubank wasn’t the type of dangerous one-punch counterpuncher Benn will encounter against Garcia.

His previous opponent did much of his damage through combinations and was no longer at his peak. Garcia presents a different threat with a lightning-fast left hook that has produced some of his biggest knockdowns.

Benn’s aggressive style gives Garcia opportunities to land that shot. Charging forward into exchanges worked in earlier bouts, but those attacks can put him directly in range of Garcia’s best weapon.

The September fight will test Benn’s assertion that he performs best when doubted. This isn’t another meeting with an aging veteran. He’s facing a dangerous puncher in his own division with the exact weapon to punish the aggression he relies on.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Faces Oliver Zaren October 8
Sports.content:
The matchup gives Iglesias a challenger who has yet to lose as a professional. Zaren is 19-0 with one draw and seven knockouts and has spent most of his career fighting in Europe.

Iglesias, 15-0 with 14 knockouts, captured the vacant IBF title by stopping Pavel Silyagin in the eighth round in April in Montreal. The Cuban southpaw had already established himself as one of the division’s biggest punchers before winning the belt.

Zaren had been linked to Iglesias several weeks ago after withdrawing from negotiations for a European title fight against Jose Luis Navarro. Those talks never produced a fight, opening the door for his first world title opportunity.

The fight also keeps Iglesias at super middleweight after a possible meeting with WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames failed to come together earlier this year.

Zaren faces a massive jump in competition. Iglesias has stopped 14 of his 15 professional opponents, including Silyagin, Petro Ivanov and Evgeny Shvedenko.

The Danish challenger has never faced anyone with Iglesias’ combination of power and experience at this level. Zaren will have to prove quickly that his success against European opposition prepared him for a champion who has rarely needed the scorecards.

Sports.title: WBC Blocks Carlos Adames From Denzel Bentley Fight
Sports.content:
That restriction rules out an immediate fight with Denzel Bentley. Adames recently called out the newly elevated WBO middleweight champion for a unification, a fight Bentley wanted as well.

Adames had also explored moving to super middleweight to challenge IBF champion Osleys Iglesias. Talks for that match stalled earlier this year, leaving Bentley as the immediate option at 160 pounds.

The sanctioning body has now taken that choice away.

Ramos has been chasing Adames and can secure the fight by defeating Nursultanov. The 25-year-old interim champion earned his position by beating Shane Mosley Jr. last year.

Nursultanov has plenty to gain beyond disrupting Ramos. Victory in September would send the Kazakh contender directly into a championship fight against Adames.

Adames last defended his WBC belt against Austin Williams in March, winning a unanimous decision. His next challenger will now come from the September 19 fight rather than one of the bigger-name alternatives he wanted.

A Bentley unification would have given Adames the opportunity to add a second middleweight championship belt.

The ruling prevents Adames from taking a voluntary defense while he waits. He must sit tight until Ramos and Nursultanov determine who gets him next.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs. Lucas Bahdi Get Another Week to Avoid Purse Bid
Sports.content:
“The purse bid for the vacant WBA Lightweight World Championship bout between Floyd Schofield and Lucas Bahdi, which was scheduled to take place this Tuesday, August 11, has been postponed at the request of both parties, who asked for additional time as they continue working toward an agreement,” the WBA stated Monday.

For Schofield, 23, this is a valuable opening in a lightweight division filled with difficult fights. He can become a world champion without having to go through WBC champion William Zepeda, WBO champion Abdullah Mason, or IBF champion Raymond Muratalla. At this stage of his career, getting a direct title opportunity without first eliminating another top contender is about as favorable a position as Schofield could want.

Bahdi has his own opportunity. The Canadian made his biggest impression by knocking out Ashton Sylve in the fifth round in July 2024. He now has the chance to turn that victory into something considerably bigger.

The fact that both camps requested the extension is encouraging for the fight getting made. They have until August 18 to complete an agreement before the purse-bid process resumes.

Ghana News.title: UAE donates US$1m relief items to support Ghana’s June 29 flood victims
Ghana News.content:
The Government of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has donated relief items valued at US$1 million to the Government of Ghana to support communities affected by the devastating floods of June 29.

The donation, made through UAE AID, included essential food and household supplies such as cooking oil, sardines, spaghetti, rice, beans, gari, sachet water, mattresses, and blankets.

Welcoming the UAE delegation, the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, Seidu Issifu, expressed profound appreciation on behalf of the President of Ghana, John Dramani Mahama, and the people of Ghana for the generous humanitarian assistance.

He said the UAE’s swift response demonstrated the longstanding friendship, solidarity, and cooperation between Ghana and the UAE.

According to him, the timely assistance would provide much-needed relief to communities affected by the floods, while further strengthening the longstanding bilateral relations between the two countries.

Presenting the relief items, the Executive Director for Operations of UAE AID, Rashid Al Shamsi, said the UAE considered Ghana a home and remained committed to supporting the country during difficult times.

“We believe in shared responsibility, and at this time, we want to share that responsibility by supporting the Government of Ghana,” he said.

Receiving the items on behalf of the government, the Deputy Minister for the Interior, Ebenezer Okletey Terlabi, commended the government and people of the UAE for the gesture.

He also acknowledged the role of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) in coordinating the national disaster response.

Mr Terlabi emphasised that effective disaster prevention, preparedness, and response required collective action from the government, communities, individuals, institutions, development partners, and other stakeholders.

The Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs, James Gyakye Quayson, also expressed appreciation to the government and people of the UAE, describing the donation as a further demonstration of the strong and enduring relations between Ghana and the UAE.

The ceremony was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of the Interior, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, NADMO, and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly, among other stakeholders.

Ghana News.title: Government support needed to boost recycling investments – AGI
Ghana News.content:
Dr Abaidoo

A member of the Plastic Sector of the Association of Ghana Industries is calling for increased government support and incentives to enable businesses to expand their operations and make greater investments in recycling infrastructure.

Speaking at the JoyNews/IMANI Africa National Dialogue on Plastic Waste Management, Dr Paa Kwesi Eduaful Abaidoo said companies established through their association were already engaged in recycling activities and were prepared to support efforts to expand the industry.

He said the major concern was how to incentivise businesses to move into recycling on a larger scale and diversify their investments into recycling facilities and related enterprises.

“We have companies set up through our association which are basically engaged and focused on recycling activities. In terms of our preparedness and understanding, we are all for it,” he said on August 11.

However, Dr Abaidoo noted that the sector required adequate financial support from government to enable companies to build their capacity and invest in the infrastructure needed to sustain large-scale recycling.

“The issue is about how we can also be incentivised for our members to go into recycling full scale, so that we'll be able to re-diversify our investment into facilities and businesses that will be able to supply,” he said.

According to him, appropriate incentives would encourage more private-sector players to commit resources to recycling and help create the capacity required to meet growing demand for recycling services and facilities.

He therefore urged government to provide the necessary financial support to strengthen the capacity of businesses operating in the sector.

“We need that support from the government to ensure that our capacities in terms of the financial are built correctly,” he added.

Dr Abaidoo expressed optimism that the concerns raised would be communicated to the relevant government authorities for consideration as part of efforts to develop the recycling industry.

He said stronger collaboration between government and private-sector operators would be critical to creating a sustainable and commercially viable recycling sector in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Post trained teachers to private schools to reduce unemployment – GNAT to government
Ghana News.content:
The Secretary of the Greater Kumasi chapter of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), Argin Frimpong, has called on the government and the Ministry of Education to consider posting trained teachers to private schools as part of measures to reduce teacher unemployment in the country.

According to him, thousands of teachers graduate from training institutions every year, but many of them remain unemployed due to the lack of government postings.

He said posting some of the trained teachers to private schools would not only provide them with employment opportunities but also enable them to utilise the knowledge and skills acquired during their training.

Speaking to the media at the sixth graduation ceremony of Moldgold School, Mr Frimpong proposed that the government could collaborate with private schools and support them with part of the salaries of teachers posted to the institutions.

“We, the GNAT, want the government to post some of the trained teachers to private schools to enable them to contribute to quality education and reduce the unemployment rate, because most graduates are still at home,” he said.

He noted that private schools play a significant role in Ghana’s education sector and urged the Ministry of Education and the government to prioritise them in the teacher-posting system.

Meanwhile, the Director of Moldgold School, Abigail Yayarah Karikari, has called on the government to support private schools with Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) equipment to promote skills-based education.

She said the world was increasingly becoming technology- and skills-driven, making it necessary for children to acquire practical skills to prepare them for the future.

“The world is developing technologically and in terms of skills, and our children need these skills and knowledge to prepare for their future,” she said.

Madam Karikari also highlighted some of the challenges confronting private schools, including inadequate textbooks, and appealed to the government to extend support to the sector.

The graduation ceremony also featured performances by pupils who showcased their talents, drawing cheers and applause from their parents and other guests.

Ghana News.title: Republic Bank, Multimedia Group renew Habitat Fair partnership for three years
Ghana News.content:
Republic Bank Ghana has renewed its partnership with the Multimedia Group, signing a three-year agreement to become the title sponsor of the firm's Habitat Fair programme.

Speaking at the launch of the Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair on August 11, the General Manager of Joy Brands at The Multimedia Group Limited, Francis Fiifi Koomson, said the partnership builds on an existing relationship between Republic Bank and the Multimedia Group, which began three years ago when the bank became the title sponsor of the Habitat Fair.

He said the successful collaboration had recently resulted in the extension of the partnership for another five years, describing the development as a strong indication that the relationship was yielding positive results.

“Three years ago, Republic Bank became the title sponsor of the Habitat Fair of our commercial brands. That was a very exciting time, and we've had a very exciting journey,” he said.

Mr Koomson noted that the latest agreement further strengthens the partnership, particularly in the Accra market.

“With the same spirit, we sign a further three-year partnership for the Accra brands with Republic Bank. That makes Republic Bank the title sponsor of the entire Habitat Fair portfolio of the Multimedia Group nationwide,” he added.

He described the renewed partnership as a “statement of confidence” in the Multimedia Group, assuring Republic Bank of the company’s commitment to deepening and expanding the relationship in the years ahead.

“We do not take this lightly. We look forward to building this partnership and growing it further into the years ahead,” he said.

Ghana News.title: The GSA Vehicle Directive: Let us focus on the real issue
Ghana News.content:
As the media and social media debate around the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) directive begins to settle, it is important to clarify some of the issues being raised by those arguing for and against it.

This is my second submission on the directive.

One of the most common arguments is that a well-maintained, high-mileage car can be better than a poorly maintained, low-mileage one. Others argue that a vehicle driven mainly on highways will be in better condition than one that has spent its life in stop-and-go city traffic.

In isolation, these arguments sound reasonable. But dig a little deeper, and they begin to fall apart.

Buying a Salvage Car Is Often a Gamble

The true condition of a salvage vehicle sitting at an auction yard in a distant country can be difficult to establish, even for the most experienced buyer in Ghana.

A low-mileage car that has been parked for a long time may have its own problems. But how do you verify how long it has been sitting?

A high-mileage, one-owner vehicle may have been carefully maintained. But again, how do you verify that?

In many cases, buyers are making decisions based on a few photographs, a short auction description and limited vehicle-history information. That is a huge gamble.

Mileage Still Matters

You can reduce the importance placed on mileage when buying a used car, but you cannot completely remove it from the discussion. Mileage is one of the main indicators of how much a vehicle has been used, although it must never be considered on its own.

Vehicle servicing and maintenance are largely determined by mileage. Manufacturers provide schedules showing when specific maintenance work must be carried out.

The most common and relatively inexpensive items include engine oil, air filters, fuel filters and cabin filters. At higher mileage, however, vehicles may require far more expensive repairs and replacements.

These can include major engine, transmission, suspension, emissions-control and electronic components. In some cases, the combined cost of parts, labour and servicing may be higher than the value of the vehicle itself.

Such a car may be accident-free, but it could still be a financial time bomb.

Truly good, high-mileage cars are like diamonds. They exist, but they are not as common as people make them sound.

Depending on where and how a car has been used, a 10-year-old vehicle can easily have covered between 120,000 and 200,000 kilometres or more. At that stage, even a properly maintained car may become expensive to own.

It may be cheap to buy, but costly to keep. With such a vehicle, your mechanic could quickly become your best friend.

Maintenance Is the Missing Ingredient

A high-mileage car can be good. A low-mileage car can be bad.

The factor that can change either situation is maintenance.

The real question is: How do you establish the maintenance history of a vehicle you are buying without seeing or inspecting it properly?

How much confidence can you place in a few pictures on an auction website?

This is why age and mileage alone cannot tell the complete story. The history of the vehicle, how it was used, how it was maintained and the quality of previous repairs are equally important.

The 10-Year Limit Is a Reasonable Compromise

In my view, the 10-year limit is a reasonable compromise, although it needs carefully considered exemptions for categories such as vintage, exotic, enthusiast and motorsport vehicles, as stated in my previous article.

The real secret sauce is inspection.

If Ghana gets the inspection process right, the directive could protect buyers, improve the quality of vehicles entering the country and reduce the carnage on our roads.

Inspection must be rigorous, transparent and professionally managed. It should not become another system filled with bottlenecks, inconsistencies or opportunities for corruption.

Where the Real Fight Should Be

Instead of fighting only about the age of imported vehicles, we should encourage and support our leaders to focus on two important areas.

First, support companies assembling vehicles in Ghana.

The current policy should be fine-tuned to gradually move the industry from vehicle assembly to local component production, with a clear long-term target of full vehicle manufacturing.

Second, introduce government-backed, locally driven vehicle leasing.

Ghanaians need affordable and accessible financing options for new and locally assembled vehicles.

No one should have to pay cash for a new car in 2026.

Without proper financing and leasing systems, locally assembled vehicles will remain beyond the reach of many ordinary Ghanaians, no matter how good the policy sounds on paper.

Salvage Dealers Must Prepare for the Future

To dealers who currently depend on imported salvage vehicles: support the directive.

The world as you know it is changing, really fast.

Use your networks and associations to advocate for stronger local vehicle assembly and affordable financing. This can create a new and more sustainable source of vehicles for your customers.

Do not automatically see the directive as an attempt to destroy your businesses.

Every new car sold today will eventually become a used car. Within five years, many of these vehicles will enter the secondary market, and experienced used-car dealers will be well positioned to sell them.

Mechanics who specialise in rebuilding imported salvage vehicles should also begin diversifying. There will be opportunities in maintaining and repairing locally assembled vehicles, supporting dealerships and serving the growing secondary market.

The industry is not necessarily disappearing. It is changing.

The Bottom Line

Whatever vehicle you are buying, its history matters more than age or mileage alone.

What matters is how the car was used, how it was maintained, whether it was properly repaired and whether its condition can be independently verified.

The GSA directive is not perfect, but it is a step in the right direction. The conversation should now move beyond simply supporting or opposing the age limit.

The real questions are whether Ghana can build a trustworthy inspection system, make locally assembled vehicles affordable and create financing options that give ordinary people access to safer cars.

That is where the debate should be.

Ghana News.title: Photos: JoyNews, IMANI Africa drive national conversation on Ghana’s plastic waste management
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews, in collaboration with IMANI Africa, held a national dialogue on Ghana’s plastic waste management, focusing on the sustainability of the country’s Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework.

The dialogue brought together key stakeholders, including experts from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), policymakers, representatives of the Association of Ghana Industries (AGI), and other industry players, to examine challenges surrounding plastic waste management and explore sustainable solutions.

The dialogue provided a platform for stakeholders to assess existing policies, identify gaps in implementation, and discuss practical measures to improve plastic waste management in Ghana.

Participants also discussed the need for stronger collaboration among government agencies, producers, importers, industry players, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure the effective implementation of the EPR framework.

The engagement formed part of efforts to address Ghana’s growing plastic waste challenge and promote more sustainable approaches to the management of plastic products and packaging throughout their lifecycle.

Ghana News.title: Republic Bank Ghana, JoyNews launch 2026 Habitat Fair
Ghana News.content:
David Max-Fugar, General Manager for Sales, Multimedia Group and Managing Director of Republic Bank Ghana, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku signing MoU.

Republic Bank Ghana and JoyNews, a member of the Multimedia Group Limited, have launched the 2026 Habitat Fair, with Republic Bank coming on board as the lead sponsor.

The JoyNews Habitat Fair is an annual housing and lifestyle exhibition that brings together stakeholders across Ghana’s housing sector, including financial institutions, developers, homeowners and service providers.

Speaking at the launch, Manager in charge of Mortgages at Republic Bank Ghana, Frank Oppong Yeboah, advised prospective homeowners to build according to their income and financial capacity rather than take on excessive debt to complete expensive homes at once.

“You don't just go about taking a loan and developing a four-bedroom, two-storey house,” he said.

“You can decide to have one bedroom, living and dining, with all the facilities, and then as you progress, or as your income increases, you add on,” he added.

Mr Yeboah said a gradual approach to homeownership could help individuals avoid placing unnecessary pressure on their finances.

Managing Director of Republic Bank Ghana, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku, also identified affordability as one of the biggest challenges confronting Ghana’s housing sector.

According to him, the challenge goes beyond the availability of housing units, particularly as population growth and urbanisation continue to increase demand.

“The challenge is not the supply side, but affordability,” he said.

Dr Dzoboku noted that Ghana’s housing deficit, estimated at 1.8 million units in 2015, had been compounded by rapid population growth and urbanisation.

He said addressing the housing gap would require stronger collaboration among government, financial institutions, developers and other stakeholders in the sector.

“Closing this gap will require a concerted effort, not only from one institution or two institutions, but all stakeholders,” he stressed.

General Manager of Joy Brands at Multimedia Group Limited, Francis Fiifi Koomson, welcomed the partnership and expressed confidence that it would contribute positively to Ghana’s housing industry while creating opportunities for both organisations.

As part of the launch, Multimedia Group’s General Manager for Sales, David Max-Fugar, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Republic Bank Ghana to formalise the partnership.

The partnership is expected to support activities leading to this year’s Habitat Fair later in 2026.

Ghana News.title: Republic Bank becomes title sponsor of JoyNews Habitat Fair
Ghana News.content:
Republic Bank Ghana has become the new title sponsor of the JoyNews Habitat Fair, following the signing of a three-year partnership agreement with the Multimedia Group Limited.

The agreement, signed at the headquarters of Republic Bank in Accra on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, covers all Habitat Fair events across Multimedia Group brands and locations nationwide.

The partnership builds on an existing relationship between Republic Bank and the Multimedia Group, with the bank having served as title sponsor of the Habitat Fair organised by Luv FM in Kumasi for the past three years.

Fiifi Koomson, General Manager of Joy Brands at Multimedia Group, said the success of the Kumasi collaboration made the expansion a natural next step.

"Three years ago, Republic Bank became the title sponsor of the Habitat Fair of Kumasi brands, Luv FM. That was a very exciting time, and we've had a very exciting journey," he said.

Mr Koomson described the new agreement as a "statement of confidence" in the Multimedia Group, adding that the Accra brands are covered for an initial three years.

Making homeownership achievable

Managing Director of Republic Bank Ghana, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku, said the partnership comes at a time when Ghana continues to grapple with a significant housing deficit, with affordability remaining one of the biggest obstacles to homeownership.

He noted that Ghana's housing deficit was estimated at about 1.8 million housing units in 2015, with rapid urbanisation and population growth continuing to widen the gap.

According to him, the challenge goes beyond the availability of housing units.

"The challenge is not the supply side but affordability," he said, citing low household incomes, borrowing costs and land litigation among the major barriers confronting prospective homeowners.

Dr Dzoboku stressed that addressing Ghana's housing challenge would require a concerted effort involving government, financial institutions, developers, the media and other stakeholders.

Housing finance in Republic Bank's DNA

He said housing finance has been central to Republic Bank's identity since its origins as a home finance company in 1990.

"Republic Bank financing of housing, as you all know, is not a side business. It is part of our gene," he said.

The bank, he explained, has evolved from a mortgage-focused home finance company into a commercial bank, but has retained its expertise and commitment to helping Ghanaians achieve their homeownership ambitions.

Range of home financing options

Dr Dzoboku said Republic Bank currently offers a range of products designed to support customers at different stages of the homeownership journey.

These include financing for buying, building and owning a home, home completion and improvement, home equity financing, pension-backed mortgages and other housing finance solutions.

He also highlighted the bank's involvement in the National Housing Scheme with the government, through which it has supported public sector workers to acquire homes.

Beyond homeownership, he said Republic Bank had also established a Real Estate Investment Fund in 1995, providing an avenue for people interested in investing in the real estate sector.

He described the bank's approach to housing as an ecosystem that enables Ghanaians to save, invest, build, buy and create security for their families.

Habitat Fair goes nationwide

Dr Dzoboku welcomed the expansion of the Habitat Fair partnership beyond Accra and Kumasi to give more Ghanaians access to information and opportunities around housing.

He said the national reach would allow people in different parts of the country to engage financial institutions, developers and other players in the housing sector.

"So if you are a nurse in Accra, or a teacher in Zebila, or an entrepreneur in Ho, you can also have your dream home through this fair," he said.

He encouraged prospective homeowners not to abandon their aspirations because of financial or other challenges.

"Do not abandon your dream of owning a home. Come to Republic Bank Ghana. Let us understand your circumstances. We have various options and we can chart the right path for you," he said.

He described the Habitat Fair as an important platform for stakeholders in the housing ecosystem to engage directly with prospective homeowners, answer their questions and provide practical solutions.

Habitat Fair expands to Ho

General Manager, Sales at the Multimedia Group, Max Fugar, who signed the agreement on behalf of the company, described the development as a return of the Habitat Fair "home" under a new national partnership with Republic Bank.

He announced that the Habitat Fair will be held in Accra, Kumasi and Ho, expanding its reach to the Volta Region this year.

"Joy News Habitat Fair is back home. Republic Bank is now the lead sponsor of Joy News Habitat Fair. Accra, Kumasi, and Ho," Mr Fugar said.

He expressed appreciation to Republic Bank for its support and assured the bank that the Multimedia Group would deliver on the partnership.

Habitat Fair Clinic to begin at Achimota Mall

As part of activities leading to the main fair, Mr Fugar announced that the Habitat Fair Clinic will be held at Achimota Mall from August 21 to 23.

The clinic will provide an opportunity for prospective homeowners to engage directly with exhibitors and experts, including Republic Bank, on financing and other aspects of homeownership.

He encouraged members of the public to take advantage of the clinic and subsequent engagements across Multimedia Group platforms to seek answers to their housing and financing questions.

The signing ceremony was broadcast live on Joy FM and Joy News, as well as the organisation's digital platforms.

The partnership between Republic Bank and the Multimedia Group is expected to strengthen the Habitat Fair as a platform connecting prospective homeowners with financial institutions, developers, construction companies and other players across Ghana's housing ecosystem.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: What to watch in Wisconsin’s high-stakes primary
World.content:
US Democrats face another test after Michigan as voters choose nominees for governor and Congress.

A week after progressives scored a victory in Michigan’s US Senate primary, Democrats face another test, this time in the Upper Midwestern US state of Wisconsin.

Voters in the battleground state head to the polls on Tuesday in a primary that will help shape races for governor and all eight US House of Representatives seats in November, as well as the Wisconsin State Assembly and half of the State Senate.

But the biggest spotlight is on the Democratic contest for governor, which has become another proxy battle between the party’s progressive wing and its more moderate establishment.

The results will not only shape Wisconsin politics, but also could offer clues about where Democratic voters want the party to go ahead of November’s United States midterm elections.

Why is Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor so important?

Wisconsin is the next major test after progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated establishment-backed US Representative Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday, renewing questions about whether Democratic voters are moving further left.

This year’s primaries have repeatedly seen outsider candidates outperform establishment favourites, reflecting frustration among many Democratic voters after the party’s losses in the 2024 presidential election and an internal debate happening over US support for Israel. While progressive candidates have won against establishment ones in heavily Democratic states like New York or Colorado, there have been questions about whether more leftist candidates can succeed in US states, like Michigan or Wisconsin, where both Democratic and Republican candidates can have a similar level of support. US President Donald Trump won both Michigan and Wisconsin in the 2024 US presidential election after former US President Joe Biden won them in 2020.



Wisconsin will be closely watched for whether the trend of progressive wins continues.

Whoever wins will likely face Republican Representative Tom Tiffany, a Trump ally who has already been framing the race as a choice between what he calls a “socialist agenda” and “common sense”.

Who are Francesca Hong and David Crowley?

The Democratic race for the gubernatorial nominee in Wisconsin has narrowed to two very different candidates.

State Representative Francesca Hong is a lawmaker, former restaurant worker and democratic socialist who, if elected, would become Wisconsin’s first woman governor and first Asian American governor.

Hong’s campaign has focused on issues like free childcare, cancelling student debt, and abolishing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She’s also faced scrutiny over past social media posts, including ones supporting Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) policies such as abolishing the US Senate and abolishing or defunding police. She’s since distanced herself from some of those positions, saying she doesn’t support the national DSA’s full platform and has pledged not to cut police budgets. Hong has emphasised that she’s a member of the local DSA chapter in Madison, Wisconsin, but not a national member.

Hong, who has been endorsed by Minnesota Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar and has campaigned alongside left-wing commentator Hasan Piker, has also described Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide, advocated for Palestinian rights and called for repealing a Wisconsin law that bars state agencies from contracting with companies that boycott Israel.

Her main opponent, David Crowley, is the Milwaukee County executive, the chief public official for the county, who initially dropped out of the race and re-entered 10 days later, in mid-July, after being endorsed by outgoing Governor Tony Evers. The endorsement quickly cemented Crowley as the establishment favourite, with supporters arguing he’s the strongest candidate to keep the governor’s office in Democratic hands.

Crowley, however, has insisted he isn’t an establishment democrat and that he considers the term a “slur”. He is also hoping to make history as Wisconsin’s first Black governor and said he intends to focus on undecided voters.

A Marquette University Law School poll of Wisconsin Democratic primary voters conducted in late July showed Hong with a significant lead in the race.

Why has the governor’s primary been so chaotic?

Lieutenant Governor Sara Rodriguez was the first major Democrat to drop out after a campaign finance controversy. Former Wisconsin Economic Development Corporation CEO Missy Hughes later ended her campaign, further narrowing the field.



Then, less than two weeks before election day, former Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes withdrew after allegations of inappropriate behaviour resurfaced during the campaign. Barnes denied any wrongdoing, and a review commissioned by the Wisconsin Democratic Party found no actionable evidence because the allegations were anonymous and lacked specific details, according to the Associated Press.

Crowley then re-entered the race, following the endorsement of outgoing Governor Evers.

Because all of the withdrawals came after Wisconsin’s filing deadline, the candidates remain on the ballot. Almost 128,000 absentee ballots have already been returned, meaning many voters had cast ballots for candidates who were no longer actively campaigning. A judge later rejected a lawsuit that was seeking to have the absentee ballots cancelled and allow voters to vote again.

What are other races to watch?

In western Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District, Democrats are choosing between Rebecca Cooke – a nonprofit executive and the party’s 2024 nominee, who came within about three percentage points of defeating Republican Representative Derrick Van Orden – and Emily Berge, the former president of the Eau Claire City Council. The winner will face Van Orden in November in one of the country’s most competitive House races, and one Democrats see as one of their best opportunities to flip a Republican-held seat.

An additional race to watch is in the state’s 7th Congressional District. The race has largely centred on Michael Alfonso, the 26-year-old son-in-law of US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who has Trump’s endorsement. He faces several competitors, including Jessi Ebben, a manufacturing strategist and grassroots Trump organiser who has campaigned on border security, expanding American manufacturing and protecting gun rights, and Kevin Hermening, a former US Marine who was one of 66 Americans held hostage by Iran for 444 days starting in 1979.

The district is expected to remain safely Republican, meaning the primary winner will be heavily favoured in November. Democrats are also choosing between Chris Armstrong, former state Representative Fred Clark and Ginger Murray for their party’s nomination.

When do polls open and close?

Polls are open from 7am to 8pm local time (12:00-01:00 GMT on Tuesday-Wednesday).
