World.title: Salary hike: Tinubu should ensure direct transfer for military – Ndume
World.content:
Ndume

By John Alechenu

Former Senate Leader, Ali Ndume, has commended President Bola Tinubu for approving salary increases for about 250,000 personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces, saying the move will go a long way to boost the morale of troops.

President Tinubu last week approved salary increases of between 30 and 80 per cent for military personnel. The new rates take effect next month.

With the adjustment, the annual wage bill for the Armed Forces will rise from N660 billion to N924 billion. Officers above the rank of colonel -brigadier-generals, major-generals, lieutenant-generals and generals – will get 30 per cent increase.

Those from colonel down to warrant officer will get 50 per cent, while personnel from private to staff sergeant will get 80 per cent.

In a statement in Abuja on Tuesday, Ndume, who once chaired the Senate Committee on Army, said the salary review shows the President has a clear plan to tackle insecurity.

He said, “This coming after his recent expansion of military divisions from eight to 12 shows that Mr. President has his own blueprint aimed at dealing with the scourge of terrorism and banditry.

“The review of salary will go a long way in motivating our military personnel. I have been in the vanguard of better motivation for our men and officers in the military in terms of decent living wage.

“President Tinubu has once again proved that he is a responsive leader who doesn’t shut his mind to genuine and legitimate agitation of Nigerians.”

However, the Borno South Senator noted that better pay alone will not win the war against insurgency. He urged the government to also ensure prompt supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics.

Ndume said, “I have always argued that aside better welfare package and training, what they need to deal with insurgents is prompt supply of arms and ammunition.

“I also want to urge Mr. President to keep up his pledge on the provision of weapons and technological tools required to the Armed Forces to effectively discharge their duties.”

The APC Chieftain called for the annual defence budget to be placed on First Line Charge to remove bureaucratic delays.

According to him, “All these can be achieved seamlessly if we put their annual budget on First Line Charge. This envelope budgeting is trapped in unnecessary bureaucracy between the Ministry of Defense and Ministry of Finance. It is a big encumbrance to effective operations of our men and officers in the war theater.

“Mr. President should seize the initiative to ensure direct statutory transfer from the Federation Account for the military as it is done with few agencies of government.”

World.title: ECOWAS to offer $65,000 to Nigerian startups — How to apply
World.content:
The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has opened applications for its 2026 Startup Awards, with a total cash prize of $65,000 up for grabs among the top three startups.

The second edition of the ECOWAS Startup Awards is designed to identify, celebrate and support high-impact startups contributing to digital transformation, regional integration and sustainable value-chain development across West Africa.

The programme is being convened by the ECOWAS Commission’s Directorate of Private Sector and Industry, hosted in Abuja and jointly implemented by the Pan African Alliance of Small and Medium Industries (PAOSMI) and the Investment Promotion Agencies of West African States (IPAWAS).

The initiative follows the inaugural edition held in Niamey, Niger, on November 18 and 19, 2021.

The 2026 edition is expected to bring together 60 startups from ECOWAS Member States and will feature masterclasses, startup clinics, pitch competitions, exhibitions, investor deal rooms, policy dialogues and post-award acceleration.

How much can startups win?

The competition has a total cash prize of $65,000, divided among the top three startups.

Winner — $30,000

First runner-up — $20,000

Second runner-up — $15,000

Beyond the cash prizes, selected startups will receive regional exposure across the ECOWAS bloc, investor introductions, networking opportunities with founders and policymakers, mentorship and a six-month acceleration programme.

They will also have access to digital tools, including computers, accessories and software.

Six sectors eligible for the awards

Applications are open to startups operating in six strategic sectors:

1. EdTech

Startups focused on education technology and skills development.

2. FinTech

Businesses developing technology-driven financial products and services.

3. HealthTech

Startups using technology to improve healthcare delivery and related services.

4. AgriTech

Businesses working in agricultural technology and food systems.

5. CleanTech

Startups focused on clean technology, climate solutions and green innovation.

6. TravelTech

Businesses operating in tourism, hospitality and travel technology.

Who can apply?

Applicants must meet six eligibility requirements to participate in the competition.

They must:

Be a citizen of an ECOWAS Member State. Operate a startup that is registered and based within an ECOWAS country. Have been operating for at least two years. Have a working product or service. Demonstrate market traction or scalability. Submit all required documentation.

What documents are required?

Applicants are expected to prepare the following documents and materials before beginning the application:

A completed application form covering Sections A–J.

A national passport or ECOWAS-approved identity document for the lead founder, in PDF or image format and not exceeding 10MB.

A recent colour passport photograph of not more than 5MB.

Business registration certificate issued in an ECOWAS Member State, where applicable.

Two years of financial statements, management accounts or projections.

A business plan of no more than 10 pages, single-spaced and written in Times New Roman, size 12.

A pitch deck of no more than 10 slides.

A one-minute pitch video in MP4, MOV or WebM format, with a maximum file size of 100MB.

How will startups be selected?

The selection process will take place in two phases.

National selection

Each ECOWAS Member State will nominate half of its allocated slots.

The remaining half will be selected from applications submitted by the general public, meaning startups do not necessarily need a national nomination to secure a place in the competition.

Regional finals

Selected finalists will pitch before an independent regional jury in Abuja.

Winners will be determined based on scoring and consensus, with judges drawn from industry, investment and policy backgrounds.

The organisers said judges will be required to comply with conflict-of-interest and confidentiality policies.

The application portal opened on August 3, 2026, and interested startups have until August 31, 2026, to submit their applications.

The programme will then move into its next stages:

August 3, 2026: Applications open

Applications open August 31, 2026: Application deadline

Application deadline September 21–25, 2026: Virtual masterclasses and startup clinics, beginning at 9:00am

Virtual masterclasses and startup clinics, beginning at 9:00am September 28–30, 2026: Physical event in Abuja featuring pitch competitions, exhibitions and investor deal rooms

Physical event in Abuja featuring pitch competitions, exhibitions and investor deal rooms September 30, 2026: Regional finals and final pitches before the independent jury

How to apply

Eligible startup founders across ECOWAS Member States can apply through the official ECOWAS Startup Awards application portal.

Applicants are advised to have all required documents ready before starting the process. The application form can be saved as applicants progress through it.

The organisers have also published detailed guidelines containing the eligibility rules, application process, selection criteria and other requirements for participants.

Vanguard News

World.title: NFF apologises to President Tinubu, Nigerians over WAFCON setback
World.content:
Super Falcons

By Emmanuel Okogba

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has issued a formal apology to the Federal Government and the people of Nigeria following the Super Falcons’ failure to secure direct qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup at the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON).

In a statement on behalf of the NFF Executive Committee, the Super Falcons and the entire Nigerian football family, NFF President Alhaji Ibrahim Musa Gusau expressed deep regret over the result.

“We recognise the disappointment this result has caused millions of Nigerians who passionately support and identify with the Super Falcons,” Gusau said. “The team went into the competition carrying the hopes of the nation and the enormous goodwill and support of the Federal Government, and we regret that we were unable to deliver the result expected at this stage.”

The NFF extended a special apology to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, noting his strong support for Nigerian sports and women athletes in particular.

“Mr. President has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to Nigerian sports and, particularly, to the development and welfare of women in sports,” the statement said. It recalled the substantial rewards, national honours, houses and reception given to the Super Falcons after their previous WAFCON triumph, as well as continued support for the Super Eagles.

“It is therefore with genuine humility and regret that we acknowledge that we have not been able to repay that confidence with the outcome expected at this stage of the competition. We sincerely apologise to Mr. President and deeply appreciate his continued interest, encouragement and investment in Nigerian football.”

The federation also apologised to the National Assembly, the National Sports Commission, sponsors, stakeholders and Nigerian supporters at home and abroad.

Despite the setback, the NFF said a pathway remains open through the CAF play-offs for two tickets, followed by the FIFA play-off tournament.

“We must now regroup, learn from this setback and focus completely on the opportunity that remains,” Gusau said. “The NFF, technical team and players are committed to doing everything within their power to secure Nigeria’s place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.”

The federation pledged an honest assessment of preparation, technical planning, logistics and overall operations to identify areas for improvement.

“We hear the disappointment of Nigerians, we share it and we accept our responsibility. But we are not giving up,” the statement added. “Our resolve is to ensure that the Super Falcons return stronger, fight harder and do everything possible to make Mr. President, the Federal Government and Nigerians proud once again.”

The NFF thanked Nigerians for their support and urged continued backing for the Super Falcons as they pursue the remaining route to the 2027 World Cup.

World.title: UEFA Super Cup: PSG, Aston Villa set to clash as Somali referee Artan makes history
World.content:
Omar Artan

By Enitan Abdultawab

Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa will battle for the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg, Austria, on Wednesday, with Somali referee Omar Artan set to become the first non-European official to take charge of the prestigious fixture.

The annual encounter pits the reigning Champions League winners against the Europa League champions, with PSG seeking to become only the second team in the modern era to successfully defend the title after Real Madrid achieved the feat in 2016 and 2017.

PSG defeated Tottenham Hotspur on penalties in last year’s final.

However, Artan’s appointment has added another layer of interest to Wednesday’s game after the 34-year-old was prevented from officiating at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States.

Artan was among the officials selected for the tournament but was barred from entering the US days before the competition began. US officials cited vetting and national security concerns, including alleged links to terrorist organisations, although no evidence was publicly provided.

UEFA subsequently selected Artan to referee the Super Cup, a decision that has been widely welcomed within the football community.

The appointment comes after Artan was recognised as Africa’s leading referee last season. He also officiated the 2025 African Champions League final.

Reflecting on the difficult period surrounding his World Cup exclusion, Artan said the experience had been challenging but expressed gratitude for the support he received.

“A lot of people have sympathy for me because when someone has been working a lot of years and is supposed to do something, and then can’t do it, it’s very challenging,” he told UEFA.

“I really appreciate the support I received throughout the world, though. I’m so grateful.”

Artan said he had been studying both teams extensively ahead of his first assignment in European football.

“The standard in Europe is fantastic and the football they play is very, very good,” he said.

PSG’s preparations have been influenced by the late return of several of their players who featured prominently at the 2026 World Cup.

Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembélé returned to training on Monday alongside France teammates Désiré Doué and Bradley Barcola. Spain midfielder Fabián Ruiz has also resumed training after helping his country win the World Cup.

Georgian winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, whose country did not qualify for the tournament, has been back in training for longer and is expected to start.

New signing Maghnes Akliouche could also feature, although Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool.

PSG may additionally hand a debut to former Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne, who joined the French club on Sunday for a reported €10m ($11.6m).

Aston Villa, meanwhile, will begin the new campaign with several changes to their squad under manager Unai Emery.

The club lost midfielders Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans to Chelsea and Manchester United respectively, while Digne also departed for PSG.

Villa have brought in Swiss World Cup player Johan Manzambi and Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes from relegated Wolverhampton Wanderers. Manzambi, however, is unavailable because of a knee injury.

Villa booked their place in the Super Cup after defeating Freiburg 3-0 in the Europa League final.

The match will also mark their second Champions League campaign under Emery, who previously coached PSG.

With PSG aiming to add another European trophy and Villa looking to make their mark on the continental stage, Wednesday’s encounter promises a compelling start to the new European season — with Artan at the centre of a historic refereeing moment.

AFP

World.title: Former OnlyFans model sentenced to six years for killing Nigerian man
World.content:
By Adewale Adesewa

Former OnlyFans model Courtney Clenney has been sentenced to six years in prison after pleading guilty to manslaughter in the 2022 killing of her boyfriend and Nigerian man, Christian Obumseli, in Miami, Florida.

Clenney, 30, pleaded guilty on Monday to manslaughter with a deadly weapon as part of a plea agreement that brought an end to a case that had remained in the public spotlight for more than four years.

She was also sentenced to five years of probation after her release.

According to reports by CBS News and Fox News, Clenney will receive credit for the nearly four years she has already spent in custody since her arrest in August 2022. As a result, she is expected to spend about two more years in prison before beginning her probation.

Obumseli, 27, was fatally stabbed on April 3, 2022, inside the Miami apartment he shared with Clenney.

She was initially charged with second-degree murder and had maintained that she acted in self-defence during a confrontation with Obumseli.

Her lawyers had argued that Obumseli was abusive and that Clenney threw a knife at him while trying to protect herself.

Prosecutors, however, presented evidence concerning what they described as a troubled relationship involving repeated domestic conflicts.

Under the plea agreement, the original murder charge was replaced with manslaughter with a deadly weapon.

Miami-Dade prosecutor Shawn Abuhoff told the court that Clenney was accepting responsibility for her actions.

“She is taking criminal responsibility for her action, the state is willing to accept her plea,” Abuhoff said.

The sentence also requires Clenney to undergo mental health and substance abuse evaluations and treatment after her release.

Prosecutors have further said she will not be permitted to financially benefit from the case.

Obumseli’s family addressed the court during the sentencing, describing the lasting pain caused by his death.

His mother, Ocio Obumseli, said the family had continued to struggle with the loss of her son.

“The loss of Christian did not end April 4; we carry it with us every day,” she said.

She also told the court, “Christian, your legacy and your memory will remain with us. We miss you, we love you; may you continue to rest in peace, my son.”

The family’s attorney, Larry Handfield, said the guilty plea provided some measure of closure because the family wanted Clenney to accept responsibility for Obumseli’s death.

“What the family wanted was accountability,” Handfield said.



Miami-Dade State Attorney Katherine Fernandez Rundle also said the agreement allowed Obumseli’s family to hear Clenney accept responsibility for his death.

According to People, the plea agreement was reached in consultation with and with the approval of the family.

The case drew widespread attention because of the couple’s relationship and the conflicting accounts of the events that led to Obumseli’s death.

Clenney, who was also known online as Courtney Tailor, had built a large social media following before her arrest.

The guilty plea ends the criminal case without the second-degree murder trial that had been expected. Clenney will serve the remainder of her six-year sentence before beginning five years of probation.

Vanguard News

World.title: I introduced state policing in Senate — Adeleke
World.content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke

By Nwafor Sunday, Online News Editor

OSOGBO — Accord Party governorship candidate in the Osun State governorship election, Ademola Adeleke, has said he was among those who introduced the idea of state policing in the Senate, expressing confidence that the initiative would work if implemented in the state.

Adeleke stated this on Tuesday during the Arise Townhall Meeting, where he also pledged to uphold the rule of law and ensure that security agencies operate within the confines of the law.

“If you are my son and you break the law, you will go and face the law. I believe in the rule of law. I will make sure state police work in my state. I am not among those that say state police cannot work. It will work,” he said.

On infrastructure, Adeleke said his administration had reconstructed roads that had been abandoned for decades, describing the projects as durable and well executed.

“I have constructed roads abandoned for about 45 years. The roads are superb and clean. They are good roads,” he said.

The Accord Party candidate also dismissed suggestions that he would need to buy votes to win the election, saying his administration had provided palliatives to residents since assuming office.

He accused his political opponents of believing that voters could be influenced with cash during elections.

“I don’t need to buy votes. I have been giving my people palliatives since I came in. They believe they can give ₦20,000 and money to voters in Osun. My people are smarter,” Adeleke said.

He further accused his opponents of contributing to the economic challenges facing the state, alleging that they had “crippled Osun State’s economy” and were now seeking to use money to influence voters.

“My people are smarter,” he added.

Adeleke expressed confidence in his electoral prospects, saying he was certain of victory in the governorship election. “I will not lose this election. I am confident,” he said.

World.title: ‘Oyetola behind freezing of Osun account’, Adeleke alleges
World.content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has alleged that his predecessor Gboyega Oyetola was behind the freezing of the state government’s account by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

Adeleke made the allegation on Tuesday during the Arise Town Hall for Osun governorship candidates ahead of the poll on August 15, accusing Oyetola of using the name of President Bola Tinubu and federal institutions to exert pressure on his administration.

The governor claimed that Oyetola, who now serves as Nigeria’s Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, had been making various demands while allegedly telling government agencies that the President had directed them to act.

“I am sure he (Oyetola) told EFCC to freeze our account, that Mr. President said it should be frozen,” Adeleke said.

He said the situation changed after Tinubu personally contacted him, claiming that the President expressed shock and embarrassment over what had happened.

“So, when Mr President called, a lot of people were shocked. Because when Mr President called, he said he was embarrassed. He said it is not acceptable because I told him, the President, that he would not want democracy to go down; he wants a free and fair election,” Adeleke said.

He further accused Oyetola of exploiting his relationship with Tinubu to pursue political interests in Osun, alleging that his predecessor had not recovered from his defeat in the previous governorship election.

“Oyetola is feeling that pain of defeat. He is only using the President to vow that he will destroy Osun State. He is using federal might,” the governor alleged.

Adeleke and Oyetola have remained political rivals since the 2022 Osun governorship election, which Adeleke won after defeating the then-incumbent Oyetola.

The governor is seeking another term of four years in office.

World.title: 2027: Atiku raises concern over outdated BVAS
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has raised concerns over the alleged use of an outdated operating system on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), warning that it could pose cybersecurity and operational risks ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Paul Ibe disclosed this on his Facebook handle on Tuesday.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), raised the concerns following the reported failures recorded during the Osun State mock accreditation exercise on August 1, 2026, and comments by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Director of ICT, Dr Lawrence Bayode.

Bayode, while speaking on Arise TV on Monday, reportedly said the BVAS, introduced into Nigeria’s electoral process in 2021, currently runs on Android version 10.

In a statement issued by his Media Office in Abuja on Tuesday, Atiku said Android version 10 had reached end-of-life status in 2023 and no longer receives regular updates or security patches.

He argued that running an election technology platform such as BVAS on an outdated operating system could expose the electoral process to cybersecurity and operational vulnerabilities.

Atiku questioned why INEC, with what he described as its substantial budget, had not upgraded the BVAS software ahead of the 2027 general elections or used forthcoming off-cycle elections, including the Osun governorship election, to test an updated version.

He described what he called INEC’s handling of the BVAS issue as “suspicious” and alleged that it could undermine the integrity of the country’s elections.

According to him, vulnerabilities in an outdated operating system could potentially be exploited by cybercriminals to gain unauthorised access to devices and tamper with stored voter accreditation or polling unit result data before transmission.

He also raised concerns about the transmission of polling unit results over public telecommunications networks to the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal.

Atiku said outdated security and cryptographic components could increase exposure to cyber threats, including attempts to intercept, block or manipulate data transmitted between polling units and the result-viewing platform.

The former Vice President further expressed concern about the biometric functions of BVAS, which uses fingerprint and facial recognition for voter accreditation.

He argued that an outdated biometric framework could affect the system’s accuracy and resilience against attempts to circumvent its verification processes.

Atiku also warned that software defects associated with legacy systems could lead to application crashes, particularly during periods of heavy usage, potentially causing delays in voter accreditation.

He said he supported calls by cybersecurity experts for an independent and comprehensive audit of the BVAS hardware and software ahead of the 2027 elections.

According to him, running critical national infrastructure on an end-of-life operating system could create an expanded attack surface and expose the electoral system to avoidable risks.

The statement was signed by the Atiku Media Office, Abuja, on August 11, 2026.

World.title: UBEC Urges States to Fully Utilise Basic Education Funds
World.content:
* Delta reports 90% implementation of 2025 action plan

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) has called on states to ensure full utilisation of available funds and prompt implementation of approved programmes to improve basic education delivery across Nigeria.

The call was made during a courtesy visit to the Delta State Government, represented by Deputy Governor, Monday Onyeme, in Asaba, as part of the 30th quarterly meeting of UBEC management with executive chairmen of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs).

The meeting, themed, ‘Repositioning Basic Education in Nigeria to Optimise Investment and Impact,’ focused on how investments and innovations can translate into better classrooms and learning outcomes.

UBEC commended Delta State for accessing its UBE matching grants up to 2025.

The commission also urged the state to take advantage of the education component of the World Bank-supported HOPE Education Programme, with up to $500 million earmarked for education.

States were told that to qualify, they must access the 2026 matching grant and implement at least 50 per cent of their 2025 Action Plan.

Responding, Onyeme said updated records showed that Delta had about N1 billion in unutilised funds, contrary to the N8 billion earlier reported.

He added that the state had implemented about 90 per cent of its 2025 Action Plan and had already received its 2026 matching grant.

The UBEC team also highlighted Delta’s technology-driven teacher attendance system, Attend360, as a model that could strengthen accountability in basic education nationwide.

“There is no education or quality learning without a good teacher or without a teacher in the classroom,” the executive secretary noted.

During a visit to the Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, UBEC called for stronger collaboration with traditional institutions.

Azinge described basic education as the foundation of Nigeria’s future and urged UBEC and SUBEBs to ensure no child, including those with disabilities and from disadvantaged backgrounds, is left behind.

UBEC assured the Asagba that it will continue working with states to ensure that investments in basic education yield visible impact in classrooms.

World.title: Delta Suspends Works Commissioner over Alleged Assault on Gov’s Aide
World.content:
T6Sylvester Idowu in Warri, Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Delta State Government yesterday suspended the state Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads), Hon. Izeze Rume Yakubu Reuben, with immediate effect.

The suspension, according to a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr. Kingsley Emu, is to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into allegations linking the commissioner to the recent assault of the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Protocol, Mr. Simon Mudi, popularly known as ‘Temple’.

The incident reportedly occurred at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state during the Delta Central meeting of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The SSG said the suspension was necessary to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference and to establish the facts surrounding the incident.

The state government, he said, remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and the sanctity of human lives under all circumstances.

Dr. Emu stressed that the government’s commitment to these principles remained unwavering, even when individuals or institutions of the state were involved.

“The suspension is expected to remain in force pending the outcome of the investigation by the relevant security agencies,” he said.

World.title: NHRC Demands Immediate Arrest, Prosecution of Sheikh Jingir Over Hate Speech
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has called for the immediate arrest and prosecution of prominent Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, over what it described as hateful and inciting remarks capable of aggravating religious tensions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, made the demand after the NHRC reviewed a viral video in which the cleric allegedly canvassed religiously exclusive politics and urged his supporters to obtain their permanent voter cards (PVCs) to “show their limit”.

Ojukwu, who condemned the remarks in strong terms, said the cleric’s reference to people of other faiths as “infidels”, coupled with his political exhortations, constituted a dangerous attempt to mobilise citizens along religious lines.

According to him, the statements amounted to hate speech and incitement to religious hatred, with the potential to trigger violence at a time Nigeria is preparing for another politically sensitive electoral cycle.

The NHRC boss said the remarks were inconsistent with the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and peaceful coexistence, as well as Nigeria’s obligations under international human rights instruments.

“The commission finds these remarks to be hate speech and incitement to religious hatred and potential violence. At a time when we are preparing for another general election, such utterances are reckless and dangerous,” he said.

Ojukwu warned that failure by the authorities to respond decisively could encourage other influential religious and political actors to make increasingly provocative statements as the 2027 elections draw closer.

“We cannot afford to look away. If we fail to speak and act now, we embolden both Christian and Muslim clerics and other influential persons to make worse statements in the coming months. That path leads only to crisis,” he said.

Consequently, the commission called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant authorities to immediately arrest and prosecute Jingir for alleged hate speech and incitement.

The NHRC insisted that any prosecution should be pursued irrespective of the cleric’s status or political affiliation, arguing that equal application of the law was necessary to deter others from exploiting religious sentiments for political purposes.

The commission’s intervention comes as political actors, religious leaders and civil society groups increasingly turn their attention to the potential impact of identity-based mobilisation on the 2027 electoral process.

Ojukwu further urged religious leaders, traditional rulers and politicians to abandon divisive rhetoric and instead encourage Nigerians to assess political leaders on the basis of competence, service delivery, integrity and respect for fundamental human rights.

He also called on Nigerians to reject identity politics and resist attempts to turn religious affiliation into a tool for political mobilisation.

“The commission will continue to monitor compliance and will engage with security agencies, INEC, and civil society to ensure that the 2027 elections are free from hate and violence,” he said.

The NHRC’s position adds a fresh dimension to the growing debate over the role of religious rhetoric in Nigeria’s electoral politics, particularly as political parties and prospective candidates begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

Jingir has previously been involved in controversies surrounding politically charged religious messaging.

In the run-up to the 2019 general election, he attracted criticism over a video message to followers concerning voting and religious identity.

The latest NHRC intervention therefore places renewed focus on the responsibility of influential religious figures to ensure that political mobilisation does not cross the line into rhetoric capable of threatening peaceful coexistence or electoral stability.

World.title: Journalists Urged to Harness AI to Transform Reporting
World.content:
The future of journalism is being reshaped by Artificial Intelligence (AI), offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance reporting, streamline workflows, and deliver more engaging content to readers worldwide.

The Chief Executive of Chesca Global Solutions Limited, Ms. Franca Ibuzo, stated this in a press statement, noting that “in automated news gathering, AI can scan vast amounts of data, social media feeds, and public records in real time, and help journalists identify breaking stories faster.”

According to her, during fact‑ checking and verification, with misinformation on the rise, AI tools assist in verifying sources, cross‑checking facts, and ensuring accuracy before publication.

She noted that “content personalisation and AI algorithms now tailor news delivery to readers’ interests, improving engagement and ensuring diverse perspectives reach the right audiences.”

Ibuzo added: “Multimedia enhancement, from generating graphics to transcribing interviews, AI reduces repetitive tasks, allowing journalists to focus on news writing.”

“Transcribing and translation are powered by AI, which enables newsrooms to break language barriers, making stories accessible to international audiences instantly.”

She, however, exphasised that “AI is not replacing journalists but rather it is empowering them.

“By leveraging AI responsibly, we can uphold the integrity of journalism while embracing innovation that makes reporting more efficient and impactful.”

“As media organisations adopt AI, ethical considerations remain paramount. Transparency, accountability, and human oversight are essential to ensure that technology strengthens trust rather than undermines it,” she said.

She urged “media organisations management to reiterate their commitment to advancing journalism through innovation by equipping reporters and editors with cutting‑edge tools to deliver credible, timely, and engaging news.”

World.title: NCWS Tasks Women to Vote Wisely, Seeks More Political Positions
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The National Council of Women’s Societies (NCWS) has urged women in Nigeria to mobilise and vote wisely in the 2027 general election in accordance with their conscience.

The President of NCWS, South-West Forum, Mrs. Priscilla Kuye, who made the call in her welcome address at the council’s annual conference held in Ibadan, Oyo State, said women should actively participate in the electoral process and support candidates committed to good governance, the rule of law and promotion of fundamental human rights.

According to her, the council was concerned about insecurity, kidnapping, unemployment, hunger and inadequate access to water and electricity in the country.

“We want good governance and promotion of the rule of law. We want all women and girls to be accorded their fundamental human rights in accordance with our constitution,” she said.

Kuye disclosed that the seminar, which focused on ‘Human Rights, Justice, Action for all Women and Girls in the Society’, was organised to educate women on issues affecting them, particularly ahead of the 2027 elections.

Stating that the conference brought together women from various associations across the South-west geopolitical zone.

In its communiqué, the conference called for the mobilisation and sensitisation of women to vote wisely, while advocating increased representation of women in political positions of responsibility.

The council also urged women to seek more elective and political positions while calling for the empowerment of women through access to low-interest loans to enable them to establish and expand businesses.

The NCWS further encouraged educated women to guide and support less-educated women, while calling on men to stop relegating women to the background in all spheres of life.

It also recommended increased media publicity for the council’s activities, including jingles, interviews, and other platforms to showcase the achievements of its members.

The council proposed the organisation of a mega meeting where political stakeholders and other power brokers would be invited to pledge their support for women.

The communiqué also announced plans to celebrate the centenary birthday of one of the founding mothers of NCWS and its first Secretary-General in 1962, Prof. Adetoun Ogunsheye.

Ogunsheye, according to the council, is Nigeria’s first female professor, and her centenary celebration is scheduled for December 5, 2026.

The NCWS was registered as a society on June 24, 1965, after its formation in Ibadan by women’s organisations seeking to promote women’s education, political participation and economic development.

The organisation has since expanded to all states of Nigeria with a national body.

World.title: Aviation Unions Picket Air Peace Operations, Attack Workers over Refusal to Join Associations
World.content:
*Disrupt over 70 Air Peace domestic, regional flights

*United Nigeria Airlines grounds operations in protest

Chinedu Eze

The National Union of Air Transport Employees (NUATE) and the Air Transport Service Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (ATSSSAN) early Tuesday picketed the operation of Nigeria’s leading carrier, Air Peace, at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, forcing the airline to cancel over 70 daily flights.

The unions said they are protesting against the 5% Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) owed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) but the airlines.

But NCAA had earlier confirmed that it had made agreed payment arrangement with the airlines to offset the debt which accrued when jet fuel prices spiked from N900 per litre to N3, 500 during the US-Iran war.

The unions also said the second reason why they picketed the airlines was because they refused to allow their workers join the unions.

But the unions only disrupted Air Peace operations, beat up and injured the airlines workers for refusing to join the unions. They did not give any explanation why they only targeted Air Peace operation because besides Aero Contractors and Arik Air, other domestic airlines workers are not members of any of the unions.

However, United Nigeria Airlines has suspended its operation in protest against the disruption of Air Peace flights. The airline directed its workers to suspend flight operations.

Air Peace in a statement said, “We wish to inform our esteemed passengers and the general flying public of temporary disruptions to our flight operations arising from the picketing of our airline and the ongoing industrial action by members of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), the Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria (ATSSSAN), and the Trade Union Congress (TUC).

“The ongoing industrial action has resulted in the barricading of the entrances to our departure terminals at Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 1 (Alpha and Zulu Terminals) and Terminal 2 in Lagos, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport Terminal in Abuja.”

The airline further explained that the blockade has restricted access to these terminals, preventing the departure of scheduled flights from Lagos and Abuja. Consequently, passengers scheduled to travel across our network have been significantly affected by the disruption to flight operations.

“Air Peace sincerely apologises to all affected and stranded passengers for the disruption and inconvenience caused by circumstances beyond the airline’s control. Passengers scheduled to travel later today are being contacted and provided with relevant updates as the situation evolves,” the airlines said.

The Director General of NCAA, Captain Chris Najomo, said in a statement that the agency was aware of the ongoing industrial action by aviation unions and its impact on passengers and other stakeholders.

“The NCAA appeals to the unions to sheathe their swords and exercise restraint pending the return of the Honourable Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, who has been actively working towards resolving the issues. The matter would have been addressed at the meeting convened by the Honourable Minister last week, but the meeting could not hold as the airline operators failed to honour the invitation,” he said.

But the Airlines Operators of Nigeria in a statement said that they did not have issues with labour; that NCAA had directed them on what to do and both the airlines and the agency agreed on payment schedule for the debt that accumulated during the US-Iran crisis and they have been complying with the payment so, the unions have no role to play in the arrangement.

However, the unions picketing Air Peace operations beat up the airlines workers when they said they do not want to become members of the unions, but even some members of the unions admitted to THISDAY that it is not compulsory for workers to join any union.

In fact, Under Nigerian labour law, trade union membership is entirely voluntary for all workers, including those in the aviation sector. No employee can be forced to join a union or be punished for refusing to join one.

World.title: ‘Nigeria Loses 600,000 People Annually over Administration of Medical Oxygen’
World.content:
Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki

The Vice Chancellor of David Umahi Federal University of Health Sciences (DUFUS), Ebonyi State, Professor Jesse Uneke, has said that Nigeria is losing over 600,000 people yearly due to issues relating to the administration of medical oxygen.

Uneke, who is the Nigerian and State Lead/Principal Investigator for the EQUI-RESP Africa Research Project, disclosed this in Abakaliki, the Ebonyi State capital, during the First Stakeholders’ Engagement Event/Co-Creation Workshop on Medical Oxygen Economy organised by the university in conjunction with the University of Edinburgh, UK, supported by the National Institute for Health and Research (NIHR), UK.

He explained that the administration of medical oxygen issues was happening because there was no platform where stakeholders in the medical oxygen space could come together to discuss the research-policy interface and see how to contextualise some of the strategies against the problems for the country.

“That is why, in this phase of this project, we have decided to start with this kind of stakeholders’ engagement. I am excited that we have every key stakeholder in the medical oxygen space represented here,” Uneke said.

He opined that the project started its first phase by carrying out intervention work in three industrial areas of the state: quarry industrial site in Onueke, rice mill in Abakaliki, and timber market.

According to him, “This project has to do with respiratory health, and the idea is to come up with strategies that will lead to interventions that will improve health outcomes as far as respiratory health is concerned.

“We carried out intervention research in these three areas, where the project was able to treat between 300 and 400 people free of charge.

“We provided them with inhalers, carried out other free diagnoses and guided them on how to stay healthy regarding their respiratory health.

“We are very grateful to the founders of this project for selecting Nigeria as one of the five countries in Africa where the EQUI RESP project is being implemented.

“The project is significantly placed within the global health space because, if anything is going to happen in terms of research aimed at identifying strategies that will enhance health outcomes in Africa, Nigeria cannot be excluded.

“We are fortunate that Nigeria was not just selected as one of the five African countries. We also have Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, South Africa, Cameroon, and, of course, Nigeria. We have two centres in Nigeria, one in Ebonyi State and one in Lagos State.

“Because the project also has to do with health policy and health systems, particularly moving evidence into policy, I was brought into the project and asked to lead the Ebonyi State research. So, we are very grateful that this project came to Nigeria and, specifically, to Ebonyi State.”

He added that: “Ebonyi State was selected because of the very excellent work that the current administration under Governor Francis Nwifuru is doing.

“Ebonyi is one of the states where partners can easily come and carry out projects in collaboration with not only the state government, but also institutions like our university and other institutions within the state, including the two teaching hospitals. There is also an enabling environment and the excellent work being done by the state Commissioner for Health.

“We are now getting into the second phase. We have moved from the community-based project to the hospital-based phase. In this hospital-based phase, we are focusing on medical oxygen and the medical oxygen economy.

“From what we have seen, this is one of the areas that is not well emphasised as far as the health sector is concerned. Nigeria is said to be losing over 600,000 people yearly due to issues related to the administration of medical oxygen. The problem is that these deaths are very preventable.”

In his remarks, the Chief Medical Director, Alex Ekwueme Federal University Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (AE-FUTHA), Professor Robinson Onoh, described the EQUI-RESP Africa Research project as multi-country research involving Nigeria and other countries and also a multi-centre research involving different centres.

He commended Governor Francis Nwifuru for creating the enabling environment for oxygen production centres in the state, which were not in existence before he came on board.

He said: “I want to commend the governor of Ebonyi State because before he came in as governor, there was no place where oxygen was produced in Ebonyi State. But by the time he came up and created an enabling environment, we now have areas in Ebonyi State where oxygen is being produced.

“And today, we can boast of multiple centres in Ebonyi State where medical oxygen is being produced. The importance of medical oxygen was noticed during the era of COVID. That was when it became obvious that we have an issue with that in Nigeria.

“Because it was discovered that for COVID patients to survive, you need oxygen. And when you now have multiple persons needing oxygen, we now discovered that there was a problem. And that’s why oxygen is being produced in a lot of places.

“And I want to inform you that one of the oxygen production centres in Ebonyi State is located in AE-FUTHA. So, I commend the governor for that.”

World.title: CMFC Shows Bright Prospects Three Months after Transformation
World.content:
Three months after shareholders approved the change from Deap Capital

Management & Trust Plc to Critical Minerals Financing Corp Plc (CMFC), the company has started showing very bright prospects going by its latest financial results for nine months ended June 30, 2026.

The company was restructured following the entry of Banklink Africa Private

Equities Limited as a core investor, making CMFC as a specialised financing and investment Banking institution focused on developing Africa’s critical minerals, metals, and commodities sectors.

Unaudited interim financial statements of the company for the nine month ended

June 30, 2026 submitted to the NGX on August5, showed that CMFC has started to earn income and closing period with a robust cash position.

Specifically, unlike the nine months ended June 2025 when the company recorded zero income, it ended nine months in 2026 with an income of N82.641 million. A further analysis of the earnings showed that 90 per cent was recorded between

March and June 2026. Also, the company closed the period with a robust cash position of over N6 billion, a situation market analysts said gives the company opportunity for business funding to earn more income in the coming months.

Besides, the company has paid off the AMCON negotiated debt of N430 million for which they were originally claiming N2.5 billion. Also, AMCON, which used to be the largest shareholder with 16 per cent of the paid-up capital, is no longer a shareholder in the company, freeing the company from issues related to its painful past years.

Banlink Africa Private Equities Limited is now the majority shareholder and has

committed a total of N6 billion to accelerate the corporate transition of CMFC. Investors in the Nigeria Exchange Limited ( NGX) have embraced these developments in CMFC with a lot of optimism. Since August 2025 when the company and Banklink Africa Private Equities Limited started their discussions about Banklink’s strategic investment in the company to August 7, 2026 more than 1.44 billion shares of the company have been traded out of the total issued and fully paid up share capital of 1,500,660,000. This shows a turnover of 97 per cent compared to 946 million shares of the company traded between May 2023 when the company restarted operation after 10 years of inactivity and July 31, 2025. The stock has also become very liquid since the new investors showed interest in the company with daily deals being in excess of 190 transactions compared to less than 40 deals in the period from May 2023 to July 31, 2025 before Banklink Africa Private Equities Limited invested in the company. At the same time the price has moved from N1.35 per shares in the first week of August 2025 to N11.43 on January 31, 2026 before it came down from February 2026 to the present level of N3.01 on August 5, 2026 when the nine months result for 2026 was released to the market.

The result has given a complete picture of the turnaround and transformation of the company from negative shareholders fund of N2.3 billion as at September 30 , 2025 to a positive shareholders funds of N4.3 billion as at June 30, 2026, a positive movement of 272 per cent. This improvement in the asset base of the company has led to the net asset per share improving from negative 155 kobo as at September 30, 2025 to positive 167 kobo as at June 2026, a favourable change of 208 per cent.

In the same period the company has successfully converted legacy debts of N1.8 billion out of N2.52 billion into 1,068, 980,259 Ordinary shares of 50k each , thereby increasing the paid-up capital to 2,569, 640,259 ordinary shares of 50k each after receiving the approval of the Securities and Exchange Commission ( SEC) to that effect.

The Chairman, CMFC Plc, Mr Lamon Rutten, who was appointed in March 2026, has said the transition reflected company’s sharpened focus on capital structuring, investment banking, transaction advisory, project development support, and financing solutions for stakeholders across the minerals and commodities sector.

According to him, the completion of the transition to CMFC marks the beginning of an exciting new phase for the company.

Rutten, a founding Chief Executive Officer of Saudi Mining Exchange and Mumbai Commodity Exchange (MCX), said: “We are strategically positioned to deliver world- class capital structuring, advisory, and financing solutions to mining and metals companies operating across gold, copper, cobalt, lithium, tungsten, tin, tantalum, and other critical mineral sectors.”

He explained that CMFC’s strategy is focused on addressing the significant financing and transaction-structuring gap within Africa’s mining industry by combining global financial expertise, sector-specific knowledge, and strategic partnerships.

Market analysts have said with the new board members and management of CMFC, shareholders are in for an exciting time going forward. For instance, the chairman, Rutten, is a globally respected expert in commodity markets, structured commodity finance, and exchange development with over 30 years of international experience across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

Founding CEO of the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), which he led to become the world's second-largest commodity exchange after CME, achieving a public listing valued at approximately US $1.5 billion. Previously Founding CEO of the Indonesia Commodity & Derivatives Exchange (ICDX) and a key architect of the Saudi Mining Exchange initiative.

Earlier Rutten led international commodity risk management and trade finance programmes at the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). Has advised governments, multilateral institutions, and financial organisations on commodity market development.

On the other hand, the President & Co-Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Israel Ovirih, is a development economist and veteran structured-finance expert with over 30 years of experience in Nigerian and international capital markets. Founder and Chairman of Banklink Africa Private Equities Group with a formidable track record in capital syndication, project finance, and institutional advisory. He has arranged and advised on financing programmes exceeding US $1.5 billion across energy, marine, and oil & gas sectors. Previously held senior strategic roles at Guaranty Trust Bank, Oceanic Bank, and ETBank (now Sterling Bank), and currently sits on multiple corporate boards across Africa driving economic transformation initiatives.

World.title: Forgotten Springbok to get a shot against All Blacks
World.content:
Widely regarded as a generational talent during his schoolboy days, Curwin Bosch – who has just two Springbok caps to his name – is no longer the young kid on the block.

A full decade has passed since he hade his Test debut just a couple of months after his 19th birthday, which came as a substitute against Argentina on 19 August 2017.

He would again feature for the Springboks when he started at fullback in the one off Test against Wales in Washington in 2018, but from there his national career never really took off as expected.



The 29-year-old has now returned to the Bulls, more experienced and certainly still with several years of rugby ahead of him, and now he also faces the unique prospect of featuring against the All Blacks in their third tour match of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry this Saturday.

Bosch told SARugbymag.co.za that it was “amazing to be back in South Africa” after two seasons in France with Brive.

“The two seasons I spent in France were really good for me, but there’s just no place like home. Even Pretoria, for me, feels like home.”

New chapter for former Springbok

Before heading to France, Bosch had become a mainstay at the Sharks – racking up over 100 caps for the Durban side in all competitions – but he admits he needed a change.

“I started becoming too comfortable at the Sharks. It was a safe space for me. I knew everyone, I knew the whole of Durban. Sometimes it is hard to leave that comfort, but it was exactly what I needed.

“The last couple of seasons in South Africa, I felt boxed in a little bit. That time in France freed me up, going back to almost how you used to play rugby at school. You see the space, and you play the space. That’s when I’m at my best.”



Opportunity in store

It shouldn’t be forgotten that the utility back – who is equally comfortable at flyhalf or fullback – is still only reaching an age where he has both experience and maturity on his side.

As the Bulls prepare to face the All Blacks this Saturday, it now remains to be seen whether Bosch can provide a reminder of his enduring class, especially for those who may have forgotten about him when he was somewhat ‘out of sight and out of mind’ in France.

World.title: Uber kills off UberX service in South Africa
World.content:
Uber will discontinue its UberX service in South Africa from 1 September 2026, as the ride-hailing company restructures its product offering in the country. Image: Flickr

Uber is set to discontinue its long-standing UberX service in South Africa from 1 September 2026, as the ride-hailing company restructures its product offering in the country.

The service, which was first introduced in Cape Town in June 2014 before expanding to Johannesburg, has for more than a decade served as Uber’s core budget-friendly ride option.

Simplify its offering

Uber has notified customers that UberX will be retired as part of a move to simplify its South African offering into four categories: Uber Go, Uber Comfort, Uber Black and Uber Reserve.



Uber Go will serve as the entry-level option, while Comfort and Black will cater to passengers looking for higher levels of vehicle quality and service. Reserve will remain available for customers wanting to arrange rides in advance.

Tier Offers Uber Go A smaller, lower-priced car built for quick trips around town Uber Comfort Newer vehicles with extra space and the option to request a quiet ride Uber Black Premium vehicles and top-tier drivers, with longer wait times Uber Reserve Rides booked up to 90 days in advance with guaranteed pricing and pickup times

Growing concerns

The change comes amid growing concerns across the local e-hailing industry about vehicle standards, driver reliability and intense competition in the lower-cost segment.

Budget e-hailing services have faced mounting pressure to keep fares competitive, with the resulting price competition contributing to concerns about the quality and reliability of some services.



Uber’s restructuring is expected to give passengers a clearer choice between different levels of service while moving away from a single dominant budget product.

Tighten regulation

The changes also come as South Africa moves to tighten regulation of the e-hailing industry.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has signed the National Land Transport Amendment Act (NLTAA) into law, introducing new requirements aimed at formalising the sector and improving passenger and driver safety.



Among the provisions are requirements relating to driver vetting, operating licences, company registration and emergency panic buttons in vehicles.

Transport Minister Barbara Creecy has said the legislation will provide greater recognition for e-hailing drivers within the country’s public transport system.

“It benefits South African drivers by recognising them as formal public transport operators or drivers, legalising their status,” Creecy said.



“Legitimising the profession means the subsector can benefit from basic conditions of employment and comply with labour and employment laws.”

Years of tension

The regulatory changes follow years of tension and uncertainty surrounding the position of e-hailing services within South Africa’s broader public transport system.

For Uber passengers, the most immediate change will be the disappearance of UberX from the app from 1 September, with Uber Go becoming the company’s entry-level alternative.

World.title: Why your fuel light may come on faster in this week’s cold snap
World.content:
This week's cold snap is affecting more than just the roads, it is also costing drivers more at the pump: Image ChatGPT

With an orange level warning for disruptive snow still in effect over parts of the Eastern Cape, and cold, wet conditions gripping much of the country this week, most of the attention has gone to icy roads and falling temperatures.

What gets less attention is what this cold snap is doing to your fuel bill.

Cold weather can reduce fuel efficiency by 12% to 20% or more, and the effect is worse on short trips.



According to the US Department of Energy’s fuel economy research, a petrol engine can lose as much as a third of its efficiency on trips of three to four kilometres when temperatures drop, compared to a mild day.

Why cold weather burns more petrol

A cold engine has to work harder before it reaches its most efficient operating temperature, and that warm-up period uses more fuel than normal driving.

Engine oil and other fluids also thicken in the cold, adding friction the engine has to overcome.



Denser cold air increases resistance against the vehicle, and tyre pressure naturally drops as temperatures fall, which increases rolling resistance and forces the engine to work harder to maintain speed.

Short trips take the biggest hit, since the car spends most of the journey at a less efficient temperature before the engine ever properly warms up.

Idling to warm up the car before driving does not help either, since a vehicle uses fuel while getting zero kilometres per litre while sitting still.



What this looks like in rand terms

At the current inland price of R25.58 per litre for 95 unleaded petrol, filling a 45-litre tank costs around R1 151.

If cold weather cuts your efficiency by 15%, a fairly typical figure for winter short trips, you would need roughly 6.75 litres more fuel to cover the same distance you’d normally get from that tank, an extra R173.

Diesel users feel it too.

At R26.17 a litre (wholesale), that same 45-litre tank works out to about R1 178.



A 15% efficiency drop adds close to R177 in extra fuel to travel the same distance.

For bakkie owners and anyone doing daily long-distance commutes, that adds up fast over a cold month.

What you can do about it this week

A few small habits can soften the impact while this cold front sits over the country.



Combining short errands into one trip means the engine only has to warm up once instead of several times.

Checking tyre pressure regularly matters more in cold weather, since pressure drops as the temperature does.

Avoiding long idling periods to warm up the car, and rather driving off gently instead, also helps the engine reach an efficient temperature faster.



None of this will stop winter driving from costing more at the pump, but it does explain why my own tank has been emptying faster this week than it did back in summer.
